XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prynhawn da, Aelodau. Heddiw, rydym yn nodi 60 mlynedd ers trychineb Aberfan, pan gollodd 116 o blant a 28 o oedolion eu bywydau ar 21 Hydref 1966. Cyn i ni ddechrau busnes y prynhawn yma, gwahoddaf yr Aelodau i nodi munud o dawelwch i gofio am Aberfan.

Today, we mark the sixtieth anniversary of the Aberfan disaster, in which 116 children and 28 adults lost their lives on 21 October 1966. Before we begin this afternoon's business, I invite Members to observe a minute's silence in remembrance of Aberfan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Rydw i wedi trafod Twf Swyddi Cymru+ gyda'r Dirprwy Weinidog, gan gynnwys y pwysau y mae darparwyr yn ei reoli wrth iddyn nhw ymateb i'r galw parhaus am gymorth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I have discussed Jobs Growth Wales+ with the Deputy Minister, including the pressures that some providers are managing as they respond to continued demand for support.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Cabinet Minister. As you are aware, we are facing a 'not in education, employment or training' crisis in Wales, with everything that that means for young people's life chances, their employment and, of particular concern to me, their mental health and well-being. However, we're not now just facing the prospect of cuts in further education funding, but, as I've highlighted to you in correspondence, providers of services to young people through Jobs Growth Wales+, which is effectively a post-16 provision, are also seeing significant cuts. I'm grateful to you for your correspondence, but I have written back to you explaining that ACT, which has been praised across this Chamber for their transformative work with young people, has currently gone from a confirmed contract value of £18.8 million last year to £13.9 million in 2026-27.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Fel y gwyddoch, rydym yn wynebu argyfwng o ran pobl nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant yng Nghymru, gyda phopeth y mae hynny'n ei olygu i gyfleoedd bywyd pobl ifanc, eu cyflogaeth, a rhywbeth sy'n destun pryder arbennig i mi, sef eu hiechyd meddwl a'u lles. Fodd bynnag, nid yn unig ein bod yn wynebu'r posibilrwydd nawr o doriadau i gyllid addysg bellach, ond fel y nodais mewn gohebiaeth, mae darparwyr gwasanaethau i bobl ifanc drwy Twf Swyddi Cymru+, sydd i bob pwrpas yn ddarpariaeth ôl-16, hefyd yn wynebu toriadau sylweddol. Rwy'n ddiolchgar i chi am eich gohebiaeth, ond rwyf wedi ysgrifennu'n ôl atoch yn egluro bod gwerth contract ACT, sydd wedi cael eu canmol ar draws y Siambr hon am eu gwaith trawsnewidiol gyda phobl ifanc, wedi mynd o £18.8 miliwn wedi'i gadarnhau y llynedd i £13.9 miliwn yn 2026-27.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Can we have the question, please, Lynne?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A gawn ni'r cwestiwn, os gwelwch yn dda, Lynne?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: That is a 26 per cent cut. On the basis of these figures, can we accept that the Plaid Cymru Government is committed to tackling the NEET crisis, and, if that is the case, what are you going to do to reverse these cuts and ensure that all learners have an opportunity to have their education?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae hynny'n doriad o 26 y cant. Ar sail y ffigurau hyn, a allwn dderbyn bod Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru wedi ymrwymo i fynd i'r afael â'r argyfwng o ran pobl nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant, ac os felly, beth rydych chi'n mynd i'w wneud i wrthdroi'r toriadau hyn a sicrhau bod cyfle gan bob dysgwr i gael eu haddysg?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I am grateful to the Member for her question, and, as I said just now, I have, obviously, had discussions already with Cabinet colleagues to see what more can be done within the resources that we have. I think it is certainly the case that we are seeing not just in Wales, but across the UK, a huge issue in terms of the labour market. It has, obviously, led to the Milburn review, and I agree, actually, with Alan Milburn that working on the supply side, working on employability support programmes, is not going to be enough to deal with the scale of the problem, because the problem is really on the demand side largely. That's where we also need to focus, and I think that, really, the scale of the problem means that we do need a scale of intervention on a similar level to the one that we saw back in 1997—the New Deal for the unemployed. So, we are looking forward to the final report of the Milburn review. We hope that the UK Government will inject the level of investment that is needed not just in Wales, but across the UK, to address the problem that young people and others are facing because of the nature of the labour market need at the moment.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n ddiolchgar i'r Aelod am ei chwestiwn, ac fel y dywedais nawr, yn amlwg, cefais drafodaethau eisoes gyda chyd-Aelodau o'r Cabinet i weld beth arall y gellir ei wneud o fewn yr adnoddau sydd gennym. Credaf ei bod yn sicr yn wir ein bod yn gweld problem enfawr o ran y farchnad lafur, nid yn unig yng Nghymru, ond ledled y DU. Mae wedi arwain at adolygiad Milburn, ac rwy'n cytuno ag Alan Milburn na fydd gweithio ar ochr y cyflenwad, gweithio ar raglenni cymorth cyflogadwyedd, yn ddigon i fynd i'r afael â maint y broblem, gan fod y broblem mewn gwirionedd ar ochr y galw i raddau helaeth. Dyna ble mae angen inni ganolbwyntio hefyd, ac mae maint y broblem yn golygu bod angen ymyrraeth arnom ar lefel debyg i'r hyn a welsom yn ôl ym 1997—y Fargen Newydd ar gyfer y di-waith. Felly, rydym yn edrych ymlaen at adroddiad terfynol adolygiad Milburn. Gobeithiwn y bydd Llywodraeth y DU yn buddsoddi’r lefel sydd ei hangen nid yn unig yng Nghymru ond ledled y DU, i fynd i’r afael â’r broblem y mae pobl ifanc ac eraill yn ei hwynebu oherwydd natur anghenion y farchnad lafur ar hyn o bryd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cabinet Minister, I welcome your commitment to extend Jobs Growth Wales+ to consider the incentives for employers, because young people leaving the programme need apprenticeships and jobs to move into. I recently met with Williams Electrical (Cymru) Ltd, a Carmarthenshire firm that wants to take on more apprentices but says it can no longer afford to. Under the reformed qualifications, a first-year electrical apprentice without the relevant foundation qualification must undertake broader construction training and skills. The concern for the firm is that the additional college day in the first year leaves just three weeks on site whilst they're having to pay a full week's wages for that apprentice. Carmarthenshire's over-65 population has grown by almost a fifth, while apprenticeship starts across Wales are at their lowest since records began. Yet electrical contractors are generally excluded from the Construction Industry Training Board apprenticeship grants available to other construction employers. So, will you discuss with the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education how those incentives could include targeted support for smaller electrical firms to cover that additional college day so that businesses like Williams can train the electricians that Wales desperately needs? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog Cabinet, rwy'n croesawu eich ymrwymiad i ymestyn Twf Swyddi Cymru+ i ystyried y cymelliadau i gyflogwyr, gan fod angen prentisiaethau a swyddi ar bobl ifanc sy'n gadael y rhaglen i gamu ymlaen iddynt. Yn ddiweddar, cyfarfûm â Williams Electrical (Cymru) Ltd, cwmni o sir Gaerfyrddin sydd eisiau cyflogi mwy o brentisiaid ond sy'n dweud na allant fforddio gwneud hynny mwyach. O dan y cymwysterau diwygiedig, rhaid i brentis trydanol blwyddyn gyntaf heb y cymhwyster sylfaen perthnasol ymgymryd â hyfforddiant a sgiliau adeiladu ehangach. Y pryder i'r cwmni yw bod y diwrnod coleg ychwanegol yn y flwyddyn gyntaf yn gadael tair wythnos yn unig ar y safle a'u bod yn gorfod talu cyflog wythnos lawn am y prentis hwnnw. Mae poblogaeth dros 65 oed sir Gaerfyrddin wedi tyfu bron i bumed, tra bo nifer y prentisiaethau a ddechreuwyd ledled Cymru ar eu lefel isaf ers dechrau cadw cofnodion. Ac eto, mae contractwyr trydanol yn gyffredinol wedi'u heithrio o grantiau prentisiaeth Bwrdd Hyfforddi'r Diwydiant Adeiladu sydd ar gael i gyflogwyr adeiladu eraill. Felly, a wnewch chi drafod gyda'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol sut y gallai'r cymelliadau hynny gynnwys cymorth wedi'i dargedu ar gyfer cwmnïau trydanol llai i dalu am y diwrnod coleg ychwanegol hwnnw fel y gall busnesau fel Williams hyfforddi'r trydanwyr y mae eu hangen yn daer ar Gymru? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Deputy Minister has been very clear in his view that apprenticeships are absolutely central to enabling young people to achieve their potential and also for us to drive the kind of economic development that we want to see across every sector and across every community. We'll certainly very much welcome those ideas and take them up in discussion with the Deputy Minister in the context of the work that is already ongoing through the skills audit and following the skills summit a few weeks ago.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog wedi dweud yn glir iawn ei fod o'r farn fod prentisiaethau'n hollbwysig i alluogi pobl ifanc i gyflawni eu potensial a hefyd i ni i hybu'r math o ddatblygu economaidd rydym am ei weld ar draws pob sector ac ar draws pob cymuned. Byddwn yn sicr yn croesawu'r syniadau hynny'n fawr ac yn eu trafod gyda'r Dirprwy Weinidog yng nghyd-destun y gwaith sydd eisoes yn mynd rhagddo drwy'r archwiliad sgiliau ac yn dilyn yr uwchgynhadledd sgiliau ychydig wythnosau yn ôl.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cabinet Minister, I heard your response to Lynne Neagle a moment ago, rightfully outlining the challenge around NEETs, but you need to acknowledge that there's a particular problem here in Wales. In England, the numbers have actually dropped in the last 12 months to 13.3 per cent, whereas, in Wales, numbers have shot up to 17 per cent of 16 to 25-year-olds not in work, training or education. It's vitally important that we get those young people into those positions as quickly as possible. As you know, Jobs Growth Wales+ makes a big difference in that, and you do have already the policy levers to be able to make a difference in this area, and it's about prioritising whether or not you think it's an important matter for you to tackle. I think in particular, in my own constituency of Fflint Wrecsam, that Coleg Cambria run a fantastic summer school with Jobs Growth Wales+, where 100 young people took part in that summer school—a record number so far. So, Cabinet Minister, will you commit today, for the sake of the 16 to 25-year-olds, to ensuring that this is a priority and that you do use the policy levers you already have to ensure that young people have a fighting chance?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog Cabinet, clywais eich ymateb i Lynne Neagle eiliad yn ôl, yn amlinellu'r her yn gywir ddigon o ran pobl nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant, ond mae angen ichi gydnabod bod problem arbennig yma yng Nghymru. Yn Lloegr, mae'r niferoedd wedi gostwng yn y 12 mis diwethaf i 13.3 y cant, tra bo'r niferoedd yng Nghymru wedi saethu i fyny i 17 y cant o bobl 16 i 25 oed nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant. Mae'n hanfodol bwysig ein bod yn sicrhau bod y bobl ifanc hyn yn cael y swyddi hynny cyn gynted â phosibl. Fel y gwyddoch, mae Twf Swyddi Cymru+ yn gwneud gwahaniaeth mawr yn hynny o beth, ac mae gennych eisoes y liferi polisi i allu gwneud gwahaniaeth yn y maes hwn, ac mae a wnelo â blaenoriaethu p'un a ydych chi'n credu ei fod yn fater pwysig i chi fynd i'r afael ag ef ai peidio. Yn fy etholaeth i yn Fflint Wrecsam, rwy'n meddwl yn arbennig am Coleg Cambria sy'n cynnal ysgol haf wych gyda Twf Swyddi Cymru+, a chymerodd 100 o bobl ifanc ran yn yr ysgol haf honno—y nifer uchaf erioed hyd yma. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, a wnewch chi ymrwymo heddiw, er mwyn pobl 16 i 25 oed, i sicrhau bod hyn yn flaenoriaeth a'ch bod yn defnyddio'r liferi polisi sydd gennych eisoes i sicrhau bod rhywfaint o obaith i bobl ifanc?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Where I agree with the Member is that the existing interventions in Wales were not working, and the actual outcomes were worse. As a result of that, we have commissioned, as a Government, work by Professor Melanie Jones, one of the leading figures in labour market economics, to understand, 'Well, let's look across the world at what does work in order to inform our own use of the policy levers that we do have.' But I should say that the consensus view, which is emerging through the work of the Milburn review and economists that are looking at this, is that the supply-side approach, which is basically saying, 'There's an unemployed person here and if we can make them employable, then they can get into the labour market', the increasing consensus view is that that's incorrect, largely. The problem is on the demand side. The jobs are not being generated to a sufficient degree to actually create those job opportunities, and there are particular structural problems in terms of entry-level jobs. That's why I think sector-led approaches, the likes of which we've begun to see, haven't we, in recent weeks and months—the retail sector, the construction sector, coming forward and making commitments to create those entry-level jobs—those kind of approaches are likely to have a better effect. The opportunity for us in Wales is to work with sectors—and we've just heard some specific examples in an earlier question as well—to provide those entry-level jobs, and, yes, make sure that our training skills system is working with employers for real job opportunities that are going to be created.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yr hyn rwy'n cytuno â'r Aelod yn ei gylch yw nad oedd yr ymyriadau presennol yng Nghymru yn gweithio, ac roedd y canlyniadau eu hunain yn waeth. O ganlyniad i hynny, fel Llywodraeth, rydym wedi comisiynu gwaith gan yr Athro Melanie Jones, un o'r ffigurau blaenllaw ym maes economeg y farchnad lafur, i ddeall, 'Wel, gadewch inni edrych ar draws y byd ar yr hyn sy'n gweithio er mwyn llywio ein defnydd ein hunain o'r liferi polisi sydd gennym.' Ond dylwn ddweud mai'r consensws, sy'n dod i'r amlwg drwy waith adolygiad Milburn ac economegwyr sy'n edrych ar hyn, yw bod dull gweithredu ochr y cyflenwad, sydd yn y bôn yn dweud, 'Mae unigolyn di-waith yma ac os gallwn eu gwneud yn gyflogadwy, gallant fynd i mewn i'r farchnad lafur', y consensws cynyddol yw bod hynny'n anghywir at ei gilydd. Mae'r broblem ar ochr y galw. Nid yw'r swyddi'n cael eu creu i raddau digonol i greu'r cyfleoedd swyddi hynny, ac mae problemau strwythurol penodol o ran swyddi lefel mynediad. Dyna pam y credaf fod dulliau a arweinir gan sectorau, fel y rhai rydym wedi dechrau eu gweld, onid ydym, yn yr wythnosau a'r misoedd diwethaf—y sector manwerthu, y sector adeiladu, yn camu i'r bwlch ac yn gwneud ymrwymiadau i greu'r swyddi lefel mynediad hynny—mae'r mathau hynny o ddulliau gweithredu'n debygol o gael gwell effaith. Y cyfle i ni yng Nghymru yw gweithio gyda sectorau—ac rydym newydd glywed rhai enghreifftiau penodol mewn cwestiwn cynharach hefyd—i ddarparu'r swyddi lefel mynediad hynny, ac ie, sicrhau bod ein system hyfforddiant sgiliau yn gweithio gyda chyflogwyr ar gyfleoedd swyddi go iawn a fydd yn cael eu creu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog a minnau'n trafod yn rheolaidd sut y gall sgiliau, cymorth cyflogadwyedd a phrentisiaethau arfogi pobl ifanc ledled Cymru i lwyddo mewn economi sy'n newid yn gyflym. Roedd y materion hyn yn nodwedd o'n huwchgynhadledd sgiliau'r dyfodol hynod lwyddiannus yn gynharach y mis hwn ac maen nhw’n ganolog i'm cenhadaeth cynhyrchiant.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Deputy Minister and I regularly discuss how skills, employability support and apprenticeships can equip young people across Wales to succeed in a rapidly changing economy. These issues were a feature of our highly successful future skills summit earlier this month and are central to my productivity mission.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Cabinet Minister. In Blaenau Gwent, nearly three in 10 residents aged 16 and over have no formal qualifications, which is the highest proportion in the whole of Wales, while neighbouring Caerphilly has the fourth highest. I've seen first-hand the vital role that organisations such as ACT has in Ebbw Vale. They play such an important role in supporting young people facing really complex needs and barriers to education, training and employment. For many of these young people, progress can mean overcoming mental health challenges, gaining qualifications after leaving school without any, finding secure housing or even turning away from crime as well. They need to have a system that can respond to the full range of barriers they face as an individual and gives them the best opportunity as well to fulfil their potential. So, Cabinet Minister, how will the Welsh Government ensure we have a fit-for-purpose system, with the flexibility and stability needed to support young people to fulfil their potential, particularly those facing extreme barriers?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Ym Mlaenau Gwent, nid oes gan bron i dri o bob 10 o drigolion 16 oed a hŷn unrhyw gymwysterau ffurfiol, sef y gyfran uchaf yng Nghymru gyfan, tra bo ganddynt y bedwaredd gyfradd uchaf drws nesaf yng Nghaerffili. Rwyf wedi gweld â'm llygaid fy hun y rôl hanfodol y mae sefydliadau fel ACT yng Nglynebwy yn ei chwarae. Maent yn chwarae rhan mor bwysig yn cefnogi pobl ifanc sy'n wynebu anghenion cymhleth iawn a rhwystrau i addysg, hyfforddiant a chyflogaeth. I lawer o'r bobl ifanc hyn, gall cynnydd olygu goresgyn heriau iechyd meddwl, ennill cymwysterau ar ôl gadael ysgol heb unrhyw gymwysterau, dod o hyd i dai diogel neu hyd yn oed droi cefn ar droseddu hefyd. Mae angen iddynt gael system a all ymateb i'r ystod lawn o rwystrau y maent yn eu hwynebu fel unigolyn a rhoi'r cyfle gorau iddynt gyflawni eu potensial. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, sut y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn sicrhau bod gennym system sy'n addas i’r diben, ac sydd â'r hyblygrwydd a'r sefydlogrwydd sydd eu hangen i gefnogi pobl ifanc i gyflawni eu potensial, yn enwedig y rhai sy'n wynebu rhwystrau eithafol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I am grateful to the Member for her question. I think that, certainly, we acknowledge the importance of programmes like Jobs Growth Wales. We've committed to continuing that next year, even, as I said, as we begin the work of understanding what more we can do and what we can do differently, because, even though these programmes have made a contribution, they have not solved the problem; the problem has got worse. And so, we need to find out what is missing, what additional can we do. As I was saying, I think the growing view among those who work in and analyse this field is that we need to work more on the demand side to generate the jobs, and also we need to have a place-based approach. So, I think you're absolutely right to focus on the specific needs, which will be different in Blaenau Gwent to other places. The opportunities will be different. The employers that we can work with to create particular sectoral opportunities will be different. So, it's that combination not just of the existing approaches, but blending them with new interventions that are demand led and placed based. That's the way, in a holistic fashion, I think that we can provide a durable and comprehensive solution that will deliver hope to young people and to communities across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n ddiolchgar i'r Aelod am ei chwestiwn. Yn sicr, rwy'n credu ein bod yn cydnabod pwysigrwydd rhaglenni fel Twf Swyddi Cymru. Rydym wedi ymrwymo i barhau â'r rhaglen honno y flwyddyn nesaf, hyd yn oed wrth inni ddechrau'r gwaith, fel y dywedais, o ddeall beth arall y gallwn ei wneud, a beth y gallwn ei wneud yn wahanol, oherwydd er bod y rhaglenni hyn wedi gwneud cyfraniad, nid ydynt wedi datrys y broblem; mae'r broblem wedi gwaethygu. Ac felly, mae angen inni ddarganfod beth sydd ar goll, beth arall y gallwn ei wneud. Fel roeddwn i'n ei ddweud, credaf mai'r farn gynyddol ymhlith y rhai sy'n gweithio yn y maes hwn ac yn ei ddadansoddi yw bod angen inni weithio mwy ar ochr y galw i greu'r swyddi, ac mae angen inni gael dull sy'n seiliedig ar leoedd hefyd. Felly, rwy'n credu eich bod yn llygad eich lle i ganolbwyntio ar yr anghenion penodol, a fydd yn wahanol ym Mlaenau Gwent i fannau eraill. Bydd y cyfleoedd yn wahanol. Bydd y cyflogwyr y gallwn weithio gyda nhw i greu cyfleoedd sectoraidd penodol yn wahanol. Felly, mae a wnelo â chyfuniad nid yn unig o'r dulliau presennol, ond eu cymysgu ag ymyriadau newydd sy'n cael eu harwain gan alw ac sy'n seiliedig ar leoedd. Credaf mai dyna sut y gallwn ddarparu, mewn modd cyfannol, ateb gwydn a chynhwysfawr a fydd yn rhoi gobaith i bobl ifanc ac i gymunedau ledled Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, traditionally, entry-level roles have allowed young people to gain the experience needed to progress into more skilled employment. But artificial intelligence now threatens to automate some of those opportunities. What assessment, therefore, has the Welsh Government made of the impact of AI on entry-level employment opportunities for young people in Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni, and what discussions has the Cabinet Minister had with the Deputy Minister for skills about ensuring that training provision in our constituency prepares young people for the jobs likely to be available in five to 10 years' time?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, yn draddodiadol, mae rolau lefel mynediad wedi caniatáu i bobl ifanc ennill y profiad sydd ei angen arnynt i gamu ymlaen i gyflogaeth fwy medrus. Ond mae deallusrwydd artiffisial bellach yn bygwth awtomeiddio rhai o'r cyfleoedd hynny. Felly, pa asesiad y mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'i wneud o effaith deallusrwydd artiffisial ar gyfleoedd cyflogaeth lefel mynediad i bobl ifanc ym Mlaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni, a pha drafodaethau y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi'u cael gyda'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros sgiliau ynghylch sicrhau bod darpariaeth hyfforddiant yn ein hetholaeth yn paratoi pobl ifanc ar gyfer y swyddi sy'n debygol o fod ar gael ymhen pump i ddeng mlynedd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm really grateful to the Member for an absolutely vitally important question, which I think is at the forefront of all of our minds at the moment, isn't it? I think it's certainly true that AI is one of the factors that is driving this unique level of disruption that is going on in the labour market. I think that it is a complex picture, and it's fair to say that the evidence is still emerging. We were discussing this at the jobs summit, and we need to have a better understanding and better data. So, there is a live data set that actually looks at what is happening in the American labour market. Month by month, we can see what's happening, and we can see that, particularly, it's young people that are being disrupted most in terms of higher levels of unemployment. We can even be more specific: it's 22 to 25-year-olds who are facing a 20 per cent higher level of unemployment than was previously the case. Now, we need to get that kind of data here and we need to understand how this is playing out across different sectors and across different geographies. That work is ongoing, and I hope to be able to update Senedd Members more in this regard because I think it's one of the central challenges that we're facing at the moment.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n ddiolchgar iawn i'r Aelod am gwestiwn hollbwysig, sydd, yn fy marn i, ar ein meddyliau ni oll ar hyn o bryd, onid yw? Rwy'n credu ei bod yn sicr yn wir fod deallusrwydd artiffisial yn un o'r ffactorau sy'n achosi'r lefel unigryw hon o darfu ar y farchnad lafur. Rwy'n credu ei fod yn ddarlun cymhleth, ac mae'n deg dweud bod y dystiolaeth yn dal i ddod i'r amlwg. Buom yn trafod hyn yn yr uwchgynhadledd swyddi, ac mae angen inni gael gwell dealltwriaeth a data gwell. Felly, mae yna set ddata fyw sy'n edrych ar yr hyn sy'n digwydd ym marchnad lafur America. Fis ar ôl mis, gallwn weld beth sy'n digwydd, a gallwn weld mai pobl ifanc yn fwyaf arbennig sy'n cael eu heffeithio fwyaf o ran lefelau uwch o ddiweithdra. Gallwn fod hyd yn oed yn fwy penodol: mae pobl 22 i 25 oed yn wynebu lefel 20 y cant yn uwch o ddiweithdra nag o'r blaen. Nawr, mae angen inni gael y math hwnnw o ddata yma ac mae angen inni ddeall sut y mae hyn yn datblygu ar draws gwahanol sectorau ac ar draws daearyddiaeth wahanol. Mae'r gwaith hwnnw'n parhau, ac rwy'n gobeithio gallu rhoi mwy o wybodaeth i Aelodau'r Senedd yn hyn o beth gan y credaf ei bod yn un o'r heriau mwyaf a wynebwn ar hyn o bryd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiynau Heb Rybudd gan Lefarwyr y Pleidiau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Questions Without Notice from Party Spokespeople

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf ar lefarwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Gweinidog Cabinet. Llefarydd Reform UK, Jason O'Connell.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minister. Reform UK spokesperson, Jason O'Connell.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. Minister, as discussed recently in this Chamber, 500 jobs in Admiral are at risk of redundancy. These are real Welsh people, real Welsh families and actual livelihoods that are now facing uncertainty. Many of those jobs are based across our constituencies in Swansea, Cardiff and Newport. And now we learn that, while Welsh workers face the prospect of losing their jobs, some roles—the majority of those 500 jobs—are going to be outsourced to India. Now, this is a massive slap in the face to all those men and women that have worked hard, paid their taxes, only for their jobs to be sent abroad, and is a firm rebuke to this Government's economic credentials. This should be a massive wake-up call for this Welsh Government. So, Minister, what direct action are you taking to stop skilled Welsh jobs being shipped overseas, to protect workers here in Wales, and to ensure that companies benefiting from operating in this country have a genuine incentive to keep those jobs here? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Weinidog, fel y trafodwyd yn ddiweddar yn y Siambr hon, mae 500 o swyddi yn Admiral mewn perygl o gael eu dileu. Mae'r rhain yn Gymry go iawn, yn deuluoedd go iawn ac yn fywoliaeth go iawn i bobl sydd bellach yn wynebu ansicrwydd. Mae llawer o'r swyddi hyn wedi'u lleoli ar draws ein hetholaethau yn Abertawe, Caerdydd a Chasnewydd. A nawr, er bod gweithwyr yng Nghymru yn wynebu'r posibilrwydd o golli eu swyddi, clywn y bydd rhai rolau—y rhan fwyaf o'r 500 o swyddi hynny—yn cael eu hallanoli i India. Nawr, mae hon yn ergyd enfawr i'r holl ddynion a menywod sydd wedi gweithio'n galed, wedi talu eu trethi, dim ond i'w swyddi gael eu hanfon dramor, ac mae'n ergyd fawr i hygrededd economaidd y Llywodraeth hon. Dylai hyn fod yn rhybudd enfawr i'r Llywodraeth hon yng Nghymru. Felly, Weinidog, pa gamau uniongyrchol rydych chi'n eu cymryd i atal swyddi medrus o Gymru rhag cael eu hanfon dramor, i ddiogelu gweithwyr yma yng Nghymru, ac i sicrhau bod gan gwmnïau sy'n elwa o weithredu yn y wlad hon gymhelliant gwirioneddol i gadw'r swyddi hynny yma? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Clearly, this was very disappointing news to hear and, obviously, very worrying for the workers and their families involved. I've met with Admiral, and, indeed, with Legal & General as well, to see what we could do—first of all to understand what we could do in the context of those that are at risk of losing their jobs, and we obviously stand ready to do what we can in that regard, but also to understand more about the reasons for these decisions and what we could do, working with these companies and with their sectors, to create additional jobs as well.

Now, Admiral have, in that conversation, confirmed to us that they are going to retain their Cardiff and Swansea offices. In my conversation with Legal & General—and, indeed, with Admiral as well—we did talk about what are the growth opportunities, where we as a Government can work with the companies and with the sectors in order to identify growth possibilities, because we retain important strengths in these sectors, and it's important not to lose sight of that, despite this obviously disappointing news.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn amlwg, roedd hyn yn newyddion siomedig iawn, ac yn peri cryn bryder i'r gweithwyr a'u teuluoedd wrth gwrs. Rwyf wedi cyfarfod ag Admiral, a gyda Legal & General hefyd yn wir, i weld beth y gallem ei wneud—yn gyntaf oll i ddeall beth y gallem ei wneud yng nghyd-destun y rhai sydd mewn perygl o golli eu swyddi, ac rydym yn amlwg yn barod i wneud yr hyn a allwn yn hynny o beth, ond hefyd i ddeall mwy am y rhesymau dros y penderfyniadau hyn a'r hyn y gallem ei wneud, gan weithio gyda'r cwmnïau hyn a'u sectorau, i greu swyddi ychwanegol hefyd.

Nawr, mae Admiral, yn y sgwrs honno, wedi cadarnhau i ni eu bod yn mynd i gadw eu swyddfeydd yng Nghaerdydd ac Abertawe. Yn fy sgwrs gyda Legal & General—a gydag Admiral hefyd yn wir—buom yn siarad ynglŷn â beth yw'r cyfleoedd twf, lle gallwn ni fel Llywodraeth weithio gyda'r cwmnïau a chyda'r sectorau er mwyn nodi posibiliadau twf, gan fod gennym gryfderau pwysig yn y sectorau hyn o hyd, ac mae'n bwysig peidio â cholli golwg ar hynny, er gwaethaf y newyddion hwn sy'n amlwg yn siomedig.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. I thought I was going to get called—excuse me.

Minister, thank you for that, but, as we move on, unlike Plaid's new energy quango, North sea drilling could unlock billions for the UK economy, support thousands of jobs and strengthen our energy security. As Reform UK's Richard Tice has been calling for for years, the Jackdaw project has now been given the green light, and, as we know on this side of the Chamber, that's nowhere near enough. Now, Reform believes the United Kingdom should extract every last drop of oil out of the North sea—and gas—to support our economy, protect jobs and reduce our reliance on imports. Instead, Plaid wants to waste taxpayers' money on another quango and renewable energy schemes that offer absolutely no guarantee of cheaper bills to the men and women of our country. Minister, let's get real for a moment and focus on the action that will actually make a difference to people's pockets here in Wales. What steps are you taking to press Westminster to issue new exploration licences, unlock our North sea resources, boost our economy and bring down household bills for people across Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Roeddwn yn credu fy mod yn mynd i gael fy ngalw—esgusodwch fi.

Weinidog, diolch, ond wrth inni symud ymlaen, yn wahanol i gwango ynni newydd Plaid Cymru, gallai drilio ym môr y Gogledd ddatgloi biliynau i economi'r DU, cefnogi miloedd o swyddi a chryfhau ein diogeledd ynni. Fel y mae Richard Tice o Reform UK wedi bod yn galw amdano ers blynyddoedd, mae prosiect Jackdaw bellach wedi cael y golau gwyrdd, ac fel y gwyddom ar yr ochr hon i'r Siambr, nid yw hynny'n agos at ddigon. Nawr, mae Reform yn credu y dylai'r Deyrnas Unedig echdynnu pob diferyn o olew allan o fôr y Gogledd—a nwy—i gefnogi ein heconomi, diogelu swyddi a lleihau ein dibyniaeth ar fewnforion. Yn hytrach, mae Plaid Cymru eisiau gwastraffu arian trethdalwyr ar gwango arall a chynlluniau ynni adnewyddadwy nad ydynt yn cynnig unrhyw sicrwydd o gwbl o filiau rhatach i ddynion a menywod ein gwlad. Weinidog, gadewch inni fod yn realistig am eiliad a chanolbwyntio ar y camau a fydd o ddifrif yn gwneud gwahaniaeth i bocedi pobl yma yng Nghymru. Pa gamau rydych chi'n eu cymryd i bwyso ar San Steffan i gyhoeddi trwyddedau fforio newydd, datgloi ein hadnoddau ym môr y Gogledd, hybu ein heconomi a gostwng biliau aelwydydd pobl ledled Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Look, the real opportunity for us—. If you want to talk about energy off our shores, the real opportunity for us in Wales, it's in our floating offshore wind sector, it's in our tidal stream and tidal lagoon industries. That's where the real opportunity, in terms of jobs, is. So, let's focus there, because there are important messages where it would be useful if we could speak with one voice to urge the UK Government, for example, to realise the strategic value of marine energy, of floating offshore wind, of tidal. We have some unique geographic assets. No, they don't involve fossil fuels, but they are definitely sectors of the future that not only will be important in energy terms, but, if we get this right, will create massive supply chain opportunities to build out manufacturing at our ports in Port Talbot and in ports across the whole of Wales. So, let's focus there, where the real opportunity is for Wales, rather than be distracted by issues and questions that are not our responsibility and won't directly benefit us.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Edrychwch, y cyfle go iawn i ni—. Os ydych chi eisiau siarad am ynni ar y môr, mae'r cyfle go iawn i ni yng Nghymru yn ein sector ffermydd gwynt arnofiol ar y môr, yn ein diwydiannau ffrydiau llanw a môr-lynnoedd llanw. Dyna ble mae'r cyfle go iawn o ran swyddi. Felly, gadewch inni ganolbwyntio ar hynny, gan fod negeseuon pwysig lle byddai'n ddefnyddiol pe gallem siarad ag un llais i annog Llywodraeth y DU, er enghraifft, i nodi gwerth strategol ynni'r môr, ffermydd gwynt arnofiol ar y môr, ac ynni'r llanw. Mae gennym asedau daearyddol unigryw. Na, nid ydynt yn cynnwys tanwydd ffosil, ond maent yn bendant yn sectorau'r dyfodol a fydd nid yn unig yn bwysig o ran ynni, ond os gwnawn hyn yn iawn, byddant yn creu cyfleoedd enfawr yn y gadwyn gyflenwi i gynyddu gweithgynhyrchu yn ein porthladdoedd ym Mhort Talbot ac mewn porthladdoedd ledled Cymru gyfan. Felly, gadewch inni ganolbwyntio ar hynny, lle mae'r cyfle go iawn i Gymru, yn hytrach na rhoi ein sylw i faterion a chwestiynau nad ydynt yn gyfrifoldeb i ni ac na fyddant o fudd uniongyrchol i ni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Minister. The biggest word in that statement I picked up on was 'if' we get this right. That's a very big 'if' indeed.

But, moving on, today, Reform UK will lead a debate calling for a ban on face coverings used to conceal identities and intimidate the public. Wales has become a country where criminals can hide their faces while law-abiding citizens are frightened to walk down their own high streets. Across Wales, hard-working businesses are struggling, shopkeepers face intimidation and theft, customers are being driven away, and once-thriving town centres are suffering, leading to damage to our economic outlook. All too often, those responsible are hiding behind balaclavas, riding illegal e-bikes, making it harder for the police to identify them. Minister, we both know that enough is enough. Our high streets belong to families, shoppers and hard-working businesses, not masked thugs. We know this matter is reserved to the police, but councils across Wales are considering using their powers to ban face coverings, including balaclavas. We in Reform will do everything we can to support them. Minister, do you agree that Reform UK's face coverings ban would curb anti-social behaviour and help protect Welsh town centres?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog. Y gair pwysicaf y sylwais arno yn y datganiad hwnnw oedd 'os' y gwnawn hyn yn iawn. Mae hwnnw'n 'os' mawr iawn yn wir.

Ond gan symud ymlaen, heddiw, bydd Reform UK yn arwain dadl yn galw am waharddiad ar orchuddion a ddefnyddir i guddio wynebau ac i ddychryn y cyhoedd. Mae Cymru wedi dod yn wlad lle gall troseddwyr guddio eu hwynebau tra bod ofn cerdded ar hyd eu strydoedd mawr eu hunain ar ddinasyddion sy'n ufudd i'r gyfraith. Ledled Cymru, mae busnesau gweithgar yn ei chael hi'n anodd, mae siopwyr yn wynebu bygythiad a lladradau, mae cwsmeriaid yn cadw draw, ac mae canol trefi a fu unwaith yn ffyniannus yn dioddef, gan arwain at niwed i'n rhagolygon economaidd. Yn rhy aml, mae'r rhai sy'n gyfrifol yn cuddio y tu ôl i falaclafas, yn reidio beiciau trydan anghyfreithlon, gan ei gwneud yn anos i'r heddlu eu hadnabod. Weinidog, gwyddom mai digon yw digon. Mae ein strydoedd mawr yn eiddo i deuluoedd, siopwyr a busnesau gweithgar, nid i labystiaid mewn mygydau. Gwyddom fod hwn yn fater a gedwir yn ôl i'r heddlu, ond mae cynghorau ledled Cymru yn ystyried defnyddio eu pwerau i wahardd gorchuddion wyneb, gan gynnwys balaclafas. Byddwn ni yn Reform yn gwneud popeth yn ein gallu i'w cefnogi. Weinidog, a ydych chi'n cytuno y byddai gwaharddiad Reform UK ar orchuddion wyneb yn cyfyngu ar ymddygiad gwrthgymdeithasol ac yn helpu i ddiogelu canol trefi Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: How this is relevant to these particular questions—. But, look, this is an attempt, once again, to use this platform to sow division. Speak to the shop workers' union—there's a very real issue in terms of the abuse that they face. Meet with the unions and understand the proposals that they are bringing forward to actually make a difference to those workers' lives, not constantly use this place as a platform just to play politics and sow division and hate.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Sut y mae hyn yn berthnasol i'r cwestiynau penodol hyn—. Ond edrychwch, dyma ymgais, unwaith eto, i ddefnyddio'r platfform hwn i hau ymraniad. Siaradwch ag undeb y gweithwyr siopau—mae problem wirioneddol o ran y gamdriniaeth y maent yn ei hwynebu. Cyfarfyddwch â'r undebau a deallwch y cynigion y maent yn eu cyflwyno i wneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol i fywydau'r gweithwyr hynny, nid defnyddio'r lle hwn yn gyson fel llwyfan i chwarae gwleidyddiaeth a hau ymraniad a chasineb.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Shav Taj.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Labour spokesperson, Shav Taj.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We've been talking about data, and of course data centres have been in the news quite a lot recently. The planning Minister recently responded to a written question of mine stating that the current system for approving data centres has robust checks and balances in place to ensure that their environmental and community impacts are properly considered. Now, does the Cabinet Minister agree with the planning Minister? And, if the current system is robust for all data centre applications, why is his Government then writing a data centre framework?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym wedi bod yn sôn am ddata, ac wrth gwrs, mae canolfannau data wedi cael llawer o sylw yn y newyddion yn ddiweddar. Yn ddiweddar, ymatebodd y Gweinidog cynllunio i gwestiwn ysgrifenedig gennyf yn nodi bod gan y system bresennol ar gyfer cymeradwyo canolfannau data drefniadau cadarn ar waith i sicrhau bod eu heffeithiau amgylcheddol a chymunedol yn cael eu hystyried yn briodol. Nawr, a yw'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn cytuno â'r Gweinidog cynllunio? Ac os yw'r system bresennol yn gadarn ar gyfer pob cais am ganolfan ddata, pam felly y mae ei Lywodraeth yn ysgrifennu fframwaith canolfannau data?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: What I think that we've said is that we are bringing forward a general policy framework around data centres. I will leave it to the planning Minister to address the planning dimension of that. Technology changes all the time, and I think that, because of the number of dimensions involved in relation to data centres—their potential contribution to the economy, but also the need to make sure that legitimate questions around land use, around the use of water and the use of energy are addressed properly—it is sensible for us to have a framework, as most other countries are doing at the moment, to ensure that we maximise the benefits and the opportunities, but also mitigate against any potential downside were a framework of that nature not put in place.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n credu mai'r hyn rydym wedi'i ddweud yw ein bod yn cyflwyno fframwaith polisi cyffredinol o amgylch canolfannau data. Fe'i gadawaf i'r Gweinidog cynllunio fynd i'r afael â'r elfen gynllunio o hynny. Mae technoleg yn newid drwy'r amser, ac oherwydd yr elfennau niferus sy'n gysylltiedig â chanolfannau data—eu cyfraniad posibl i'r economi, ond hefyd yr angen i sicrhau y rhoddir ystyriaeth lawn i gwestiynau teilwng ynghylch defnydd tir, defnydd dŵr a defnydd ynni—ei bod yn synhwyrol inni gael fframwaith, fel y mae'r rhan fwyaf o wledydd eraill yn ei wneud ar hyn o bryd, i sicrhau ein bod yn gwneud y mwyaf o'r manteision a'r cyfleoedd, ond hefyd i liniaru unrhyw anfanteision posibl pe na bai fframwaith o'r natur honno ar waith.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Janet Finch-Saunders.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Conservatives spokesperson, Janet Finch-Saunders.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Of course, Cabinet Minister, our portfolio covers connectivity across Wales, and good broadband and strong mobile signal is certainly a huge component of that. Ofcom found that much of Wales has the poorest broadband provision in the UK. Wales has an average broadband speed of 6.5 Mbps compared with the UK average of 7.5 Mbps. Twelve local authorities across Wales are classified as having the poorest broadband provision, with some areas receiving speeds of only around 2 Mbps. I've spoken so many times about this with the previous Government, and it is fair to say that, in rural areas, parts of my constituency of Bangor Conwy Môn, some residents are still facing extremely poor broadband connectivity. Now, we need to see increased emphasis—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Wrth gwrs, Weinidog Cabinet, mae ein portffolio'n cynnwys cysylltedd ledled Cymru, ac mae band eang da a signal ffonau symudol cryf yn sicr yn elfen enfawr o hynny. Canfu Ofcom fod gan lawer o Gymru'r ddarpariaeth band eang waethaf yn y DU. Mae gan Gymru gyflymder band eang cyfartalog o 6.5 Mbps o gymharu â chyfartaledd y DU o 7.5 Mbps. Mae deuddeg awdurdod lleol ledled Cymru wedi'u dosbarthu fel rhai sydd â'r ddarpariaeth band eang waethaf, gyda rhai ardaloedd yn cael cyflymderau o oddeutu 2 Mbps yn unig. Rwyf wedi siarad gymaint o weithiau am hyn gyda'r Llywodraeth flaenorol, ac mae'n deg dweud, mewn ardaloedd gwledig, rhannau o fy etholaeth i, sef Bangor Conwy Môn, fod rhai trigolion yn dal i wynebu cysylltedd band eang gwael iawn. Nawr, mae angen inni weld mwy o bwyslais—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Can we have the question, please?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A gawn ni'r cwestiwn, os gwelwch yn dda?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yes. We need to see a greater emphasis on funding. How will you address these notspots?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Iawn. Mae angen inni weld mwy o bwyslais ar gyllid. Sut y byddwch chi'n mynd i'r afael â'r mannau gwan hyn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I totally accept the premise of the question, that this is vitally important for social and economic reasons. Of course, it's fundamentally a UK Government responsibility, and so one of the things that we absolutely need to do is to get them to deliver faster on the promises that they've made through Project Gigabit and others.

In every infrastructure investment that the UK Government makes, it's always us in Wales that are at the wrong end of a very long line. And it shouldn't be the case, actually, because digital infrastructure, by its very nature, has the capacity to actually limit the costs of distance. But, unfortunately, the way that decisions have been made in the UK, it has had the opposite effect. We will do what we can within our resources to make up for the deficiencies of the decisions made by the UK Government. We will obviously put every pressure that we can to make sure that they live up to their responsibilities.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n derbyn sail y cwestiwn yn llwyr, fod hyn yn hanfodol bwysig am resymau cymdeithasol ac economaidd. Wrth gwrs, mae'n gyfrifoldeb i Lywodraeth y DU yn ei hanfod, ac felly un o'r pethau y mae angen i ni eu gwneud yw eu cymell i fynd ati'n gyflymach i gyflawni'r addewidion a wnaethant drwy Brosiect Gigabit a phethau eraill.

Ym mhob buddsoddiad seilwaith y mae Llywodraeth y DU yn ei wneud, ni yng Nghymru sydd bob amser ar y pen anghywir mewn ciw hir iawn. Ac ni ddylai hynny fod yn wir, mewn gwirionedd, gan fod gan seilwaith digidol ynddo'i hun y gallu i leihau costau pellter. Ond yn anffodus, mae'r ffordd y gwnaed y penderfyniadau yn y DU wedi cael effaith i'r gwrthwyneb. Byddwn yn gwneud yr hyn a allwn o fewn ein hadnoddau i wneud iawn am ddiffygion y penderfyniadau a wnaed gan Lywodraeth y DU. Yn amlwg, byddwn yn rhoi'r holl bwysau y gallwn ei roi i sicrhau eu bod yn cyflawni eu cyfrifoldebau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. I just need to correct you. In the previous UK Conservative Government, under David Cameron, £56.9 million of funding came directly into Wales for superfast Cymru broadband. And we then had Project Gigabit under Boris Johnson, the Right Honourable, again under a Conservative Government. This must continue. And additionally, companies are now phasing out copper cables. So, my residents in Bangor Conwy Môn are really struggling, because, with the phasing out of copper cables, which connect many residents to landlines, there's growing concern about people living in rural areas with poor mobile phone coverage. What steps are you taking, Cabinet Minister, to ensure that those households in rural, isolated parts—and there are many within Wales, but there are a lot in Bangor Conwy Môn—? How are you going to support them as a Government throughout this transition, and how are you going to work with the UK Government now to ensure we get much better funding into Wales for this? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Mae angen i mi eich cywiro. O dan Lywodraeth Geidwadol flaenorol y DU, o dan arweiniad David Cameron, daeth £56.9 miliwn o gyllid yn uniongyrchol i Gymru ar gyfer band eang cyflym iawn yng Nghymru. Ac yna cawsom Brosiect Gigabit o dan y Gwir Anrhydeddus Boris Johnson, unwaith eto o dan Lywodraeth Geidwadol. Rhaid i hyn barhau. Ac yn ogystal, mae cwmnïau bellach yn rhoi'r gorau yn raddol i ddefnyddio ceblau copr. Felly, mae fy mhreswylwyr ym Mangor Conwy Môn yn ei chael hi'n anodd iawn, oherwydd, wrth iddynt roi'r gorau yn raddol i ddefnyddio ceblau copr, sy'n cysylltu llawer o drigolion â llinellau tir, mae pryder cynyddol am bobl sy'n byw mewn ardaloedd gwledig sydd â signal ffonau symudol gwael. Pa gamau rydych chi'n eu cymryd, Weinidog Cabinet, i sicrhau bod cartrefi mewn rhannau gwledig, anghysbell—ac mae nifer yng Nghymru, ond mae llawer ym Mangor Conwy Môn—? Sut rydych chi'n mynd i'w cefnogi fel Llywodraeth drwy'r cyfnod pontio hwn, a sut rydych chi'n mynd i weithio gyda Llywodraeth y DU nawr i sicrhau ein bod yn cael cyllid llawer gwell i Gymru ar gyfer hyn? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, as I said, we will first of all hold the UK Government and the relevant stakeholders to the commitments that they have made. Where it's possible, within the resources that we have, and within the levers that we have, we will do everything that we can to mitigate any of the deficiencies from the lack of investment that flows from the UK Government. I've met with some of the key companies in the sector to see in which ways we can work smarter, develop innovative solutions, in order to make sure that no community or no individual, as far as is possible, is digitally left behind. But we do need the UK Government to put that investment in that was promised.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, fel y dywedais, yn gyntaf oll byddwn yn dal Llywodraeth y DU a'r rhanddeiliaid perthnasol i'r ymrwymiadau y maent wedi'u gwneud. Lle bo'n bosibl, o fewn yr adnoddau sydd gennym, ac o fewn yr ysgogiadau sydd gennym, byddwn yn gwneud popeth yn ein gallu i liniaru unrhyw ddiffyg o ganlyniad i'r diffyg buddsoddiad gan Lywodraeth y DU. Rwyf wedi cyfarfod â rhai o'r cwmnïau allweddol yn y sector i weld ym mha ffyrdd y gallwn weithio'n ddoethach, datblygu atebion arloesol, er mwyn sicrhau nad oes unrhyw gymuned nac unrhyw unigolyn, cyn belled ag y bo modd, yn cael eu gadael ar ôl yn ddigidol. Ond mae angen i Lywodraeth y DU ddarparu'r buddsoddiad a addawyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Electric Arc Furnace

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Pa drafodaethau y mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cynnal gyda'r Grid Cenedlaethol ynglŷn â gosod ffwrnais arc drydan ym Mhort Talbot? OQ64761
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What discussions is the Government having with National Grid regarding the electric arc furnace installation in Port Talbot? OQ64761

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae swyddogion Llywodraeth Cymru yn cynnal cyfarfodydd rheolaidd gyda National Grid Electricity Transmission. Mae gwaith gosod ffwrnais arc drydan Tata Steel UK yn fater masnachol. Fodd bynnag, rydyn ni’n codi'r mater fel y bo'n briodol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Government officials hold regular meetings with National Grid Electricity Transmission. Tata Steel UK’s electric arc furnace installation is a commercial matter. However, we do raise the matter as appropriate.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Weinidog. The decision to close the blast furnaces in Port Talbot was disastrous for my local community. Thousands of jobs were lost and the impact on the wider economy is severe. The National Grid connection offer for the new electric arc furnace was contracted for the end of 2027. However, a range of factors, such as planning and ground conditions, are threatening to delay the project, and some sources are saying that it could be as late as 2029 before the new furnace comes online.

Previously, you've mentioned that the Welsh Government is not a party to the commercial agreement between National Grid and Tata, but I'd like to ask what conversations you've had with National Grid regarding these delays and what further action will you take to prevent any further issues that could harm jobs and the local economy in Port Talbot. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog. Roedd y penderfyniad i gau'r ffwrneisi chwyth ym Mhort Talbot yn drychinebus i fy nghymuned leol. Collwyd miloedd o swyddi ac mae'r effaith ar yr economi ehangach yn ddifrifol. Roedd y cynnig i gysylltu'r ffwrnais arc drydan newydd â'r Grid Cenedlaethol wedi'i gontractio ar gyfer diwedd 2027. Fodd bynnag, mae amrywiaeth o ffactorau, megis cynllunio a chyflwr y tir, yn bygwth gohirio'r prosiect, ac mae rhai ffynonellau'n dweud y gallai fod mor hwyr â 2029 cyn i'r ffwrnais newydd ddod yn weithredol.

Rydych chi wedi dweud yn flaenorol nad yw Llywodraeth Cymru yn rhan o'r cytundeb masnachol rhwng y Grid Cenedlaethol a Tata, ond hoffwn ofyn pa sgyrsiau a gawsoch chi gyda'r Grid Cenedlaethol ynghylch yr oedi hwn a pha gamau pellach y byddwch chi'n eu cymryd i atal unrhyw broblemau pellach a allai niweidio swyddi a'r economi leol ym Mhort Talbot. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yes, I'm very grateful to the Member for his supplementary question. I met with Tata Steel UK's chief executive officer, Rajesh Nair, and the steel unions at Tata's Port Talbot site on 24 September to receive a further update on developments. We focused on a whole range of matters, including the issues around connectivity to the grid, which is at the heart of his question, but there were other matters as well around UK Government trade quotas and the effect that that was having on the domestic steel market. Following that meeting, I did meet with the UK Government's Minister for Reindustrialisation, Blair McDougall, together with the Secretary of State for Wales to discuss some of the matters that were raised.

So, we are constantly engaging with the company, with the unions and also with the UK Government to ensure that Wales does—. I absolutely agree with him about the tragedy, really, of the loss of the blast furnaces, but we now need to make sure that we maximise the opportunity represented by the electric arc furnace. It will be the first or second-largest electric arc furnace anywhere in the world. There is the prospect for us to be producing more than 50 per cent of UK domestic steel capacity at a time when the UK Government has said that it wants to increase the level of domestic procurement. So, there is an opportunity there that is massive. We need to stay focused, I absolutely agree, in order to seize that opportunity.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n ddiolchgar iawn i'r Aelod am ei gwestiwn atodol. Cyfarfûm â phrif swyddog gweithredol Tata Steel UK, Rajesh Nair, a'r undebau dur ar safle Tata ym Mhort Talbot ar 24 Medi i gael diweddariad pellach ar ddatblygiadau. Fe wnaethom ganolbwyntio ar ystod eang o faterion, gan gynnwys y materion ynghylch cysylltedd â'r grid, sef yr hyn sydd wrth wraidd ei gwestiwn, ond roedd materion eraill hefyd yn codi ynglŷn â chwotâu masnach Llywodraeth y DU a'r effaith yr oedd hynny'n ei chael ar y farchnad ddur ddomestig. Yn dilyn y cyfarfod hwnnw, cyfarfûm â Gweinidog Ailddiwydiannu Llywodraeth y DU, Blair McDougall, ynghyd ag Ysgrifennydd Gwladol Cymru i drafod rhai o'r materion a godwyd.

Felly, rydym yn ymgysylltu'n gyson â'r cwmni, gyda'r undebau a hefyd gyda Llywodraeth y DU i sicrhau bod Cymru'n—. Rwy'n cytuno'n llwyr ag ef am y drasiedi o golli'r ffwrneisi chwyth, ond mae angen inni wneud yn siŵr nawr ein bod yn gwneud y mwyaf o'r cyfle a ddaw gan y ffwrnais arc drydan. Dyma'r ffwrnais arc drydan fwyaf neu'r ail fwyaf yn unman yn y byd. Mae potensial i ni allu cynhyrchu mwy na 50 y cant o gapasiti dur domestig y DU ar adeg pan fo Llywodraeth y DU wedi dweud ei bod eisiau cynyddu'r lefel sy'n cael ei chaffael yn ddomestig. Felly, mae yna gyfle enfawr yno. Rwy'n cytuno'n llwyr fod angen inni barhau i gadw ffocws er mwyn manteisio ar y cyfle hwnnw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Gweinidog Cabinet, I visited National Grid at Margam substation over the summer to discuss the connection to the Port Talbot substation needed for Tata Steel's electric arc furnace. National Grid explained that there were a number of unexpected barriers, as the Member has previously alluded to, for example, poor ground conditions that increase the number of piles required in the ground from the initial 400 to 11,000, adding an estimated 34 weeks to complete construction. They also outlined plans to recover some of that lost time. Given the importance of the project to the future of steel making in Port Talbot, can the Gweinidog confirm whether any progress has been made in reducing that 34-week delay and whether there is scope to shorten the construction programme further?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog Cabinet, ymwelais â'r Grid Cenedlaethol yn is-orsaf Margam dros yr haf i drafod y cysylltiad ag is-orsaf Port Talbot sydd ei angen ar gyfer ffwrnais arc drydan Tata Steel. Esboniodd y Grid Cenedlaethol fod nifer o rwystrau annisgwyl, fel y nododd yr Aelod yn flaenorol, er enghraifft, cyflwr gwael y tir sy'n cynyddu nifer y pyst sydd eu hangen yn y ddaear o'r 400 cychwynnol i 11,000, gan ychwanegu 34 wythnos amcangyfrifedig i gwblhau'r gwaith adeiladu. Hefyd, fe wnaethant amlinellu cynlluniau i adfer rhywfaint o'r amser coll hwnnw. O ystyried pwysigrwydd y prosiect i ddyfodol cynhyrchiant dur ym Mhort Talbot, a all y Gweinidog gadarnhau p'un a wnaed unrhyw gynnydd ar leihau'r oedi o 34 wythnos ac a oes lle i fyrhau'r rhaglen adeiladu ymhellach?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I think I will have to leave it to the company to share any information it would like to put in the public domain in relation to the current state of play. This is obviously market sensitive information. You can appreciate that it's most appropriate that that comes from the company, and I'm sure that they would want to allow the workforce to hear that information first. 

But I think that one of the positive things that I'm sure that Tata Steel would not in any way have a problem with me sharing was the very positive experience that they had with Neath Port Talbot Council. We often hear, don't we, in the context of economic development, concerns around planning delay. Well, the message that I very clearly heard from the company was that they were incredibly impressed by the way in which the planning officers of Neath Port Talbot Council had really worked at an incredible pace and shown some innovation in how to manage that process. And there may be wider lessons that can be shared with other major projects across Wales. And we talked a little bit about how we could share that best practice.

As a result of this experience as well, we are very conscious of the importance of focusing in a very granular fashion on major developments and what that means for the grid. And we are, as I said, in discussion with National Grid Electricity Transmission and other relevant stakeholders to make sure that we learn from this experience and make sure that we identify areas where we can make progress in terms of the grid connection and its important role in our economy.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n credu y bydd yn rhaid imi adael i'r cwmni rannu unrhyw wybodaeth yr hoffai ei roi yn y parth cyhoeddus mewn perthynas â'r sefyllfa bresennol. Mae hon yn amlwg yn wybodaeth sensitif i'r farchnad. Gallwch ddeall ei bod yn briodol i hynny ddod gan y cwmni, ac rwy'n siŵr y byddent am ganiatáu i'r gweithlu glywed y wybodaeth honno yn gyntaf.

Ond rwy'n meddwl mai un o'r pethau cadarnhaol yr wyf yn siŵr na fyddai gan Tata Steel broblem gyda mi'n ei rannu oedd y profiad cadarnhaol iawn a gawsant gyda Chyngor Castell-nedd Port Talbot. Rydym yn aml yn clywed pryderon, onid ydym, yng nghyd-destun datblygu economaidd, ynghylch oedi gyda chynllunio. Wel, y neges a glywais yn glir iawn gan y cwmni oedd bod y ffordd yr oedd swyddogion cynllunio Cyngor Castell-nedd Port Talbot wedi gweithio ar gyflymder anhygoel ac wedi dangos arloesedd o ran sut i reoli'r broses honno wedi creu argraff enfawr arnynt. Ac efallai y bydd gwersi ehangach y gellir eu rhannu â phrosiectau mawr eraill ledled Cymru. Ac fe wnaethom siarad ychydig ynglŷn â sut y gallem rannu'r arfer gorau hwnnw.

O ganlyniad i'r profiad hwn hefyd, rydym yn ymwybodol iawn o bwysigrwydd cadw ffocws manwl iawn ar ddatblygiadau mawr a beth y mae hynny'n ei olygu i'r grid. Ac fel y dywedais, rydym yn trafod gyda Trawsyrru Trydan y Grid Cenedlaethol a rhanddeiliaid perthnasol eraill i wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn dysgu o'r profiad hwn a gwneud yn siŵr ein bod yn nodi meysydd lle gallwn wneud cynnydd o ran y cysylltiad grid a'i rôl bwysig yn ein heconomi.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae'r rhaglen lywodraethu yn nodi'r ystod o fesurau y byddwn ni'n eu cymryd i wella cyfleoedd a chanlyniadau economaidd ar gyfer pob rhan o Gymru. Mae hyn yn cynnwys y genhadaeth genedlaethol ar gynhyrchiant, gan gefnogi busnesau bach a'r stryd fawr i ffynnu a sicrhau bod gan Gymru y sgiliau sydd eu hangen arni ar gyfer y dyfodol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The programme for government sets out the range of measures that we will take to improve economic opportunities and outcomes for every part of Wales. This includes the national productivity mission, supporting small businesses and high streets to thrive and ensuring Wales has the skills it needs for the future.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am eich ateb, Weinidog. Fy mhryder yw bod gormod o'n pobl ifanc talentog ym Mlaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni yn teimlo bod yn rhaid iddynt symud i ffwrdd i ddod o hyd i yrfaoedd cynaliadwy hirdymor. Tu hwnt i ffrydiau cyllido cyffredinol, pa warantau targedig all Llywodraeth Cymru eu cynnig i greu swyddi medrus sy'n ddiogel ar gyfer y dyfodol yn eu milltir sgwâr fel y gallwn stopio allforio ein cenhedlaeth nesaf?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for your response, Minister. My concern is that too many of our talented young people in Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni feel that they have to move away to find careers that are sustainable and long term. Beyond the general funding streams, what targeted assurances can the Welsh Government provide to create skilled, futureproofed jobs in their local area so that we can stop exporting our next generation?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn atodol. Mae'r cwestiwn yma yn greiddiol i'n strategaeth economaidd ni. Mi oeddwn i, y bore yma, wedi cwrdd, am y tro cyntaf, gyda'r panel sydd yn ein cynorthwyo ni i ddylunio'r asiantaeth ddatblygu, ac un o'r themâu roeddwn i wedi'u pwysleisio oedd yr angen i sicrhau ein bod ni'n cynhyrchu swyddi da ym mhobman. Dŷn ni ddim eisiau gweld sefyllfa lle mae Cymru yn efelychu yr hyn rŷn ni wedi gweld o ran datblygiad anwastad y Deyrnas Unedig, lle mae ffyniant ond yn cronni mewn un cornel o'n gwlad. Rŷn ni eisiau i dde-ddwyrain Cymru ffynnu, rŷn ni eisiau i ogledd-ddwyrain Cymru ffynnu, ac rŷn ni'n falch iawn o'r llwyddiant sydd yn digwydd yno, ond rŷn ni eisiau i hynny gael ei ledu drwy'r Cymoedd, drwy Flaenau'r Cymoedd, i'r gorllewin, mewn i Gymru wledig, i'r gogledd-orllewin. Mae'n rhaid codi Cymru oll i fyny, a dyna'r ffordd rŷn fel Llywodraeth am weithredu, a dyna'r nod a'r genhadaeth rŷn ni wedi'u rhoi yn barod i'r asiantaeth ddatblygu newydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for that supplementary question. This question is at the heart of our economic strategy. This morning, I met, for the first time, with the panel assisting us to design the new development agency, and one of the themes that I emphasised was the need to ensure that we do generate good jobs everywhere. We don't want to see a situation where Wales emulates what we've seen in terms of the uneven development across the United Kingdom, where prosperity only accrues in one corner of our nation. We want the south-east of Wales to prosper, we want the north-east of Wales to prosper, and we are very proud of the success that there has been there, but we also want that to permeate through the Valleys, the Heads of the Valleys, into the west, into rural Wales, and into the north-west of Wales. We must raise up the whole of Wales, and that is how we as a Government intend to operate, and that is the aim and the mission that we have already given to the new development agency.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, one concern I've got, from speaking to lots of people in the constituency, who feel young people are leaving the area of Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni at a large pace now. We can see that the population age is going up in every census, and anyone who's been around the town recently feels that young people are leaving for cities, going over to England or to other parts of the world. What help can you do to incentivise businesses into the constituency, because it's businesses that will create those jobs, but Government have the levers of power to pull? So, I'd be grateful if you could tell us today what levers you're going to pull to bring in those jobs to keep young people here.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, mae gennyf bryder yn sgil siarad â llawer o bobl yn yr etholaeth sy'n teimlo bod pobl ifanc yn gadael ardal Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni yn gyflym iawn nawr. Gallwn weld bod oedran y boblogaeth yn codi ym mhob cyfrifiad, ac mae unrhyw un sydd wedi bod o gwmpas y dref yn ddiweddar yn teimlo bod pobl ifanc yn gadael am y dinasoedd, yn mynd draw i Loegr neu i rannau eraill o'r byd. Pa help y gallwch chi ei roi i ysgogi busnesau i ddod i mewn i'r etholaeth, oherwydd busnesau fydd yn creu'r swyddi hynny, ond gan y Llywodraeth y mae'r liferi grym? Felly, buaswn yn ddiolchgar pe gallech chi ddweud wrthym heddiw pa liferi rydych chi'n mynd i'w tynnu i ddod â'r swyddi hynny i mewn i gadw pobl ifanc yma.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I think that's a really important question, and Governments, of course, at one level, have to create the broad conditions of economic success, but we also have to work in a very, very focused way, in the near term, which is about job creation in businesses. Ultimately, Governments can help create those conditions, but it's not Governments that regenerate communities; it's communities and businesses within them that regenerate communities and create those jobs. So, certainly, in looking at the role of inward investment, for example, I think it's critical that we think about the way in which we can make sure that there are opportunities for foreign direct investment in every part of Wales. And, interestingly, in a conversation I had with one of the leading firms in the compound semiconductor cluster, they brought many of their suppliers into Wales, they wanted to be close to the cluster, but those companies said, 'We don't want to be in Newport. We don't need to be in Newport. We want to be in the northern Valleys. We think that's a better fit for us. The skills are there. There are advantages for us.' And there are, of course, fantastic transport links. So, there are unique assets, both people based and also physical assets, that can be leveraged in every community. And we need to be thinking in that granular way to identify opportunities that fit, community by community, across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n credu bod hwnnw'n gwestiwn pwysig iawn, ac ar un lefel, rhaid i Lywodraethau greu amodau eang llwyddiant economaidd, ond rhaid inni hefyd weithio mewn ffordd ofalus iawn yn y tymor byr, sy'n ymwneud â chreu swyddi mewn busnesau. Yn y pen draw, gall Llywodraethau helpu i greu'r amodau hynny, ond nid Llywodraethau sy'n adfywio cymunedau; cymunedau a'r busnesau o'u mewn sy'n adfywio cymunedau ac yn creu'r swyddi hynny. Felly, yn sicr, wrth edrych ar rôl mewnfuddsoddiad, er enghraifft, rwy'n credu ei bod hi'n hanfodol ein bod yn meddwl am y ffordd y gallwn wneud yn siŵr bod cyfleoedd ar gyfer buddsoddiad uniongyrchol tramor ym mhob rhan o Gymru. Ac yn ddiddorol, mewn sgwrs a gefais gydag un o'r cwmnïau mwyaf blaenllaw yn y clwstwr lled-ddargludyddion cyfansawdd, fe wnaethant ddod â llawer o'u cyflenwyr i Gymru, roeddent eisiau bod yn agos at y clwstwr, ond dywedodd y cwmnïau hynny, 'Nid ydym eisiau bod yng Nghasnewydd. Nid oes angen inni fod yng Nghasnewydd. Rydym eisiau bod yn y Cymoedd gogleddol. Rydym yn meddwl bod hynny'n fwy addas i ni. Mae'r sgiliau yno. Mae manteision i ni.' Ac wrth gwrs, mae yna gysylltiadau trafnidiaeth gwych. Felly, mae yna asedau unigryw, yn seiliedig ar bobl a hefyd ar asedau ffisegol, y gellir eu defnyddio ym mhob cymuned. Ac mae angen inni feddwl yn y ffordd fanwl honno i nodi cyfleoedd sy'n addas, fesul cymuned, ledled Cymru.
