XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. Sut mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cefnogi busnesau i elwa ar wariant caffael cyhoeddus? OQ64792
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. How is the Welsh Government supporting businesses to benefit from public procurement spending? OQ64792

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Rydyn ni'n benderfynol bod mwy o fusnesau yng Nghymru yn elwa ar gaffael cyhoeddus. Mae Busnes Cymru yn darparu cyngor wedi'i deilwra, tra bod Deddf Caffael 2023 yn ei gwneud hi'n ofynnol i awdurdodau, mewn caffaeliadau a gwmpesir, ystyried rhwystrau sy'n wynebu busnesau ac a ellir rhannu contractau yn lotiau priodol. Rydyn ni hefyd yn datblygu opsiynau polisi i gryfhau'r cymorth ymhellach.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We are determined that more Welsh businesses benefit from public procurement. Business Wales provides tailored advice, while the Procurement Act 2023 requires authorities, in covered procurements, to consider barriers facing businesses and whether contracts can appropriately be divided into lots. We are also developing policy options to strengthen support further.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. The Plaid Cymru manifesto sets a target to significantly increase the amount of public procurement spending within Wales to 70 per cent. Given that we spend £11 billion every year on public procurement, there's enormous potential there, isn't there, to better support Welsh businesses, potentially to create tens of thousands of jobs and to boost local supply chains as well. And the best bit, of course, is that this isn't new money; this is money that we're already spending. We need to spend it smarter; we need to make sure more of it goes to local businesses, to our workers and to our communities. So, can the Minister outline what practical steps he's taking to attain that 70 per cent target, and how we plan to measure progress? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr. Mae maniffesto Plaid Cymru yn gosod targed i gynyddu swm y gwariant caffael cyhoeddus yng Nghymru yn sylweddol i 70 y cant. O ystyried ein bod yn gwario £11 biliwn bob blwyddyn ar gaffael cyhoeddus, mae potensial enfawr yno, onid oes, i gefnogi busnesau Cymru yn well, ac o bosibl i greu degau o filoedd o swyddi ac i roi hwb i gadwyni cyflenwi lleol hefyd. A'r peth gorau, wrth gwrs, yw nad arian newydd yw hwn; mae hwn yn arian rydym eisoes yn ei wario. Mae angen inni ei wario'n ddoethach; mae angen inni wneud yn siŵr bod mwy ohono'n mynd i fusnesau lleol, i'n gweithwyr ac i'n cymunedau. Felly, a all y Gweinidog amlinellu pa gamau ymarferol y mae'n eu cymryd i gyrraedd y targed o 70 y cant, a sut y bwriadwn fesur cynnydd? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yes, absolutely. The formal responsibility is with the finance Minister, but with this, it is very critically, as the Member says, a massive economic driver. It's one of the key tools of industrial policy, actually, public procurement. So, beyond the target, how are we going to achieve it then, getting up to that 70 per cent? We will be setting this out in more detail very shortly. But part of it is working through, as I said, the way in which procurement contracts are structured. So, traditionally, large-scale construction contracts, for example, tend to go to companies the other side of the border because of the scale and the risk involved. Well, just breaking those contracts up into smaller lots, it sounds very simple, but it has a huge impact, and it allows then companies, financially and practically, to get—. The same companies that often end up delivering the project anyway, but now you're taking out a tier and keeping all of that value in Wales.

I think that part of it is also about training companies up, companies that possibly have not been involved in larger scale procurement exercises and might have some fear or inhibition about doing so, so working with them in a different context. I'm going to a procurement exercise in north Wales in relation to the Wylfa project. It's the same kind of approach: how to get Welsh SMEs, many of which have never thought of putting themselves forward, just to understand, 'Look, there's nothing to be worried about; it's a process. You've got the skills, you've got the capacity, you can deliver the product, in many cases at lower cost; you've just got to have the confidence to put your name forward.'
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn hollol. Y Gweinidog cyllid sydd â'r cyfrifoldeb ffurfiol, ond gyda hyn, mae'n allweddol iawn, fel y dywed yr Aelod, yn sbardun economaidd enfawr. Mae caffael cyhoeddus yn un o brif arfau polisi diwydiannol mewn gwirionedd. Felly, y tu hwnt i'r targed, sut rydym ni'n mynd i gyrraedd y 70 y cant? Byddwn yn nodi hyn yn fanylach cyn bo hir iawn. Ond fel y dywedais, rhan ohono yw gweithio drwy'r ffordd y mae contractau caffael wedi'u strwythuro. Felly, yn draddodiadol, mae contractau adeiladu ar raddfa fawr, er enghraifft, yn tueddu i fynd i gwmnïau ar yr ochr arall i'r ffin oherwydd y raddfa a'r risg sy'n gysylltiedig. Wel, mae torri'r contractau hynny'n lotiau llai yn swnio'n syml iawn, ond mae'n cael effaith enfawr, ac mae'n caniatáu i gwmnïau, yn ariannol ac yn ymarferol, i gael—. Yn aml, yr un cwmnïau sy'n cyflawni'r prosiect beth bynnag, ond nawr rydych chi'n tynnu haen allan ac yn cadw'r holl werth hwnnw yng Nghymru.

Rwy'n credu bod rhan ohono hefyd yn ymwneud â hyfforddi cwmnïau nad ydynt o bosibl wedi bod yn rhan o ymarferion caffael ar raddfa fwy ac a allai fod â pheth ofn neu betruster ynglŷn â gwneud hynny, felly gweithio gyda nhw mewn cyd-destun gwahanol. Rwy'n mynd i ymarfer caffael yng ngogledd Cymru mewn perthynas â phrosiect Wylfa. Yr un math o ddull gweithredu ydyw: sut i gael busnesau bach a chanolig Cymru, y bydd llawer ohonynt heb feddwl am gynnig eu hunain erioed, i ddeall, 'Edrychwch, nid oes dim i boeni yn ei gylch; proses yw hi. Mae gennych chi'r sgiliau, mae gennych chi'r capasiti, gallwch ddarparu'r cynnyrch, ar gost is mewn llawer o achosion; rhaid i chi gael hyder i gynnig eich hunain, dyna i gyd.'

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau bod cymorth i'r sector amddiffyn yn cael ei ystyried mewn ffordd amserol a chymesur. Tra bod y fframwaith buddsoddi moesegol mewn amddiffyn yn cael ei ddatblygu, mae trefniadau interim ar waith i alluogi penderfyniadau brys i gael eu gwneud pan fo angen.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We are committed to ensuring that support for the defence sector is considered in a timely and proportionate way. Whilst the defence ethical investment framework is being developed, interim arrangements are in place to enable urgent decisions to be taken where required.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Earlier this year, I visited PMB Battery Technologies, a cutting-edge research and manufacturing company that operates facilities in Ebbw Vale and in Adelaide, Australia. This is a company specialising in advanced battery technology, and a great benefit to the local economy and the people it employs. That day, I met directly with apprentices at the company, young people from Ebbw Vale and the local area, fresh out of education, now in high-skilled and well-paid, meaningful employment. This is exactly the sort of industry we need to attract to deprived areas like Blaenau Gwent, which suffer with high levels of people, especially young people, classified as NEET, not in employment, education or training.

Companies like this rely on Government grants to expand their operations in Wales and ensure that old and outdated facilities meet the needs of modern research and manufacturing. So, what steps is the Government taking to ensure that competitive modern industries are kept in Wales, grants are timely, and that they are not pushed to relocate elsewhere?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Yn gynharach eleni, ymwelais â PMB Battery Technologies, cwmni ymchwil a gweithgynhyrchu arloesol sy'n gweithredu cyfleusterau yng Nglynebwy ac yn Adelaide, Awstralia. Mae hwn yn gwmni sy'n arbenigo mewn uwch-dechnoleg batri, ac o fudd mawr i'r economi leol a'r bobl y mae'n eu cyflogi. Y diwrnod hwnnw, cyfarfûm yn uniongyrchol â phrentisiaid yn y cwmni, pobl ifanc o Lynebwy a'r ardal leol, a oedd newydd adael addysg, a bellach mewn swydd fedrus werth chweil ar gyflog da. Dyma'r union fath o ddiwydiant y mae angen inni ei ddenu i ardaloedd difreintiedig fel Blaenau Gwent, sy'n dioddef gyda lefelau uchel o bobl, yn enwedig pobl ifanc, wedi'u categoreiddio'n NEET, nad ydynt mewn cyflogaeth, addysg na hyfforddiant.

Mae cwmnïau fel hyn yn dibynnu ar grantiau'r Llywodraeth i ehangu eu gweithgarwch yng Nghymru a sicrhau bod hen gyfleusterau sydd wedi dyddio'n diwallu anghenion ymchwil a gweithgynhyrchu modern. Felly, pa gamau y mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd i sicrhau bod diwydiannau modern cystadleuol yn cael eu cadw yng Nghymru, fod grantiau'n amserol, ac nad ydynt yn cael eu gwthio i adleoli yn rhywle arall?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm grateful to the Member, not least for giving an example of the very phenomenon that I was referring to in response to a colleague earlier, that these high-tech companies can find very, very successful bases in all parts of Wales, including in the northern Valleys. We are committed to doing whatever we can in every sector, but in this sector as well, to support the creation of high-tech jobs. Where decisions are time critical, as I've said on a number of occasions, we've created a route for those decisions to be made exceptionally, before the framework is published and shared with the Senedd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n ddiolchgar i'r Aelod, yn enwedig am roi enghraifft o'r union ffenomen yr oeddwn yn cyfeirio ati mewn ymateb i gyd-Aelod yn gynharach, y gall y cwmnïau uwch-dechnoleg hyn ddod o hyd i safleoedd llwyddiannus iawn ym mhob rhan o Gymru, gan gynnwys y Cymoedd gogleddol. Rydym wedi ymrwymo i wneud yr hyn a allwn ym mhob sector, ond yn y sector hwn hefyd, i gefnogi creu swyddi uwch-dechnoleg. Lle mae gofyn gwneud penderfyniadau'n amserol, fel y dywedais ar sawl achlysur, rydym wedi creu llwybr i'r penderfyniadau hynny gael eu gwneud ar sail eithriadol, cyn i'r fframwaith gael ei gyhoeddi a'i rannu gyda'r Senedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Artificial Intelligence

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 7. Pa waith y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn ei wneud i sicrhau bod deallusrwydd artiffisial yn cael ei fabwysiadu'n foesegol yng Nghymru? OQ64785
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 7. What work is the Cabinet Minister undertaking to ensure the ethical adoption of AI in Wales? OQ64785

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Rydyn ni’n gweithio ar draws y Llywodraeth a chyda gwasanaethau cyhoeddus, busnesau a phartneriaid i gefnogi'r broses o fabwysiadu AI yn ddiogel, yn dryloyw ac yn atebol. Mae hyn yn cynnwys cryfhau sgiliau, caffael cyfrifol, technoleg Gymraeg a'r sylfeini digidol ehangach sydd eu hangen i sicrhau bod AI yn darparu gwerth cyhoeddus ac o fudd i gymunedau ledled Cymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We are working across Government and with public services, businesses and partners to support the safe, transparent and accountable adoption of AI. This includes strengthening skills, responsible procurement, Welsh language technology and the wider digital foundations needed to ensure AI delivers public value and benefits communities across Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. AI-driven automation is having a growing impact on the labour market and especially on entry-level employment and on workplace learning, and is widening already existing inequalities. Young people at the start of their careers are particularly vulnerable to things like job displacement and a lack of fair access to opportunities and face the collapse of those traditional pathways that let graduates and early-career workers gain that essential experience in learning. I know we did touch on this earlier, but what measures is the Cabinet Minister taking to establish clear frameworks for the responsible, ethical and transparent use of AI when it comes to employment, and what is being done to protect and help workers to adapt to changing role requirements and the changing jobs market?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Mae awtomeiddio wedi'i yrru gan ddeallusrwydd artiffisial yn cael effaith gynyddol ar y farchnad lafur ac yn enwedig ar gyflogaeth lefel mynediad ac ar ddysgu yn y gweithle, ac mae'n ehangu anghydraddoldebau sydd eisoes yn bodoli. Mae pobl ifanc ar ddechrau eu gyrfaoedd yn arbennig o agored i bethau fel dadleoli swyddi a diffyg mynediad teg at gyfleoedd ac yn wynebu methiant y llwybrau traddodiadol sy'n caniatáu i raddedigion a gweithwyr gyrfa gynnar gael profiad dysgu hanfodol. Rwy'n gwybod ein bod wedi cyffwrdd â hyn yn gynharach, ond pa fesurau y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn eu cymryd i sefydlu fframweithiau clir ar gyfer y defnydd cyfrifol, moesegol a thryloyw o ddeallusrwydd artiffisial mewn cyflogaeth, a beth sy'n cael ei wneud i ddiogelu a helpu gweithwyr i addasu i ofynion rôl sy'n newid a marchnad swyddi sy'n newid?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The Member raises a really important point. AI must be adopted, in our view, in a way that is fair, transparent and doesn't deepen inequalities. Our approach is rooted in social partnership. Guidance, which has been developed with trade unions and public sector employees, puts worker voice, fair work and human oversight at the heart of workplace AI. We're drawing up a national AI governance framework to provide clear guardrails around accountability, transparency, fairness and risk, and we're still working out, as I said earlier, what the full impacts are on overall employment.

We recognise, though, that AI is changing the skills employers need, and the concerns that I referenced earlier in terms of entry-level roles and traditional routes into work. That's why we're working with employers, with trade unions, with education providers, first of all to understand how AI is changing recruitment, training and workplace learning, while investing, crucially, in digital and AI skills through personal learning accounts and our AI skills pilot.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r Aelod yn codi pwynt pwysig iawn. Yn ein barn ni, rhaid mabwysiadu deallusrwydd artiffisial mewn ffordd sy'n deg, yn dryloyw ac nad yw'n dyfnhau anghydraddoldebau. Mae ein dull o weithredu wedi'i wreiddio mewn partneriaeth gymdeithasol. Mae canllawiau, a ddatblygwyd gydag undebau llafur a gweithwyr y sector cyhoeddus, yn rhoi llais gweithwyr, gwaith teg a goruchwyliaeth ddynol wrth wraidd deallusrwydd artiffisial yn y gweithle. Rydym yn llunio fframwaith llywodraethu cenedlaethol ar gyfer deallusrwydd artiffisial i ddarparu canllawiau clir ynghylch atebolrwydd, tryloywder, tegwch a risg, ac rydym yn dal i ystyried, fel y dywedais yn gynharach, beth yw'r effeithiau llawn ar gyflogaeth yn gyffredinol.

Rydym yn cydnabod, fodd bynnag, fod deallusrwydd artiffisial yn newid y sgiliau sydd eu hangen ar gyflogwyr, a'r pryderon y cyfeiriais atynt yn gynharach o ran rolau lefel mynediad a llwybrau traddodiadol i mewn i waith. Dyna pam ein bod ni'n gweithio gyda chyflogwyr, gydag undebau llafur, gyda darparwyr addysg, yn gyntaf oll i ddeall sut y mae deallusrwydd artiffisial yn newid recriwtio, hyfforddiant a dysgu yn y gweithle, gan fuddsoddi ar yr un pryd, yn hollbwysig, mewn sgiliau digidol a deallusrwydd artiffisial trwy gyfrifon dysgu personol a'n cynllun peilot sgiliau deallusrwydd artiffisial.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: My priority is high standards and high aspirations for every learner. That is why this Government has worked at pace to develop the 'Foundational literacy and numeracy plan'. The plan sets out a clear and ambitious programme of action to raise literacy and numeracy outcomes throughout this Senedd term and is our first step in delivering sustained improvements in educational outcomes for all learners in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fy mlaenoriaeth yw safonau uchel a dyheadau uchel i bob dysgwr. Dyna pam y mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi gweithio'n gyflym i ddatblygu'r 'Cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol'. Mae'r cynllun yn nodi rhaglen weithredu glir ac uchelgeisiol i godi canlyniadau llythrennedd a rhifedd drwy gydol tymor y Senedd hon a dyma ein cam cyntaf tuag at gyflawni gwelliannau parhaus yng nghanlyniadau addysgol pob dysgwr yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that answer, Cabinet Minister, but there's a clear link also between attendance and educational outcomes, and we know we've got a huge attendance problem in Wales, with over 100,000 pupils every year missing at least 10 per cent of their lessons in the last year for which we have figures. In fact, the attendance records that have been provisionally published for 2025-26 suggest that this attendance problem is actually getting worse, not getting better. There's been a fall in the average attendance to just under 91 per cent in 2025-26. What action is your Welsh Government taking to address these appalling figures—which seem to be on the slide, not getting any better—and why is it that we have such a persistent attendance problem when other parts of the UK seem to be getting their act together and getting kids back into school?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am yr ateb hwnnw, Weinidog Cabinet, ond mae cysylltiad clir hefyd rhwng presenoldeb a chanlyniadau addysgol, ac rydym yn gwybod bod gennym broblem enfawr gyda phresenoldeb yng Nghymru, gyda dros 100,000 o ddisgyblion bob blwyddyn yn colli o leiaf 10 y cant o'u gwersi yn y flwyddyn ddiwethaf y mae gennym ffigurau ar ei chyfer. Mewn gwirionedd, mae'r cofnodion presenoldeb sydd wedi'u cyhoeddi dros dro ar gyfer 2025-26 yn awgrymu bod problem presenoldeb yn gwaethygu mewn gwirionedd, nid yn gwella. Bu gostyngiad yn y presenoldeb cyfartalog i ychydig o dan 91 y cant yn 2025-26. Pa gamau y mae eich Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i fynd i'r afael â'r ffigurau ofnadwy hyn—sy'n ymddangos fel pe baent yn llithro, nid yn gwella—a pham y mae gennym broblem presenoldeb mor barhaus pan fo'n ymddangos bod rhannau eraill o'r DU yn llwyddo i gael plant yn ôl i'r ysgol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It's because they have a Labour Government.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Am fod ganddynt Lywodraeth Lafur.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I think that's pushing it rather at this point, but thank you for the contribution.

Of course, this is an important area for us. There has been, you're quite right, a slight reduction on the latest figures, and there are a number of actions we are taking to tackle that. We are aware that school attendance has gone up again incrementally post COVID but is nowhere near the rate pre COVID. We're also aware that the cohort we are now targeting is likely to require a considerable focus and probably considerable support to push that figure higher. 

One of the things we have included in our literacy and numeracy foundational plan is targets on attendance. You will see a 0.5 per cent increase year on year to bring that level up. There's also a focus on persistent absence, which is missing 10 per cent or more of school sessions. A 2 per cent increase year on year is what we expect there.

There are a number of other areas we are focusing on. You will have heard me speak about the national framework on behaviour, attendance and well-being we are now bringing together, in the recognition that no single intervention, albeit we have targets now too, will address those persistent absence problems. They are often complex issues and do require tailored support, which is why we are looking at this framework in the round and making swift progress on introducing that.

Another thing we have done is to look in more detail—. Because often what we find is that reliable, consistent data across Wales is sometimes hard to find, so we've published new school attendance code guidance to give us that greater consistency in recording absence across Wales, to help us to target our work around this area to make a difference and to increase those figures over time. Because I agree with you: you need to be at school to benefit from the education system. It is very much a focus for us. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n credu bod hynny'n ymestyn pethau braidd ar y pwynt hwn, ond diolch am y cyfraniad.

Wrth gwrs, mae hwn yn faes pwysig i ni. Rydych chi'n hollol iawn, fe fu gostyngiad bach yn y ffigurau diweddaraf, ac mae nifer o gamau rydym yn eu cymryd i fynd i'r afael â hynny. Rydym yn ymwybodol fod presenoldeb ysgol wedi codi eto'n raddol ar ôl COVID ond nid yw'n agos at y gyfradd cyn COVID. Rydym hefyd yn ymwybodol fod y garfan rydym yn ei thargedu nawr yn debygol o fod angen ffocws sylweddol a chefnogaeth sylweddol yn ôl pob tebyg i wthio'r ffigur hwnnw'n uwch.

Un o'r pethau rydym wedi'u cynnwys yn ein cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol yw targedau ar bresenoldeb. Fe welwch gynnydd o 0.5 y cant o un flwyddyn i'r llall i godi'r lefel honno. Mae yna ffocws hefyd ar absenoldeb parhaus, sef colli 10 y cant neu fwy o sesiynau ysgol. Cynnydd o 2 y cant o un flwyddyn i'r llall yw'r hyn rydym yn ei ddisgwyl yno.

Mae yna nifer o feysydd eraill rydym canolbwyntio arnynt. Fe fyddwch wedi fy nghlywed yn siarad am y fframwaith cenedlaethol ar ymddygiad, presenoldeb a llesiant yr ydym bellach yn ei lunio, gan gydnabod na fydd unrhyw ymyrraeth unigol ynddi'i hun, er bod gennym dargedau nawr, yn datrys y problemau absenoldeb parhaus hynny. Maent yn aml yn faterion cymhleth ac mae angen cymorth wedi'i deilwra, a dyna pam ein bod ni'n edrych ar y fframwaith hwn yn ei gyfanrwydd ac yn gwneud cynnydd cyflym ar ei gyflwyno.

Peth arall a wnaethom yw edrych yn fwy manwl—. Oherwydd yn aml fe welwn fod data dibynadwy, cyson ledled Cymru weithiau'n anodd ei ganfod, felly rydym wedi cyhoeddi canllawiau newydd ar y cod presenoldeb ysgol i'w gwneud hi'n bosibl cofnodi absenoldeb yn fwy cyson ledled Cymru, i'n helpu i dargedu ein gwaith yn y maes hwn i wneud gwahaniaeth ac i gynyddu'r ffigurau hynny dros amser. Oherwydd rwy'n cytuno â chi: mae angen i chi fod yn yr ysgol i allu elwa o'r system addysg. Mae'n ffocws pwysig iawn i ni. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Can I start by declaring an interest? My wife works in an additional learning needs provision within a school in Conwy.

I thank the leader of the Welsh Conservatives for bringing this question forward. Minister, I was speaking to a teacher in Rhyl, and it was explained to me that the school in which that teacher worked can't afford pens or pencils, and staff are currently using their own money to buy learning resources. It's no surprise, then, that the Institute for Fiscal Studies has claimed that students in that local authority area are up to 23 months behind the national average. As we are seeing a shift towards greater school-level flexibility on learning approaches and a more interlinked learning approach, researchers from Cardiff University have warned that schools need significant investment in materials and learning resources to avoid the widening of educational outcome gaps between different parts of Wales. How can we expect teachers in my constituency to achieve the best outcomes for students when their schools can't even afford pens and pencils? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
A gaf i ddechrau trwy ddatgan buddiant? Mae fy ngwraig yn gweithio mewn darpariaeth anghenion dysgu ychwanegol mewn ysgol yng Nghonwy.

Diolch i arweinydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig am gyflwyno'r cwestiwn hwn. Weinidog, roeddwn i'n siarad ag athro yn y Rhyl, ac eglurwyd i mi nad yw'r ysgol lle roedd yr athro hwnnw'n gweithio yn gallu fforddio ysgrifbinnau na phensiliau, ac mae staff ar hyn o bryd yn defnyddio eu harian eu hunain i brynu adnoddau dysgu. Nid yw'n syndod, felly, fod y Sefydliad Astudiaethau Cyllidol wedi honni bod myfyrwyr yn ardal yr awdurdod lleol hwnnw hyd at 23 mis ar ei hôl hi o gymharu â'r cyfartaledd cenedlaethol. Wrth inni weld newid tuag at fwy o hyblygrwydd ar lefel ysgol ynghylch dulliau dysgu a dull dysgu mwy cydgysylltiedig, mae ymchwilwyr o Brifysgol Caerdydd wedi rhybuddio bod angen buddsoddiad sylweddol ar ysgolion mewn deunyddiau ac adnoddau dysgu er mwyn osgoi ehangu bylchau mewn canlyniadau addysgol rhwng gwahanol rannau o Gymru. Sut y gallwn ni ddisgwyl i athrawon yn fy etholaeth i gyflawni'r canlyniadau gorau i fyfyrwyr pan nad yw eu hysgolion yn gallu fforddio ysgrifbinnau a phensiliau hyd yn oed? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Obviously, funding for schools is a priority for us, which is why we were pleased last week, or was it the week before, that the supplementary budget did go through, with that £60 million earmarked for pressures in schools linked to ALN, but a recognition that schools and the education system is under pressure across Wales.

On the points you make about those flexibilities locally, I would refer you back again to the foundational literacy and numeracy plan, because that will show us, on a national and a local level, the direction we're going in. It will make it easier for us to align the support appropriately in different areas and different schools in Wales in order to make that progress. I've also announced an intention to conduct a targeted review of the curriculum to make sure that we can have a better understanding and provide better advice to schools about some of the areas we expect learners to have access to.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn amlwg, mae cyllid ar gyfer ysgolion yn flaenoriaeth i ni, a dyna pam ein bod ni'n falch yr wythnos diwethaf, neu'r wythnos flaenorol, fod y gyllideb atodol wedi mynd drwodd, gyda £60 miliwn wedi'i glustnodi ar gyfer pwysau mewn ysgolion sy'n gysylltiedig ag ADY, ond gan gydnabod bod ysgolion a'r system addysg dan bwysau ledled Cymru.

Ar y pwyntiau rydych chi'n eu gwneud am hyblygrwydd lleol, carwn eich cyfeirio'n ôl eto at y cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol, oherwydd bydd hwnnw'n dangos i ni, ar lefel genedlaethol a lleol, i ba gyfeiriad rydym ni'n mynd. Bydd yn ei gwneud hi'n haws inni alinio'r gefnogaeth yn briodol mewn gwahanol ardaloedd ac ysgolion gwahanol yng Nghymru er mwyn gwneud y cynnydd hwnnw. Rwyf hefyd wedi cyhoeddi bwriad i gynnal adolygiad wedi'i dargedu o'r cwricwlwm i wneud yn siŵr y gallwn gael gwell dealltwriaeth a rhoi gwell cyngor i ysgolion am rai o'r meysydd y disgwyliwn i ddysgwyr gael mynediad atynt.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Weinidog, rydym yn gwybod bod gweithlu addysg sy'n cael ei gefnogi a'i werthfawrogi yn hanfodol er mwyn codi safonau a gwella canlyniadau ein dysgwyr. Felly, rwy'n croesawu’r dyfarniad cyflog o 3.5 y cant, sydd wedi'i ariannu'n llawn ac yn sicrhau cydraddoldeb â Lloegr, yn ogystal â'r buddsoddiad ychwanegol rŷch chi newydd sôn amdano fe i leddfu'r pwysau sy'n gysylltiedig ag ADY. Mae ASCL Cymru, sydd hefyd yn cynrychioli arweinwyr ysgolion, wedi derbyn y dyfarniad cyflog o 3.5 y cant. A yw'r Gweinidog yn cytuno gyda fi ei bod hi er budd staff ysgolion a disgyblion fel ei gilydd i'r rheini sydd yn parhau mewn anghydfod i ymgysylltu'n adeiladol â'r cynigion hyn a cheisio dod o hyd i ddatrysiad heb weithredu diwydiannol? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Cabinet Minister, we know that an education workforce that is supported and valued is essential for raising standards and improving outcomes for our learners. Therefore, I welcome the 3.5 per cent pay award, which is fully funded and ensures parity with England, as well as the additional investment that you've just mentioned to alleviate pressures associated with ALN. ASCL Cymru, which also represents school leaders, has accepted the 3.5 per cent pay award. Does the Minister agree that it is in the interests of both school staff and pupils for those who remain in dispute to engage constructively with these proposals and seek to find a resolution without resorting to industrial action?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. Mae gweithio yn agos gyda'r gweithlu i sicrhau eu bod nhw'n cael eu talu a'u cefnogi yn ddigonol ar gyfer y gwaith pwysig maen nhw'n ei wneud yn flaenoriaeth greiddiol i fi. Rwy'n ddiolchgar iawn am y gwaith mae ASCL wedi ei wneud gyda ni, er enghraifft i symud ymlaen y ddadl ehangach ynglŷn ag ariannu ysgolion. Pan ddes i i fy swydd ym mis Mai, roedd yna drafodaethau manwl yn y cyfnod hwnnw er hwyluso cael yr un math o ddyfarniad o ran codiad cyflog i athrawon yng Nghymru o'i gymharu â Lloegr, ac roedd hwnna'n ofyn pendant gan yr undebau. 

Rwyf wastad yn agored i siarad gydag unrhyw un ar sut rŷm ni'n symud y ddadl yma ymlaen ynglŷn â chefnogaeth addas i'r gweithlu, ac rwy'n benodol yn frwd iawn i drafod baich gwaith a'r moddion y gallwn eu rhoi yn eu lle er lleihau y faich honno. Dwi'n gweld nad yw arweinydd yr wrthblaid yma heddiw. Dwi wedi cael sgyrsiau gyda hi, a phob athro neu athrawes rwyf wedi cwrdd â nhw ers 20 mlynedd, yn trafod, yn benodol, baich gwaith. Mae angen symud y ddadl honno yn ei blaen, ac rwy'n barod i siarad ag unrhyw un sydd â syniadau grymus er hwyluso'r drafodaeth honno. Mae'r drws bob amser yn agored.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much. Working closely with the workforce and ensuring that they are paid and supported adequately in the important work that they do is a core priority of mine. I'm very grateful for the work that ASCL has done with us, for example to move on the broader debate on school funding. When I came into my role in May, there were detailed discussions at that point in order to facilitate getting the same kind of pay award for teachers in Wales as compared to England, and that was a very firm ask from the unions.

I'm always open to speaking to anyone as to how we move this debate forward in terms of appropriate support for the workforce, and I'm particularly eager to discuss workload and what we can put in place in order to reduce that burden. I see that the leader of the opposition isn't here today. I've had conversations with her, and every teacher that I've met over a period of 20 years, discussing workload specifically. We need to move that debate forward, and I'm willing to speak to anyone who has forceful ideas as to how we can make that progress. My door is always open.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Addysg Bellach
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Further Education

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i wella'r ddarpariaeth addysg bellach yn Abertawe? OQ64724
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. What is the Welsh Government doing to improve further education provision in Swansea? OQ64724

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Dirprwy Weinidog Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for the question. We are investing more than £26 million through the Sustainable Communities for Learning programme to deliver modern, high-quality further education facilities across Swansea. This includes the refurbishment of Gower College Swansea’s Tycoch campus and the redevelopment of Ysgol Gyfun Gymraeg Bryn Tawe for both secondary and further education learners.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am y cwestiwn. Rydym yn buddsoddi mwy na £26 miliwn drwy'r rhaglen Cymunedau Dysgu Cynaliadwy i ddarparu cyfleusterau addysg bellach modern o ansawdd uchel ledled Abertawe. Mae hyn yn cynnwys adnewyddu campws Tŷ Coch Coleg Gŵyr Abertawe ac ailddatblygu Ysgol Gyfun Gymraeg Bryn Tawe ar gyfer dysgwyr addysg uwchradd ac addysg bellach.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Can I thank the Minister for that reply? Perhaps I ought to say that I used to be a governor at Tycoch and my grandchild goes to Bryn Tawe, so I've got an interest, though not necessarily a financial one. I thought I'd bring that up for the record.

One of the issues I think we are all in agreement on is that we do not want young people at 16 to become not in education, employment or training. That means we must have adequate availability of courses in the further education sector. If young people do not continue in education or training at 16, then many will face a life of unemployment. Getting them at 18 to go back into taking up a course is going to be very difficult.

Gower College Swansea is doing its best to provide opportunities. I really would like to commend them, and I hope the Minister will as well. Gower College has over-recruited against the numbers funded, but they still have a waiting list for some areas. Will the Minister commit to funding further education so that there is a place in college for every young person who wants it in Swansea, so that we don't have people sitting at home who want to be learning?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
A gaf i ddiolch i'r Gweinidog am yr ateb hwnnw? Efallai y dylwn ddweud fy mod i'n arfer bod yn llywodraethwr yn Nhŷ Coch ac mae fy ŵyr yn mynd i Fryn Tawe, felly mae gennyf fuddiant, er nad un ariannol o reidrwydd. Roeddwn i'n meddwl y dylwn godi hynny ar gyfer y cofnod.

Un o'r materion y credaf ein bod ni i gyd yn cytuno yn ei gylch yw nad ydym am i bobl ifanc 16 oed beidio â bod mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant. Mae hynny'n golygu bod rhaid inni gael digon o gyrsiau ar gael yn y sector addysg bellach. Os nad yw pobl ifanc yn parhau mewn addysg neu hyfforddiant yn 16 oed, bydd llawer yn wynebu bywyd o ddiweithdra. Mae eu cael i fynd yn ôl yn 18 oed i ddilyn cwrs yn mynd i fod yn anodd iawn.

Mae Coleg Gŵyr Abertawe yn gwneud ei orau i ddarparu cyfleoedd. Hoffwn eu canmol yn fawr, ac rwy'n gobeithio y bydd y Gweinidog yn gwneud hynny hefyd. Mae Coleg Gŵyr wedi gor-recriwtio yn erbyn y niferoedd a ariannwyd, ond mae'n dal i fod ganddynt restr aros ar gyfer rhai meysydd. A wnaiff y Gweinidog ymrwymo i ariannu addysg bellach er mwyn rhoi lle mewn coleg i bob unigolyn ifanc sydd ei eisiau yn Abertawe, fel nad oes gennym bobl yn eistedd gartref sydd eisiau dysgu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
There are two points there, Mike. The first one is around NEETs. This is an area of great concern for me and the Government. We know the NEET cohort in Wales is increasing. Roughly 17 per cent of the 16 to 24-year-old age group are NEET. That's clearly not where we want to be. We have to put interventions in place to stop them becoming NEET. That takes different approaches. The Alan Milburn report showed that about 70 per cent of those who are NEET are economically inactive—that is, they are not ready for work. That is because they have several barriers in their own personal lives that stop them becoming employable. That could be around mental health issues, it could be additional learning needs, it could be childcare, transport, disabilities, and so on. I am going to lead an inter-ministerial group of people to look at the NEETs agenda and how we can bring different policy areas to play, which would obviously involve health, social services, transport and so on. So, that's the first part.

The second part is ensuring that no young person will be turned away from the course that they want to study. I am increasingly aware of the significant increases in learner numbers in FE in recent years, and I recognise that that adds funding challenges to FE colleges. I am committed to reviewing that increased level of participation and the financial pressures over the next month, as we have final figures coming through. We will consider providing additional funding over and above what Medr have already provided, £6.25 million, should that money be available, given the budgetary constraints that we are under.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae dau bwynt yno, Mike. Mae'r un cyntaf yn ymwneud â phobl ifanc NEET. Mae hwn yn faes sy'n peri pryder mawr i mi a'r Llywodraeth. Rydym yn gwybod bod y garfan NEET yng Nghymru yn cynyddu. Mae tua 17 y cant o'r grŵp oedran 16 i 24 oed yn NEET. Yn amlwg, nid dyna lle rydym eisiau bod. Rhaid inni roi ymyriadau ar waith i'w hatal rhag dod yn NEET. Geilw hynny am wahanol ddulliau o weithredu. Dangosodd adroddiad Alan Milburn fod tua 70 y cant o'r rhai sy'n NEET yn economaidd anweithgar—hynny yw, nid ydynt yn barod ar gyfer gwaith. Mae hynny oherwydd bod ganddynt sawl rhwystr yn eu bywydau personol sy'n eu hatal rhag bod yn gyflogadwy. Efallai fod hynny'n ymwneud â materion iechyd meddwl, gallai fod yn anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, gallai fod yn ofal plant, trafnidiaeth, anableddau, ac yn y blaen. Rwy'n mynd i arwain grŵp rhyngweinidogol i edrych ar yr agenda NEET a sut y gallwn ddod â gwahanol feysydd polisi'n weithredol, a fyddai'n amlwg yn cynnwys iechyd, gwasanaethau cymdeithasol, trafnidiaeth ac yn y blaen. Felly, dyna'r rhan gyntaf.

Yr ail ran yw sicrhau na fydd unrhyw berson ifanc yn cael ei wrthod rhag dilyn y cwrs y maent am ei astudio. Rwy'n fwyfwy ymwybodol o'r cynnydd sylweddol yn niferoedd y dysgwyr mewn addysg bellach yn y blynyddoedd diwethaf, ac rwy'n cydnabod bod hynny'n ychwanegu heriau ariannu i golegau addysg bellach. Rwy'n ymrwymedig i adolygu'r lefel uwch honno o gyfranogiad a'r pwysau ariannol dros y mis nesaf, wrth i ffigurau terfynol ddod drwodd. Byddwn yn ystyried darparu cyllid ychwanegol yn ogystal â'r hyn y mae Medr eisoes wedi'i ddarparu, £6.25 miliwn, os bydd yr arian hwnnw ar gael, o ystyried y cyfyngiadau cyllidebol sydd arnom.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Mike, for the question. Improving further education in Swansea must mean providing the skills local industry needs. Employers need courses shaped around their businesses, reliable partnerships with colleges and practical help. For a small business, taking on an apprentice requires a financial and resource-heavy commitment. Announcing an audit does nothing on its own to meet these costs. Since your Government took office, another group of young people have left school hoping to secure an apprenticeship and employment. Employers need immediate funding. Your manifesto promises better use of existing city and regional growth deal funding to support apprenticeships. Your Government is happy to waste our money to fund international projects like tree planting in Uganda, but it seems Welsh employers are being left to shoulder apprenticeship costs. These are our young people, they are our future. What new funding has Plaid made available to help businesses, particularly smaller employers, take on apprentices?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich cwestiwn, Mike. Rhaid i wella addysg bellach yn Abertawe olygu darparu'r sgiliau sydd eu hangen ar ddiwydiant lleol. Mae angen cyrsiau ar gyflogwyr sydd wedi'u llunio o amgylch eu busnesau, partneriaethau dibynadwy â cholegau a chymorth ymarferol. I fusnes bach, mae cyflogi prentis yn golygu ymrwymiad ariannol a llawer o adnoddau. Nid yw cyhoeddi archwiliad yn gwneud unrhyw beth ynddo'i hun i dalu'r costau hyn. Ers i'ch Llywodraeth ddod i rym, mae grŵp arall o bobl ifanc wedi gadael ysgol gan obeithio sicrhau prentisiaeth a chyflogaeth. Mae angen cyllid ar gyflogwyr ar unwaith. Mae eich maniffesto yn addo gwell defnydd o gyllid bargeinion dinesig a thwf sy'n bodoli'n barod i gefnogi prentisiaethau. Mae eich Llywodraeth yn fwy na pharod i wastraffu ein harian i ariannu prosiectau rhyngwladol fel plannu coed yn Uganda, ond ymddengys bod cyflogwyr Cymru’n cael eu gadael i ysgwyddo costau prentisiaethau. Ein pobl ifanc ni yw'r rhain, nhw yw ein dyfodol. Pa gyllid newydd y mae Plaid Cymru wedi'i ddarparu i helpu busnesau, yn enwedig cyflogwyr llai o faint, i gyflogi prentisiaid?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'll deal with the main and the most important parts of that question, if I may. If I can refer back to a skills summit we organised on 8 October in the Swansea.com Stadium, for the first time ever we brought employers, small and medium-sized and large companies together with education providers. It was a hugely successful event, where employers were telling us that they need to forge a better relationship with apprenticeship providers and vocational skills providers. Employers know what the emerging sectors are. They know what skills they need for the future. So, we need to develop a mechanism where they are telling providers what they need and that we match them both together.

Now, I heard my colleague the Minister for enterprise explain earlier on that we need to create more demand as well. And you heard him explain how we are going to do that through setting up a Welsh development agency and other programmes as well to support industry and SMEs to take on more apprenticeships. I believe that apprenticeships are a great pathway into work and into further and higher education as well. You can earn and learn at the same time. So, we are committed to supporting the apprenticeship scheme, and we will be working with employers to make sure that what they need, in terms of the skills level, matches what education providers can put on in FE colleges, universities and also through apprenticeship schemes.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe ddeliaf â phrif rannau pwysicaf y cwestiwn hwnnw, os caf. Os caf gyfeirio'n ôl at uwchgynhadledd sgiliau a drefnwyd gennym ar 8 Hydref yn Stadiwm Swansea.com, am y tro cyntaf erioed, daethom â chyflogwyr, cwmnïau bach a chanolig a chwmnïau mawr ynghyd â darparwyr addysg. Roedd yn ddigwyddiad hynod lwyddiannus, lle dywedodd cyflogwyr wrthym fod angen iddynt feithrin perthynas well â darparwyr prentisiaethau a darparwyr sgiliau galwedigaethol. Mae cyflogwyr yn gwybod beth yw'r sectorau datblygol. Maent yn gwybod pa sgiliau sydd eu hangen arnynt ar gyfer y dyfodol. Felly, mae angen inni ddatblygu mecanwaith lle maent yn dweud wrth ddarparwyr beth sydd ei angen arnynt a'n bod yn eu paru gyda'i gilydd.

Nawr, clywais fy nghyd-Aelod, y Gweinidog dros fenter, yn esbonio yn gynharach fod angen inni greu mwy o alw hefyd. Ac fe'i clywsoch yn esbonio sut y gwnawn hynny drwy sefydlu awdurdod datblygu Cymru a rhaglenni eraill hefyd i gefnogi diwydiant a busnesau bach a chanolig i gyflogi mwy o brentisiaid. Rwy'n credu bod prentisiaethau yn llwybr gwych i mewn i waith ac i addysg bellach ac addysg uwch hefyd. Gallwch ennill arian a dysgu ar yr un pryd. Felly, rydym wedi ymrwymo i gefnogi'r cynllun prentisiaethau, a byddwn yn gweithio gyda chyflogwyr i sicrhau bod yr hyn sydd ei angen arnynt, o ran y lefel sgiliau, yn cyfateb i'r hyn y gall darparwyr addysg ei gynnig mewn colegau addysg bellach, prifysgolion a hefyd drwy gynlluniau prentisiaeth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minister. Reform UK spokesperson, Stephen Senior.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. Cabinet Minister, additional learning needs funding remains a contentious issue, with a debate scheduled next month in response to a petition. ALN funding by the Welsh Government is up 14 per cent on last year, and has more than doubled in eight years. Inflation over that period has been around 35 per cent. The percentage of the education budget assigned to ALN has risen from just below 15 per cent to nearly 19 per cent over the same period. At local authority level, there have been huge variations, with increases over the last decade ranging from 65 per cent to 297 per cent. One authority now spends more than a quarter of its education budget on ALN. These figures suggest that there has been a rapid change within Welsh education. Whatever is happening looks unsustainable in terms of funding. Minister, what are your thoughts on the reasons for this ALN spending trajectory?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Weinidog Cabinet, mae cyllid anghenion dysgu ychwanegol yn parhau i fod yn fater dadleuol, gyda dadl wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer y mis nesaf mewn ymateb i ddeiseb. Mae cyllid ADY gan Lywodraeth Cymru 14 y cant yn uwch o gymharu â'r llynedd, ac mae wedi mwy na dyblu mewn wyth mlynedd. Mae chwyddiant dros y cyfnod hwnnw wedi bod oddeutu 35 y cant. Mae canran y gyllideb addysg a neilltuwyd i ADY wedi codi o ychydig o dan 15 y cant i bron i 19 y cant dros yr un cyfnod. Ar lefel awdurdodau lleol, bu amrywiadau enfawr, gyda chynnydd dros y degawd diwethaf yn amrywio o 65 y cant i 297 y cant. Mae un awdurdod bellach yn gwario mwy na chwarter ei gyllideb addysg ar ADY. Mae'r ffigurau hyn yn awgrymu bod newid cyflym wedi bod mewn addysg yng Nghymru. Mae beth bynnag sy'n digwydd yn edrych yn anghynaliadwy o ran cyllid. Weinidog, beth yw eich barn chi am y rhesymau dros y trywydd gwariant hwn mewn perthynas ag ADY?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. Thank you for the question. I think we are dealing with two issues simultaneously here. I mentioned earlier on that I was pleased that £60 million had gone into the system this year, as a result of the supplementary budget, to support with immediate pressures. But you are quite right, in the longer term we need to arrive at a system that is more sustainable and is inclusive of the learners in Wales. I think every jurisdiction everywhere over a time, and particularly post COVID, has been dealing with increasingly complex demand from children and families trying to negotiate a range of issues that their learners are facing.

The education system, arguably, experiences changes in society faster than most of us sitting here and probably most of our services as well. So, we have made an effort now to focus on the sustainability of the ALN system over time. You will have seen that a proportion of what was agreed last week has been allocated specifically for that purpose, and we will work now quickly with local authorities and other partners to work our way to a more sustainable system over time. We need this to be a coherent continuum, we need it to be of high quality, we need it to be inclusive, with—and this is the crucial part I think—clearer national expectations of what this system should look like, stronger mainstream capacity, which in turn comes with demand for support, obviously.

One of the first steps is to understand in detail, with all our partners, what an inclusive system looks like and plot our way from here to that system and this commitment—. There is a great willingness amongst all our partners to work on this and we will do so with speed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr am eich cwestiwn. Rwy'n credu ein bod yn delio â dau fater ar yr un pryd yma. Soniais yn gynharach fy mod yn falch fod £60 miliwn wedi mynd i mewn i'r system eleni, o ganlyniad i'r gyllideb atodol, i gynorthwyo gyda phwysau uniongyrchol. Ond rydych chi'n llygad eich lle fod angen inni weithio yn y tymor hwy tuag at system sy'n fwy cynaliadwy ac sy'n gynhwysol i ddysgwyr yng Nghymru. Rwy'n credu bod pob awdurdodaeth ym mhobman wedi bod yn delio ers peth amser, ac yn enwedig ar ôl COVID, â galw mwy a mwy cymhleth gan blant a theuluoedd sy'n ceisio delio ag ystod o faterion y mae eu dysgwyr yn eu hwynebu.

Gellid dadlau bod y system addysg yn profi newidiadau yn y gymdeithas yn gyflymach na'r rhan fwyaf ohonom sy'n eistedd yma a'r rhan fwyaf o'n gwasanaethau hefyd yn ôl pob tebyg. Felly, rydym wedi gwneud ymdrech nawr i ganolbwyntio ar gynaliadwyedd y system ADY dros amser. Byddwch wedi gweld bod cyfran o'r hyn a gytunwyd yr wythnos diwethaf wedi'i ddyrannu'n benodol at y diben hwnnw, a byddwn yn gweithio'n gyflym nawr gydag awdurdodau lleol a phartneriaid eraill i weithio tuag at system fwy cynaliadwy dros amser. Mae angen i hyn fod yn gontinwwm cydlynol, mae angen iddo fod o ansawdd uchel, mae angen iddo fod yn gynhwysol, gyda—a dyma'r rhan allweddol, yn fy marn i—disgwyliadau cenedlaethol cliriach o sut y dylai'r system hon edrych, capasiti cryfach i addysg brif ffrwd, sydd yn ei dro yn cynyddu'r galw am gymorth, yn amlwg.

Un o'r camau cyntaf yw deall yn fanwl, gyda'n holl bartneriaid, sut olwg sydd ar system gynhwysol a chynllunio ein ffordd o fan hyn tuag at y system honno a'r ymrwymiad hwn. Mae llawer o barodrwydd ymhlith ein holl bartneriaid i weithio ar hyn, a byddwn yn gwneud hynny'n gyflym.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Okay, thank you, Minister. I see that later on there's a question regarding teachers leaving the profession. Surveys show that poor pupil behaviour is a factor. However, Plaid's recent programme for government, whilst acknowledging workload concerns, makes no mention of behaviour.

Staff working in schools have a legal right to use reasonable force to control or restrain pupils. Welsh Government guidance explicitly states that no school should have a 'no physical contact' policy. However, there are still occasions when school staff face lengthy investigations and possible suspension for having operated within the law. This can have a devastating impact on both them and pupil behaviour in the school, whenever staff, unsurprisingly, decide that no physical intervention is their best policy.

Minister, will you ask your officials to establish whether schools are advising staff on their legal right to use reasonable force and whether disciplinary processes are being initiated despite staff having operated within the law?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Iawn, diolch, Weinidog. Rwy'n gweld bod cwestiwn yn nes ymlaen ynglŷn ag athrawon yn gadael y proffesiwn. Mae arolygon yn dangos bod ymddygiad gwael gan ddisgyblion yn ffactor. Fodd bynnag, er bod rhaglen lywodraethu ddiweddar Plaid Cymru yn cydnabod pryderon ynghylch llwyth gwaith, nid yw'n sôn am ymddygiad.

Mae gan staff sy'n gweithio mewn ysgolion hawl gyfreithiol i ddefnyddio grym rhesymol i reoli neu ffrwyno disgyblion. Mae canllawiau Llywodraeth Cymru yn nodi'n benodol na ddylai fod gan unrhyw ysgol bolisi 'dim cyswllt corfforol'. Fodd bynnag, mae achosion o hyd o staff ysgolion yn wynebu ymchwiliadau hirfaith a gwaharddiadau posibl am weithredu o fewn y gyfraith. Gall hyn gael effaith ddinistriol arnynt hwy ac ar ymddygiad disgyblion yn yr ysgol, pryd bynnag y bydd staff, heb fawr o syndod, yn penderfynu mai dim ymyrraeth gorfforol yw eu polisi gorau.

Weinidog, a wnewch chi ofyn i'ch swyddogion sefydlu a yw ysgolion yn cynghori staff ar eu hawl gyfreithiol i ddefnyddio grym rhesymol ac a yw prosesau disgyblu'n cael eu cychwyn er bod staff wedi gweithredu o fewn y gyfraith?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
It is obviously important that staff feel safe at school and are able to operate appropriately. It is clear that staff may use reasonable force where necessary to prevent harm, an offence, damage to property or serious disruption, but that intervention must necessarily, and I think we'd all agree on this, be proportionate and use the minimum force required. And it should never be used as a punishment. I think we can all agree on those principles. If there are examples, individual examples, that you have, then I would be glad to look at them.

But we are clear that that is the environment in which our workforce is working. It is also our expectation that restrictive practices are a last resort. And to go back to your first point around behaviour, the behaviour and well-being framework is a priority for this Government, and bringing together a greater national consistency around our expectations and around the support that will help the workforce and the learners in turn is a piece of work that is ongoing.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'n amlwg yn bwysig fod staff yn teimlo'n ddiogel yn yr ysgol ac yn gallu gweithredu'n briodol. Mae'n glir y gall staff ddefnyddio grym rhesymol lle bo angen i atal niwed, trosedd, difrod i eiddo neu darfu difrifol, ond mae'n rhaid i'r ymyrraeth honno, a chredaf y byddai pob un ohonom yn cytuno ar hyn, fod yn gymesur a defnyddio'r grym lleiaf sydd ei angen. Ac ni ddylid byth ei defnyddio fel cosb. Rwy'n credu y gall pob un ohonom gytuno ar yr egwyddorion hynny. Os oes gennych enghreifftiau, enghreifftiau unigol, yna buaswn yn falch o edrych arnynt.

Ond rydym yn glir mai dyna'r amgylchedd y mae ein gweithlu'n gweithio ynddo. Rydym hefyd yn disgwyl mai'r dewis olaf yw arferion cyfyngol. Ac i fynd yn ôl at eich pwynt cyntaf ynghylch ymddygiad, mae'r fframwaith ymddygiad a lles yn flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth hon, ac mae cywain mwy o gysondeb cenedlaethol ynghylch ein disgwyliadau ac ynghylch y cymorth a fydd yn helpu'r gweithlu a'r dysgwyr yn eu tro yn waith sy'n parhau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Okay, thank you, Minister. Finally, the national literacy and numeracy assessments are online and personalised to each pupil. So, they're rather like a flow chart, where the next question depends on the answers to the last one. These tests can be taken whenever the school feels it's appropriate. Pupils can take time out during the assessments, and pupils are permitted to repeat the exercise any time. This is not a standardised test where all pupils in a cohort take the same test at the same time of the year so that judgments can be made about pupil and school standards, including progress.

This is what the tests were originally designed to do when Leighton Andrews introduced them, and that is what happened when the tests were introduced in 2014. This adaptive system, as it's called, has been in place for a decade, but has clearly not led to any improvements in the Programme for International Student Assessment results. Minister, will you reintroduce standardised literacy and numeracy tests to be used by all pupils annually at the end of year 2 to year 9?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Iawn, diolch, Weinidog. Yn olaf, mae'r asesiadau llythrennedd a rhifedd cenedlaethol ar waith ac wedi'u personoli i bob disgybl. Felly, maent yn debyg i siart lif, lle mae'r cwestiwn nesaf yn dibynnu ar yr atebion i'r un diwethaf. Gellir sefyll y profion hyn pryd bynnag y mae'r ysgol yn teimlo ei bod yn briodol. Gall disgyblion gymryd seibiant yn ystod yr asesiadau, a chaniateir i ddisgyblion ailadrodd yr ymarfer unrhyw bryd. Nid prawf safonol yw hwn lle mae pob disgybl mewn carfan yn sefyll yr un prawf ar yr un adeg o'r flwyddyn fel y gellir asesu safonau disgyblion ac ysgolion, gan gynnwys cynnydd.

Dyma y cynlluniwyd y profion i'w wneud yn wreiddiol pan gawsant eu cyflwyno gan Leighton Andrews, a dyna a ddigwyddodd pan gyflwynwyd y profion yn 2014. Mae'r system ymaddasol hon, fel y'i gelwir, wedi bod ar waith ers degawd, ond yn amlwg, nid yw wedi arwain at unrhyw welliannau yng nghanlyniadau'r Rhaglen Ryngwladol Asesu Myfyrwyr. Weinidog, a wnewch chi ailgyflwyno profion llythrennedd a rhifedd safonol i'w defnyddio gan bob disgybl yn flynyddol ar ddiwedd blwyddyn 2 i flwyddyn 9?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. These are adaptive tests. The idea is that the learner engages with them, and it helps to indicate what the next steps in their development should be. That's how they've been constructed to operate.

We can use the data more broadly that this system gives us, to give us an indicator at year 6, which is what we're doing as part of this plan, and which gives us a place go to, then, as a national trajectory of improvement, and also to make sure that we can align the support available appropriately for those schools and for those learners. 

I'm not going to go back to the future. I am, however, going to have, during this Senedd term, a clearer expectation that we can communicate effectively to learners and to schools.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Mae'r rhain yn brofion ymaddasol. Y syniad yw bod y dysgwr yn ymgysylltu â nhw, ac mae hynny'n helpu i nodi beth ddylai'r camau nesaf yn eu datblygiad fod. Dyna sut y cawsant eu llunio i weithredu.

Gallwn ddefnyddio'r data y mae'r system hon yn ei roi i ni yn ehangach, i roi dangosydd i ni ym mlwyddyn 6, sef yr hyn a wnawn yn rhan o'r cynllun hwn, ac sy'n rhoi lle i ni fynd, felly, fel trywydd gwelliant cenedlaethol, ac i sicrhau y gallwn alinio'r cymorth sydd ar gael yn briodol ar gyfer yr ysgolion a'r dysgwyr hynny.

Nid wyf am fynd yn ôl i'r dyfodol. Fodd bynnag, yn ystod tymor y Senedd hon, bydd gennyf ddisgwyliad cliriach y gallwn ei gyfathrebu'n effeithiol i ddysgwyr ac ysgolion.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Lynne Neagle.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Labour spokesperson, Lynne Neagle.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. Last week, as we've heard from Sera Evans, you announced a teacher pay award of 3.5 per cent following the consultation on the independent Welsh pay review body report. That announcement was made during an active industrial dispute, and the National Association of Head Teachers have now withdrawn from talks with the Government and announced that they are moving to a statutory industrial ballot. 

Why did you make that announcement while talks were ongoing, and do you think that is in keeping with the principles of social partnership?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Yr wythnos diwethaf, fel y clywsom gan Sera Evans, fe gyhoeddoch chi godiad cyflog o 3.5 y cant i athrawon yn dilyn yr ymgynghoriad ar adroddiad corff adolygu cyflogau annibynnol Cymru. Gwnaed y cyhoeddiad hwnnw yn ystod anghydfod diwydiannol gweithredol, ac mae Cymdeithas Genedlaethol y Prifathrawon bellach wedi tynnu'n ôl o drafodaethau gyda'r Llywodraeth ac wedi cyhoeddi y byddant yn cynnal pleidlais ddiwydiannol statudol.

Pam y gwnaethoch chi'r cyhoeddiad hwnnw tra bod y trafodaethau’n mynd rhagddynt, ac a ydych chi'n credu bod hynny’n gydnaws ag egwyddorion partneriaeth gymdeithasol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. I think, as I said in my earlier answer, I remain committed to the social partnership, and I'm always willing to talk to those social partners on issues that we have in common as concerns. 

I announced that fully funded pay award last week, following that consultation, because I wanted to respect the principle of no detriment, so that there'd be no difference between the pay increases here and those over the border in England. I know this has been a continuing debate over many years, to ensure that we remain in that alignment.

I think the previous education Minister will also be aware of the financial environment, and the budgetary environment we are now in, and I judged, at this point, that 4.25 per cent was not affordable when we consider the other priorities of this Government, and Wales more broadly, around, particularly, health service demand—the national health service—and other priorities that this Government is committed to.

The 3.5 per cent was important to me. It was important to most partners. But I remain committed to talking to anybody who wishes to examine areas of mutual interest and concern.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Fel y dywedais yn fy ateb cynharach, rwy'n parhau i fod yn ymrwymedig i'r bartneriaeth gymdeithasol, ac rwyf bob amser yn barod i siarad â'r partneriaid cymdeithasol hynny ar faterion sydd gennym yn gyffredin.

Cyhoeddais y dyfarniad cyflog wedi'i ariannu'n llawn yr wythnos diwethaf, yn dilyn yr ymgynghoriad hwnnw, am fy mod i eisiau parchu egwyddor dim niwed, fel na fyddai unrhyw wahaniaeth rhwng y codiadau cyflog yma a'r rhai dros y ffin yn Lloegr. Gwn fod hon wedi bod yn ddadl barhaus ers blynyddoedd, er mwyn sicrhau ein bod yn parhau i fod wedi ein halinio.

Rwy'n credu y bydd y Gweinidog addysg blaenorol hefyd yn ymwybodol o'r amgylchedd ariannol, a'r amgylchedd cyllidebol rydym ynddo nawr, a bernais, ar hyn o bryd, nad oedd 4.25 y cant yn fforddiadwy pan ystyriwn flaenoriaethau eraill y Llywodraeth hon, a Chymru yn ehangach, ynghylch y galw, yn benodol, ar y gwasanaeth iechyd—y gwasanaeth iechyd gwladol—a blaenoriaethau eraill y mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi ymrwymo iddynt.

Roedd y ffigur o 3.5 y cant yn bwysig i mi. Roedd yn bwysig i'r rhan fwyaf o bartneriaid. Ond rwy'n parhau i fod wedi ymrwymo i siarad ag unrhyw un sy'n dymuno archwilio meysydd o ddiddordeb a phryder cyffredin.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, thank you for that answer, and I'm fully in support of no detriment myself. And I do understand the financial constraints, but would point out that the Government still has a significant amount of unallocated resource as a result of the consequentials that were received by the UK Government. 

So, since May, we've had an industrial dispute with the Association of School and College Leaders, an escalating dispute with the National Association of Head Teachers, and the National Education Union have previously gone out to indicative ballot. I hear what you're saying about being willing to talk to partners, but it doesn't seem to me like those talks are going as well as we would want them to go, really. So, in light of that, what are you going to do to get social partnership with the education trade unions back on line?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, diolch am eich ateb, ac rwy'n llwyr gefnogi'r egwyddor dim niwed fy hun. Ac rwy'n deall y cyfyngiadau ariannol, ond hoffwn nodi bod gan y Llywodraeth lawer iawn o arian heb ei ddyrannu o hyd o ganlyniad i'r cyllid canlyniadol a ddaeth i law gan Lywodraeth y DU.

Felly, ers mis Mai, rydym wedi cael anghydfod diwydiannol gyda'r Gymdeithas Arweinwyr Ysgolion a Cholegau, anghydfod sy'n dwysáu gyda Chymdeithas Genedlaethol y Prifathrawon, ac mae'r Undeb Addysg Cenedlaethol wedi cynnal pleidlais ddangosol yn y gorffennol. Rwy'n clywed yr hyn a ddywedwch am fod yn barod i siarad â phartneriaid, ond nid yw'n ymddangos i mi fod y sgyrsiau hynny'n mynd cystal ag y byddem eisiau iddynt fynd mewn gwirionedd. Felly, yng ngoleuni hynny, beth ydych chi'n mynd i'w wneud i adfer y bartneriaeth gymdeithasol gyda'r undebau addysg?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I think that the judgment on where each of these parties is depends, rather, on who you talk to at this point. I think we have, for example, had very helpful and fruitful discussions with ASCL, in particular, around some of these elements. 

The social partnership—I've been part of arrangements like this for many years—is very important to me. And it is a place where some of these pressing issues that the workforce has been calling for action on for many, many years—. It is a good place to resolve them, particularly on ALN, particularly on workload, recruitment, retention, behaviour, attendance—all these things that are very important to everybody who works in our schools and has an association with them. 

All of those issues, I am entirely open to engaging on them. But I would repeat my first point around the salary increases—the pay increases—that 3.5 per cent was as far as I felt able to go. But I am and remain committed to discussing any and all other issues.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n credu bod y farn ynglŷn â ble mae pob un o'r partïon hyn yn dibynnu i raddau ar bwy rydych yn siarad â nhw ar hyn o bryd. Rwy'n credu er enghraifft ein bod wedi cael trafodaethau defnyddiol a ffrwythlon iawn gyda'r Gymdeithas Arweinwyr Ysgolion a Cholegau, yn enwedig, ynglŷn â rhai o'r elfennau hyn.

Mae'r bartneriaeth gymdeithasol—rwyf wedi bod yn rhan o drefniadau fel hyn ers blynyddoedd lawer—yn bwysig iawn i mi. Ac mae'n fan lle mae rhai o'r materion dybryd hyn y mae'r gweithlu wedi bod yn galw am weithredu arnynt ers blynyddoedd lawer—. Mae'n lle da i'w datrys, yn enwedig o ran ADY, yn enwedig o ran llwyth gwaith, recriwtio, cadw staff, ymddygiad, presenoldeb—yr holl bethau hyn sy'n bwysig iawn i bawb sy'n gweithio yn ein hysgolion ac sydd â chysylltiad â nhw.

Rwy’n gwbl agored i ymgysylltu ar bob un o'r materion hynny. Ond rwyf am ailadrodd fy mhwynt cyntaf ynglŷn â'r codiadau tâl—y codiadau cyflog—mai 3.5 y cant oedd yr uchaf y teimlwn y gallwn fynd. Ond rwyf wedi ymrwymo ac yn parhau i fod wedi ymrwymo i drafod unrhyw faterion eraill.
