XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Paul Davies.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh Conservatives' spokesperson, Paul Davies.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Cyn i mi ofyn fy nghwestiynau, hoffwn gofnodi fy niolch i Efa Gruffudd Jones am ei gwaith fel Comisiynydd y Gymraeg. Mae hi wedi bod yn eiriolwr cadarn dros yr iaith Gymraeg, a dwi'n dymuno'n dda iddi ar gyfer y dyfodol.

Weinidog, mae adroddiad y Comisiwn Cymunedau Cymraeg, 'Cyrraedd pob cymuned, cryfhau'r Gymraeg', yn nodi y dylid ystyried gweithleoedd yn fannau allweddol ar gyfer defnyddio'r Gymraeg, ac mae'r adroddiad yn gwneud cyfres o argymhellion sydd â'r nod o gynyddu'r defnydd o'r Gymraeg yn y mannau yma. Pa gynnydd y mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi ei wneud o ran gweithredu'r argymhellion hynny, a pha dystiolaeth sydd gyda chi fod mwy o bobl yn defnyddio'r Gymraeg yn rheolaidd yn eu gweithleoedd o ganlyniad i hynny?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you, Dirprwy Lywydd. Before I ask my questions, I would like to put on record my thanks to Efa Gruffudd Jones for her work as Welsh Language Commissioner. She's been a robust advocate for the Welsh language, and I wish her well for the future.

Minister, the report of the Commission for Welsh-speaking Communities, 'Cymraeg in every community, strengthening the Welsh language', notes that workplaces should be considered as key locations for use of the Welsh language, and the report makes a series of recommendations with the aim of increasing the use of the Welsh language in those settings. What progress has the Welsh Government made in terms of implementing those recommendations, and what evidence do you have that more people are using the Welsh language regularly in their workplaces as a result of that?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr am y cwestiwn. Hoffwn i ategu fy niolch innau hefyd i Gomisiynydd y Gymraeg am ei gwaith hithau.

Mi fyddwn ni, ym mis Rhagfyr, yn cyhoeddi ymgynghoriad ar strategaeth y Gymraeg, Deddf y Gymraeg ac Addysg (Cymru) 2025, a'r cod ar y gallu i siarad Cymraeg. Byddwn i'n gofyn i chi edrych ar y pwynt hwnnw ar yr hyn rŷn ni'n ei gyhoeddi achos byddwn ni'n dangos y taflwybr i sicrhau bod defnydd o'r Gymraeg, mynediad at y Gymraeg, Cymraeg yn ein cadarnleoedd, Cymraeg yn ein hysgolion ni, yn clymu at ei gilydd i un strategaeth gydlynus, yn seiliedig ar y cysyniad bod y Gymraeg yn perthyn i ni i gyd. Yn y cyd-destun hwnnw, byddwn ni'n dangos siẁd rydyn ni'n mynd i gyrraedd y nodau priodol o ran y cyfleoedd hyn, gan gynnwys y gweithle. Mi fydd yna fanylder yn dangos y ffordd ymlaen, yn cynnwys, felly, dargedau mwy penodol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much for the question. I would like to add my thanks as well to the Welsh Language Commissioner for her work.

We will, in December, be publishing a consultation on the Welsh language strategy, the Welsh Language and Education (Wales) Act 2025, and the Welsh language proficiency code. I would ask you to look at that point at what we will publish, because we will indicate what the trajectory is to ensure that the use of the Welsh language, access to the Welsh language, the Welsh language in our heartlands, the Welsh language in our schools, all tie together under one co-ordinated strategy that will be based on the concept that the Welsh language belongs to us all. In that context, we will show how we will reach those particular goals in terms of those opportunities, including the workplace. There will be detail showing that trajectory, including, therefore, more specific targets.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Dwi'n diolch i chi am yr ymateb yna. Dwi'n edrych ymlaen i'r cyhoeddiad hynny ym mis Rhagfyr.

Nawr, daeth y comisiwn i'r casgliad hefyd nad yw'r gyllideb bresennol ar gyfer cryfhau'r Gymraeg ar lefel gymunedol yn ddigonol, a thynnodd sylw at yr angen am fwy o gefnogaeth i helpu sefydliadau i ddatblygu gweithleoedd lle siaredir y Gymraeg. Galwodd hefyd am adolygiad o'r modd y gellir defnyddio cyllid cyhoeddus a mecanweithiau cymorth i hyrwyddo nodau 'Cymraeg 2050'. Yn sgil hynny, a allwch chi ddweud wrthym ni ba gyllid sydd ar gael ar hyn o bryd i gefnogi defnyddio'r Gymraeg mewn gweithleoedd ledled Cymru, ac a allwch chi ddweud a ydych chi'n credu bod y lefel bresennol o fuddsoddiad yn ddigonol i gyflawni'r newidiadau diwylliannol a sefydliadol y mae'r comisiwn yn eu rhagweld yn ei adroddiad?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I thank you for that response. I look forward to seeing that publication in December.

Now, the commission also came to the conclusion that the current budget for strengthening the Welsh language at community level was not sufficient, and it highlighted the need for greater support to help organisations to develop workplaces where the Welsh language is spoken. It also called for a review of the way in which public funding and support mechanisms can be used to support the aims of 'Cymraeg 2050'. In light of that, can you tell us what funding is currently available to support the use of the Welsh language in workplaces across Wales, and can you tell us whether you think that the current level of investment is adequate to deliver the cultural shifts that the commission anticipates in its report?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Efallai y bydd angen i fi ysgrifennu atoch chi gyda manylder y cwestiwn cyntaf. Ond ar yr hyn a fydd yn ofynnol er mwyn gwireddu'r uchelgais yn y strategaeth y byddwn ni yn ei chyhoeddi—byddwn ni'n cyhoeddi ar gyfer ymgynghoriad ym mis Rhagfyr, i mewn i'r flwyddyn nesaf—fel rhan o hynny, er mwyn ei chyflawni hi, mi fyddwn ni'n edrych ar yr hyn sydd ei angen o ran adnoddau i'w gwireddu hi. Bydd y ddau beth yn mynd law yn llaw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Perhaps I'll have to write to you with the detailed response to that first question. But on what will be needed in order to realise the ambition in the strategy that we will publish—it will be published for consultation in December, into next year—as part of that, in order to deliver that, we will be looking at what's needed in terms of resources to deliver it. Both things will go hand in hand.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae cwestiwn 3 [OQ64738] gan Vikki Howells. Yn anffodus, mae'r Aelod wedi'i hoedi ar y ffordd nôl o ddigwyddiad yn Aberfan, felly symudaf ymlaen i gwestiwn 4, Anna Nicholl.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Question 3 [OQ64738] is from Vikki Howells. Unfortunately, the Member has been delayed on her way back from an event at Aberfan, so I'll move on to question 4, Anna Nicholl.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Sut mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn sicrhau bod cymunedau'n cael eu cynnwys mewn penderfyniadau ynghylch dyfodol ysgolion a gynhelir gan yr Eglwys yng Nghymru yng Ngheredigion Penfro? OQ64786
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. How is the Cabinet Minister ensuring community involvement in decisions about the future of Church in Wales maintained schools in Ceredigion Penfro? OQ64786

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Awdurdodau lleol sy'n gyfrifol am benderfyniadau ynghylch dyfodol ysgolion, ac mae'n rhaid iddyn nhw ddilyn gweithdrefnau statudol wrth gyflwyno cynigion. Mae hyn yn cynnwys ymgynghori â chymunedau, darparu digon o wybodaeth i bobl allu dod i farn ddeallus, ymgysylltu â phartneriaid perthnasol, gan gynnwys cyrff crefyddol, a rhoi sylw i ddymuniadau rhieni.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. Local authorities are responsible for decisions on the future of schools, and they must follow statutory procedures when bringing forward proposals. This includes consulting communities, providing sufficient information to enable people to come to informed views, engaging with relevant partners, including religious bodies, and having regard to the wishes of parents.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Cabinet Minister. I'm concerned about the low level of confidence that parents, staff and governors in Pembrokeshire have told me that they have in the council involving them meaningfully in big decisions about the future of their schools. Examples include but are not limited to church schools. I wrote to the council back in September around decisions on the future of Cilgerran school, and I'm glad this is now resolved. But, Cabinet Minister, public trust and confidence is easily lost. As Pembrokeshire County Council now consults on proposals to close Tenby Church in Wales VC Primary School and neighbouring Greenhill school, replacing them with a new three-to-19 community school, can the Cabinet Minister assure us that she expects these decisions to be based on the meaningful involvement of parents and the wider community, including open and transparent information on all options available?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Rwy'n pryderu am y lefel isel o hyder y mae rhieni, staff a llywodraethwyr yn sir Benfro wedi dweud wrthyf sydd ganddynt y bydd y cyngor yn eu cynnwys mewn ffordd ystyrlon mewn penderfyniadau mawr ynghylch dyfodol eu hysgolion. Mae enghreifftiau'n cynnwys, ond heb fod yn gyfyngedig i, ysgolion eglwysig. Ysgrifennais at y cyngor yn ôl ym mis Medi ynghylch penderfyniadau ar ddyfodol ysgol Cilgerran, ac rwy'n falch fod hyn bellach wedi'i ddatrys. Ond Weinidog Cabinet, mae ymddiriedaeth a hyder y cyhoedd yn hawdd eu colli. Wrth i Gyngor Sir Penfro ymgynghori ar gynigion i gau Ysgol Gynradd yr Eglwys yng Nghymru Dinbych-y-Pysgod, sy'n ysgol wirfoddol a gynhelir, ac ysgol gyfagos Greenhill, ac agor ysgol gymunedol newydd i blant tair i 19 oed yn eu lle, a all y Gweinidog Cabinet roi sicrwydd i ni ei bod yn disgwyl i'r penderfyniadau hyn fod yn seiliedig ar gyfranogiad ystyrlon rhieni a'r gymuned ehangach, gan gynnwys gwybodaeth agored a thryloyw am yr holl opsiynau sydd ar gael?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Local authorities are democratically accountable to their communities and are responsible for developing school organisation proposals. In so doing, they must comply with the requirements set out in the School Standards and Organisation (Wales) Act 2013, and the school organisation code, which is quite clear about the processes and involvement that is required in these cases. I do expect all proposers to comply fully with these statutory requirements and to engage openly and meaningfully with all those affected by any proposal. These decisions should be informed by the evidence gathered through consultation and taken in accordance with the legislative framework. You will be aware, because I've said it several times, that the role of Welsh Ministers in the statutory process means that I'm unable to comment on proposals that I may later be required to determine. But, in the context of all decisions, I would expect my first two points to be clear.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Mae awdurdodau lleol yn atebol yn ddemocrataidd i'w cymunedau ac yn gyfrifol am ddatblygu cynigion trefniadaeth ysgolion. Wrth wneud hynny, rhaid iddynt gydymffurfio â'r gofynion a nodir yn Neddf Safonau a Threfniadaeth Ysgolion (Cymru) 2013, a'r cod trefniadaeth ysgolion, sy'n eithaf clir ynghylch y prosesau a'r cyfranogiad sy'n ofynnol yn yr achosion hyn. Rwy'n disgwyl i bob cynigydd gydymffurfio'n llawn â'r gofynion statudol hyn ac ymgysylltu'n agored ac yn ystyrlon â phawb yr effeithir arnynt gan unrhyw gynnig. Dylai'r penderfyniadau hyn gael eu llywio gan y dystiolaeth a gesglir drwy ymgynghori a'u gwneud yn unol â'r fframwaith deddfwriaethol. Fe fyddwch yn ymwybodol, gan fy mod wedi'i ddweud sawl tro, fod rôl Gweinidogion Cymru yn y broses statudol yn golygu na allaf wneud sylwadau ar gynigion y gallai fod yn ofynnol imi wneud penderfyniad yn eu cylch yn nes ymlaen. Ond yng nghyd-destun pob penderfyniad, buaswn yn disgwyl i fy nau bwynt cyntaf fod yn glir.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ysgolion Gwledig
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rural Schools

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. Pa asesiad y mae’r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi’i wneud o’r pwysau ariannol sy’n wynebu ysgolion gwledig yng Ngwynedd Maldwyn? OQ64722
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. What assessment has the Cabinet Minister made of the financial pressures facing rural schools in Gwynedd Maldwyn? OQ64722

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. I seem to have lost you in my book. Wait a second. I'm sorry.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Ymddengys fy mod wedi eich colli yn fy llyfr. Arhoswch eiliad. Mae’n ddrwg gennyf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Rydyn ni'n cydnabod y pwysau sylweddol ar draws ein hysgolion a'n hawdurdodau lleol ni, yn ogystal ag ymrwymiad y gweithlu addysg i barhau i gefnogi dysgwyr. Mae penderfyniadau ynghylch lefel y cyllid sydd ar gael i ysgolion, gan gynnwys ysgolion gwledig, yn cael eu gwneud gan bob awdurdod lleol wrth bennu eu cyllideb gyffredinol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We recognise the significant pressures across our schools and local authorities, and acknowledge the commitment of the education workforce in continuing to support learners. Decisions on the level of funding available to schools, including rural schools, are made by each local authority as part of their overall budget setting.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Cabinet Minister. In Gwynedd Maldwyn, we're already seeing the consequences of the financial pressures on these rural schools. Both Gwynedd and Powys have closed rural primary schools and further closures are being considered or progressed. I understand smaller schools can cost more per pupil to run, but these schools are often at the heart of their communities. When one closes, it's not just the school building that is lost; children may have to travel much further, parents have to reorganise their lives, and villages lose something that is very difficult to replace. And, of course, transporting those children elsewhere comes at a cost as well. So, can I ask the Cabinet Secretary whether the Welsh Government is properly accounting for those wider costs and the impact on rural communities when assessing the funding pressures facing our rural schools? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Yng Ngwynedd Maldwyn, rydym eisoes yn gweld canlyniadau'r pwysau ariannol ar yr ysgolion gwledig hyn. Mae Gwynedd a Phowys wedi cau ysgolion cynradd gwledig ac mae cau rhagor dan ystyriaeth neu ar y gweill. Rwy'n deall y gall ysgolion llai gostio mwy i'w rhedeg fesul disgybl, ond mae'r ysgolion hyn yn aml yn hollbwysig i'w cymunedau. Pan fydd un yn cau, nid adeilad yr ysgol yn unig sy'n cael ei golli; efallai y bydd yn rhaid i blant deithio'n llawer pellach, rhaid i rieni ad-drefnu eu bywydau, ac mae pentrefi'n colli rhywbeth y mae'n anodd iawn ei adfer. Ac wrth gwrs, mae cludo'r plant hynny i rywle arall yn costio hefyd. Felly, a gaf i ofyn i Ysgrifennydd y Cabinet a yw Llywodraeth Cymru’n cyfrif y costau ehangach hynny yn iawn a'r effaith ar gymunedau gwledig wrth asesu'r pwysau ariannol sy'n wynebu ein hysgolion gwledig? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Rydyn ni'n gwybod yn iawn pa mor bwysig yw ysgolion i'n cymunedau gwledig, ac yng nghyd-destun ysgolion llai, er enghraifft, mae yna ofynion manwl iawn ynglŷn ag ymgynghori ynglŷn ag aildrefnu mewn unrhyw fodd. Mi fydd yr Aelod hefyd yn gwybod bod fy nghydweithiwr y Gweinidog dros ddygnwch gwledig yn edrych ar fesurau i feithrin a gwarchod dygnwch cymunedau gwledig, a bod ystyriaethau ynglŷn â chynnal gwasanaethau gyda phoblogaeth mwy gwasgaredig, er enghraifft, yn rhan o'r ystyriaethau hynny. Dwi'n credu mai'r ateb ehangach yw, o edrych ar y gofynion mewn cymunedau gwledig, fod yna gyfrifoldeb yn ehangach ar draws y Llywodraeth ar gyfer sicrhau ein bod ni'n deall yr heriau penodol yn yr ardaloedd hynny ac yn ymateb yn briodol iddyn nhw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. We understand just how important schools are for our rural communities, and in the context of smaller schools, for example, there are very detailed requirements in relation to consultation on any reorganisation that's proposed. The Member will also be aware that my colleague the Minister for rural resilience is looking at ways of nurturing and protecting the resilience of rural communities, and that considerations on sustaining services with a more dispersed population, for example, are part of those wider considerations. I think that the broader response is that, in looking at the needs of rural communities, there is a broader responsibility across Government in ensuring that we do understand the specific challenges faced by those areas and respond appropriately to them.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae heriau ysgolion gwledig fel y rhai yn fy etholaeth i yn symptom o heriau ehangach ein hardaloedd gwledig, gyda'r boblogaeth yn heneiddio, teuluoedd yn symud i ffwrdd, a gwasanaethau llywodraeth leol yn ddrutach i'w rhedeg ac yn anoddach i'w gweithredu. Er mwyn i ysgolion gwledig ffynnu, mae angen swyddi o ansawdd, cartrefi digonol a thrafnidiaeth gyhoeddus effeithiol, a dwi'n falch o weld y Llywodraeth yn gweithredu ar y materion hyn. Os bydd cymunedau gwledig yn ffynnu, yna bydd ysgolion gwledig yn ffynnu. Sut, felly, bydd y cynllun Ysgolion Cymunedol a Mwy yn grymuso’n hysgolion gwledig, yn ogystal â grymuso'r cymunedau maen nhw’n perthyn iddynt?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The challenges facing rural schools like those in my constituency are a symptom of the broader challenges facing our rural areas, with an ageing population, families moving away and local authority services that are more expensive to run and more difficult to administer. For rural schools to flourish, we need high-quality jobs, adequate housing and effective public transport, and I'm very pleased to see the Government taking action on these matters. If rural communities prosper, then rural schools will prosper too. How, then, will the Community Schools Plus plan empower our rural schools, as well as empowering the communities to which they belong?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. Mi fydd yr Aelod efallai'n ymwybodol ein bod ni'n peilota'r cynllun ysgolion hynny ar hyn o bryd i edrych ar ddatblygu ein dealltwriaeth ni o'r heriau sydd yn eu hwynebu nhw, ac yn tynnu, fel roeddwn i'n dweud ynghynt, yr elfennau gwahanol yma o bolisïau at ei gilydd. Mi fydd hi'n ymwybodol hefyd fod trafnidiaeth ysgol yn flaenoriaeth benodol i'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth, bod y Gweinidog dygnwch gwledig yn edrych ar y materion yma hefyd, a fy mod i innau hefyd yn edrych yn gyson ar yr heriau demograffig sydd mynd i effeithio ar sut rŷn ni'n darparu gwasanaethau ac addysg mewn cymunedau cefn gwlad, ac yng Nghymru yn ehangach, i ddweud y gwir.

Felly, beth fydden i'n annog yr Aelod i edrych arno fe yw'r gwaith manwl ar draws nifer o feysydd gwahanol rŷn ni'n symud arno fe'n gyflym ac sydd yn bethau sydd yn berthnasol i'r cwestiwn a gododd hi, ond nad sydd o angenrheidrwydd wedi eu hynysu i'r portffolio addysg yn unig, ac rŷn ni wedi mynd ati'n fwriadus i sicrhau nad ydyn ni'n edrych ar y gofynion hyn trwy un lens yn unig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much. The Member may be aware that we are currently piloting the Community Schools Plus programme at the moment in order to look at developing our understanding of the challenges facing those schools and, as I said earlier, drawing on those different elements of policies and bringing them together. I am, of course, aware, too, that school transport is a particular priority for the Deputy Minister for Transport, that the Minister for rural resilience is also looking at these issues and I, too, am looking at the demographic challenges that will impact on how we provide services and education, particularly in rural communities and in Wales more broadly, too.

So, what I would encourage the Member to look at is the detailed work happening across a number of different areas, which we are progressing quickly, as areas that relate to her question but are not necessarily reserved to the education portfolio, and we have taken meaningful steps to ensure that we don't look at these issues in isolation.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Dirprwy Weinidog Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Welsh Government is committed to lifelong learning and ensuring that adults can access opportunities to develop new skills, retrain and progress throughout their lives. Through personal learning accounts, employability programmes and further education opportunities, we support adults retraining for new careers to realise their potential and progress into sustainable employment.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi ymrwymo i ddysgu gydol oes a sicrhau y gall oedolion gael mynediad at gyfleoedd i ddatblygu sgiliau newydd, ailhyfforddi a chamu ymlaen drwy gydol eu bywydau. Drwy gyfrifon dysgu personol, rhaglenni cyflogadwyedd a chyfleoedd addysg bellach, rydym yn cefnogi oedolion sy'n ailhyfforddi ar gyfer gyrfaoedd newydd i wireddu eu potensial a chamu ymlaen i gyflogaeth gynaliadwy.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Weinidog. People retrain for many reasons: after losing a job, returning to work after raising a family, or starting a new chapter following a career break. Others come to Wales with valuable qualifications and skills that go unrecognised, despite the contribution they could make to our Welsh economy. At the Inspire! adult learning awards, I met learners determined to gain new skills and contribute to their communities. For many, adult learning is more than education; it is a vital opportunity to rebuild their careers and their lives here in Wales. One of my constituents, Yassmein Hussein, completed 13 adult learning courses through Cardiff and Vale College and Cardiff Council, leading her to win the shared futures award at the awards. Yassmein's story shows what people can achieve when they have access to the right learning opportunities. But not everyone gets that chance, and many adults still face barriers to retraining. So, I want to know how the Welsh Government is ensuring that adults who want to retrain for a new career can access the learning opportunities and support they need to make that transition.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Mae pobl yn ailhyfforddi am lawer o resymau: ar ôl colli swydd, dychwelyd i'r gwaith ar ôl magu teulu, neu ddechrau pennod newydd yn dilyn seibiant gyrfa. Mae eraill yn dod i Gymru gyda chymwysterau a sgiliau gwerthfawr nad ydynt yn cael eu cydnabod, er gwaethaf y cyfraniad y gallent ei wneud i'n heconomi yng Nghymru. Yng ngwobrau dysgu oedolion Ysbrydoli!, cyfarfûm â dysgwyr sy'n benderfynol o ennill sgiliau newydd a chyfrannu at eu cymunedau. I lawer, mae dysgu oedolion yn fwy nag addysg yn unig; mae'n gyfle hanfodol i ailadeiladu eu gyrfaoedd a'u bywydau yma yng Nghymru. Cwblhaodd un o'm hetholwyr, Yassmein Hussein, 13 cwrs dysgu oedolion drwy Goleg Caerdydd a'r Fro a Chyngor Caerdydd, a arweiniodd at ennill y wobr rhannu dyfodol yn y gwobrau. Mae stori Yassmein yn dangos yr hyn y gall pobl ei gyflawni pan fydd ganddynt fynediad at y cyfleoedd dysgu cywir. Ond nid yw pawb yn cael y cyfle hwnnw, ac mae llawer o oedolion yn dal i wynebu rhwystrau i ailhyfforddi. Felly, hoffwn wybod sut y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn sicrhau y gall oedolion sydd eisiau ailhyfforddi ar gyfer gyrfa newydd gael mynediad at y cyfleoedd dysgu a'r cymorth sydd ei angen arnynt i wneud y newid hwnnw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, like you, I was there in the Inspire! adult learning awards, and what a terrific night it was, to hear the remarkable stories of adult learners across Wales, many who have overcome very personal barriers to achieve in their learning. It really was an inspirational evening and, for me, it's one of the highlights of the year to go to that event. What it shows is that adult learning is about more than just gaining qualifications or skills. It builds confidence, it increases resilience and it improves well-being, and I was delighted to be there to share in Yassmein's success that evening.

In terms of your direct question, the Welsh Government is committed to ensuring that people of all ages have opportunities to learn throughout their lives. We do provide Medr with funding streams, which is allocated to further education colleges and other providers to support learners facing particular barriers. They may relate to disabilities, financial hardship, transport issues, childcare, mental health and well-being. This can include additional learning support, disability-related support, transport assistance, childcare, well-being services and so on, because we want to remove those barriers that stand in their way. Now, in particular, there is a community learning grant worth £6.5 million available to fund adult community learning in general, adult basic education, employability, English for speakers of other languages and well-being courses. These actually help people back into skills and work.

There is also a learning grant for learners over the age of 19, and also a personal learning account programme, which aims to help individuals upskill or reskill, as you mentioned, in priority sectors. So, the Welsh Government is absolutely clear that we do support adults in their retraining and upskilling, and want to be as supportive as we can. Because lifelong learning means exactly that: it never stops. So, we are 100 per cent committed to that programme.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, fel chi, roeddwn yno yng ngwobrau dysgu oedolion Ysbrydoli!, ac am noson wych oedd hi, i gael clywed straeon rhyfeddol dysgwyr sy'n oedolion ledled Cymru, gyda llawer ohonynt wedi goresgyn rhwystrau personol iawn i gyflawni yn eu dysgu. Roedd yn noson ysbrydoledig iawn, ac i mi, mae mynd i'r digwyddiad hwnnw yn un o uchafbwyntiau'r flwyddyn. Yr hyn y mae'n ei ddangos yw bod addysg oedolion yn ymwneud â mwy nag ennill cymwysterau neu sgiliau yn unig. Mae'n meithrin hyder, mae'n cynyddu gwydnwch ac mae'n gwella lles, ac roeddwn wrth fy modd yn bod yno i rannu llwyddiant Yassmein y noson honno.

O ran eich cwestiwn uniongyrchol, mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau bod pobl o bob oed yn cael cyfleoedd i ddysgu drwy gydol eu hoes. Rydym yn darparu ffrydiau cyllido i Medr, sy'n cael eu dyrannu i golegau addysg bellach a darparwyr eraill i gefnogi dysgwyr sy'n wynebu rhwystrau penodol. Gallant ymwneud ag anableddau, caledi ariannol, problemau trafnidiaeth, gofal plant, iechyd meddwl a lles. Gall hyn gynnwys cymorth dysgu ychwanegol, cymorth sy'n gysylltiedig ag anabledd, cymorth trafnidiaeth, gofal plant, gwasanaethau lles ac yn y blaen, gan ein bod eisiau cael gwared ar y rhwystrau sy'n sefyll yn eu ffordd. Nawr, yn fwyaf arbennig, mae grant dysgu cymunedol gwerth £6.5 miliwn ar gael i ariannu dysgu cymunedol i oedolion yn gyffredinol, addysg sylfaenol i oedolion, cyflogadwyedd, Saesneg ar gyfer siaradwyr ieithoedd eraill a chyrsiau lles. Mae'r rhain yn helpu pobl i ddychwelyd at sgiliau a gwaith.

Mae grant dysgu ar gael hefyd ar gyfer dysgwyr dros 19 oed, a rhaglen cyfrifon dysgu personol, sy'n anelu at helpu unigolion i uwchsgilio neu ailsgilio, fel y sonioch chi, mewn sectorau â blaenoriaeth. Felly, mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn gwbl glir ein bod yn cefnogi oedolion i ailhyfforddi ac uwchsgilio, ac eisiau bod mor gefnogol ag y gallwn. Oherwydd mae dysgu gydol oes yn golygu yn union hynny: nid yw byth yn dod i ben. Felly, rydym wedi ymrwymo 100 y cant i'r rhaglen honno.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Teachers Leaving the Profession

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 7. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i ganfod y rhesymau pam y mae athrawon yn gadael y proffesiwn? OQ64775
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 7. What action is the Welsh Government taking to establish the reasons for teachers leaving the profession? OQ64775

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Improving recruitment and retention is one of my priorities. We already know that teachers leave the profession for a range of reasons, including workload, well-being and working conditions. We are drawing on national and international evidence and working with our social partners to take practical action to address these issues.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gwella recriwtio a chadw staff yw un o fy mlaenoriaethau. Rydym eisoes yn gwybod bod athrawon yn gadael y proffesiwn am ystod o resymau, gan gynnwys llwyth gwaith, lles ac amodau gwaith. Rydym yn pwyso ar dystiolaeth genedlaethol a rhyngwladol ac yn gweithio gyda'n partneriaid cymdeithasol i roi camau ymarferol ar waith i fynd i'r afael â'r materion hyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Weinidog. Ym mis Mawrth, cyfaddefodd cynllun gweithlu Llywodraeth Cymru nad oedd ganddyn nhw ddata ynghylch pam mae athrawon yn gadael. Nododd Estyn yn union yr un broblem 19 mlynedd yn ôl. Mae ffigurau diweddaraf Cyngor y Gweithlu Addysg yn dangos bod mwy na 3,000 o athrawon ysgol wedi gadael y gofrestr yn y flwyddyn hyd at fis Mawrth, y nifer uchaf mewn pum mlynedd. Ond dydyn ni ddim yn gwybod pam. Does yna ddim system genedlaethol i ofyn i’r athrawon eu hunain pam maen nhw wedi gadael. Mae Lloegr a’r Alban yn gwneud hynny. Pan nad yw Cymru? A wnaiff y Gweinidog ofyn i Gyngor y Gweithlu Addysg ddechrau gofyn i athrawon sy’n gadael y gofrestr pam yr aethant, er mwyn inni ddeall sut fedrwn ni stopio mwy o athrawon rhag gadael yn y dyfodol?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Minister. In March, the Welsh Government workforce plan admitted that they did not have data as to why teachers leave the profession. Estyn noted exactly the same concern 19 years ago. The latest figures from the Education Workforce Council show that more than 3,000 schoolteachers have left the register in the year up to March, the highest number in five years. But we don't know why. There is no national system in place to ask the teachers themselves why they have left. England and Scotland do that. Why doesn't Wales? Will the Minister ask the Education Workforce Council to start asking teachers who are leaving the register why they did so, so that we can understand how we can stop more teachers from leaving in the future?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Dydw i ddim yn credu ei bod hi'n gywir i ddweud nad oes tystiolaeth gyda ni. Mae nifer o adroddiadau wedi ymchwilio i’r broblem benodol hon—un yn gymharol ddiweddar gan Cardiff Met, er enghraifft, y brifysgol yng Nghaerdydd, a gyhoeddwyd yn 2024. Mae’r OECD hefyd wedi edrych ar yr heriau yma yng nghyd-destun y gwaith y maen nhw wedi’i wneud yng Nghymru. Mae un o bwyllgorau’r Senedd hefyd wedi edrych yn fanwl ar y broblem yma.

Yr un casgliad maen nhw i gyd wedi dod iddo, i bob pwrpas, sef bod y baich gwaith yn ormodol ac yn drwm. Mae teimlad hefyd nad yw cymdeithas yn gwerthfawrogi ymdrechion athrawon fel yr oedd ar un cyfnod. Rwy’n credu bod dyletswydd arnom i gyd i edrych ar siẁd rydyn ni yn siarad am y proffesiwn addysgu; gallwn ni i gyd fod o gymorth yn y cyd-destun hwnnw o leiaf. Mae hefyd cwestiynau ynglŷn â’r llwybr proffesiynol—dyrchafiadau felly, wrth i rywun symud drwy’r system. Wedyn, mae yna feysydd a phynciau penodol lle mae’n arbennig o anodd i recriwtio a chadw athrawon. Mae dibyniaeth hefyd ar athrawon sydd efallai wedi’u cymhwyso i ddysgu un pwnc, ond sydd yn cael eu gofyn yn gynyddol i addysgu un arall.

Mae’r rhain i gyd yn faterion sydd yn dylanwadu ar ein gallu ni i recriwtio a chadw athrawon, ac mae hwn wedi bod, yn amlwg, yn flaenoriaeth i mi dros y cyfnod diwethaf. Dyna pam, er enghraifft, gwnaethom ni roi taliadau ychwanegol yn eu lle i recriwtio i rai pynciau sydd yn arbennig o anodd, ac wedyn yn edrych ar y gofynion ehangach gyda chynrychiolyddion o’r gweithlu eu hunain.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you. I don't think it's correct to say that we don't have any evidence. There are a number of reports that have looked into this specific problem—one quite recently carried out by Cardiff Met, for example, which was published in 2024. The OECD has also looked at these challenges in the context of work that they have done in Wales. One of the Senedd committees has also looked in detail at this issue.

They've all come to the same conclusion, to all intents and purposes, namely that the workload is excessive and is a heavy workload. There's also a feeling that society does not appreciate the efforts of teachers as it did at one stage in the past. I think that we all have a responsibility to examine how we speak about the education profession; we can all be of help in that context, at least. There are also questions about the professional pathway—in terms of promotions and so on, as you move through the system. Then, there are specific subject areas where it is especially difficult to recruit and retain teachers. There is a dependence as well on teachers who are perhaps qualified to teach one subject but are increasingly asked to teach another subject.

These are all issues that influence our ability to recruit and to retain teachers, and this has, clearly, been a priority for me over the recent period. That is why, for example, we provided those additional payments for recruitment to difficult-to-recruit subjects, and also are looking then at the broader requirements with representatives from the workforce itself.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: And the final question, question 8—Llŷr Powell.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 8. What action is the Welsh Government taking to improve pupil safety? OQ64768

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The safety and well-being of learners is an absolute priority for the Welsh Government. We continue to work closely with schools, local authorities, the police and other partners to prevent harm, identify emerging risks and ensure that appropriate arrangements are in place to respond effectively when concerns arise.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae diogelwch a lles dysgwyr yn flaenoriaeth absoliwt i Lywodraeth Cymru. Rydym yn parhau i weithio'n agos gydag ysgolion, awdurdodau lleol, yr heddlu a phartneriaid eraill i atal niwed, nodi risgiau sy'n dod i'r amlwg a sicrhau bod trefniadau priodol ar waith i ymateb yn effeithiol pan fydd pryderon yn codi.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that answer, Minister. In September, more than 300 pupils in the Caerphilly borough lost their free school transport because, as the council said, they fall within the two-mile measurement of the Learner Travel (Wales) Measure 2008. Now, the problem with that is that the Measure is looking at distance but not incline. I've walked this route with campaigners and parents and children themselves—I went from Aberbargoed to Bargoed—and it's the incline that is the tricky part. During different weathers, whether it's the heat we experienced in the summer, or even cold winter days, when that road can be slippery, it does become a risk. Will the Government now look at reviewing the Learner Travel (Wales) Measure 2008 and look to include the advice on inclines and the difficult weather paths that this could create?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am yr ateb hwnnw, Weinidog. Ym mis Medi, collodd dros 300 o ddisgyblion ym mwrdeistref Caerffili eu cludiant ysgol am ddim oherwydd, fel y dywedodd y cyngor, maent o fewn mesuriad dwy filltir Mesur Teithio gan Ddysgwyr (Cymru) 2008. Nawr, y broblem gyda hynny yw bod y Mesur yn edrych ar bellter ond nid ar lethr. Rwyf wedi cerdded y llwybr hwn gydag ymgyrchwyr a rhieni a phlant eu hunain—euthum o Aberbargoed i Bargoed—a'r llethr yw'r rhan anodd. Mewn gwahanol fathau o dywydd, naill ai'r gwres a brofwyd gennym yn yr haf, neu ddyddiau oer y gaeaf hyd yn oed, pan fo'r ffordd honno'n gallu bod yn llithrig, mae'n dod yn risg. A wnaiff y Llywodraeth edrych ar adolygu Mesur Teithio gan Ddysgwyr (Cymru) 2008 a cheisio cynnwys y cyngor ar lethrau a'r llwybrau tywydd anodd y gallai hyn eu creu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. As I referred to in an earlier answer around school transport more broadly, this has been a challenge on many levels—access to Welsh-medium education, for example. The cost of transport has been an increasing concern and that's why, with my colleague the Minister for transport, we are looking at school transport in particular as an immediate priority and linking that, which may be of interest to you as well, to additional learning needs learners for whom this is a pressing priority. I can't commit this afternoon to looking at the learner travel Measure again, but, certainly, issues more broadly around access to school and transport to get learners there safely are right at the top of my colleague's agenda, I know.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Fel y nodais mewn ateb cynharach ynglŷn â chludiant ysgol yn ehangach, mae hyn wedi bod yn her ar sawl lefel—mynediad at addysg cyfrwng Cymraeg, er enghraifft. Mae cost trafnidiaeth wedi bod yn bryder cynyddol a dyna pam fy mod, gyda fy nghyd-Aelod y Gweinidog trafnidiaeth, yn edrych ar gludiant ysgol yn arbennig fel blaenoriaeth uniongyrchol a chysylltu hynny, a allai fod o ddiddordeb i chi hefyd, â dysgwyr anghenion dysgu ychwanegol y mae hyn yn flaenoriaeth ddybryd iddynt. Ni allaf ymrwymo y prynhawn yma i edrych ar y Mesur Teithio gan Ddysgwyr eto, ond yn sicr, rwy'n gwybod bod materion ehangach ynghylch mynediad at ysgolion a thrafnidiaeth i gael dysgwyr yno'n ddiogel ar frig agenda fy nghyd-Aelod.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi, Weinidog a Dirprwy Weinidog.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, Minister and Deputy Minister.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. Sut mae caffael y Comisiwn yn cefnogi busnesau yng Nghymru? OQ64772
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. How does the Commission's procurement support businesses in Wales? OQ64772

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau i Gomisiwn y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Commission supports Welsh businesses by making procurement opportunities both visible and accessible. All suppliers are treated fairly and consistently under procurement law. Contracts worth more than £30,000 are advertised on Sell2Wales, allowing companies to express an interest and to tender. We also explore the market; we identify potential Welsh suppliers and alert them to suitable opportunities. We monitor spending with Wales-based suppliers through a corporate key performance indicator reported annually. At present, that is being exceeded—it's 55 per cent against our target of 50 per cent. For larger contracts involving subcontractors, we seek opportunities for Welsh businesses to join supply chains. These measures strengthen participation while maintaining an open, transparent and legally compliant procurement process for all involved.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Comisiwn yn cefnogi busnesau Cymru drwy wneud cyfleoedd caffael yn weladwy ac yn hygyrch. Mae pob cyflenwr yn cael ei drin yn deg ac yn gyson o dan gyfraith gaffael. Mae contractau gwerth mwy na £30,000 yn cael eu hysbysebu ar GwerthwchiGymru, gan ganiatáu i gwmnïau fynegi diddordeb ac i dendro. Rydym hefyd yn archwilio'r farchnad; rydym yn nodi darpar gyflenwyr Cymreig ac yn rhoi gwybod iddynt am gyfleoedd addas. Rydym yn monitro gwariant gyda chyflenwyr yng Nghymru drwy ddangosydd perfformiad allweddol corfforaethol yr adroddir yn ei gylch yn flynyddol. Ar hyn o bryd, fe ragorir ar y dangosydd—mae'n 55 y cant yn erbyn ein targed o 50 y cant. Ar gyfer contractau mwy sy'n cynnwys isgontractwyr, rydym yn chwilio am gyfleoedd i fusnesau Cymru ymuno â chadwyni cyflenwi. Mae'r mesurau hyn yn cryfhau cyfranogiad gan gynnal proses gaffael agored a thryloyw sy'n cydymffurfio â'r gyfraith i bawb sydd ynghlwm wrthi.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau i Gomisiwn y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. The Senedd should lead by example in how public money is spent. In 2018-19, the Commission introduced a performance indicator tracking procurement spending with Welsh suppliers. Following scrutiny of its 2020-21 accounts, the Public Accounts and Public Administration Committee recommended splitting the contracts into smaller lots so that the smaller Welsh firms could compete. The Commission accepted that recommendation. The Welsh Government has now pledged to increase public procurement spending with Wales-based suppliers towards 70 per cent. Small and medium-sized businesses account for over 99 per cent of enterprises in Wales. Businesses across Carmarthenshire, from Llanelli to Ammanford and Carmarthen should have a fair opportunity to compete for those contracts funded by Welsh taxpayers, but knowing how much the Commission spends with Welsh suppliers tells us little about whether that money is reaching businesses across the whole of Wales. So, will the Commission publish a regional breakdown of its procurement model spending, including how much goes to small and medium-sized businesses? And what practical steps is it taking to ensure that the smallest firms in areas such as Carmarthenshire can compete for contracts, including splitting larger contracts into smaller lots where appropriate?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Dylai'r Senedd arwain drwy esiampl o ran sut y caiff arian cyhoeddus ei wario. Yn 2018-19, cyflwynodd y Comisiwn ddangosydd perfformiad sy'n olrhain gwariant caffael gyda chyflenwyr o Gymru. Yn dilyn craffu ar ei gyfrifon 2020-21, argymhellodd y Pwyllgor Cyfrifon Cyhoeddus a Gweinyddiaeth Gyhoeddus y dylid rhannu'r contractau'n lotiau llai fel y gallai'r cwmnïau llai o Gymru gystadlu. Derbyniodd y Comisiwn yr argymhelliad hwnnw. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru bellach wedi addo cynyddu gwariant caffael cyhoeddus gyda chyflenwyr yng Nghymru hyd at 70 y cant. Busnesau bach a chanolig yw dros 99 y cant o fentrau yng Nghymru. Dylai busnesau ar draws sir Gaerfyrddin, o Lanelli i Rydaman a Chaerfyrddin gael cyfle teg i gystadlu am y contractau a ariennir gan drethdalwyr Cymru, ond nid yw gwybod faint y mae'r Comisiwn yn ei wario gyda chyflenwyr o Gymru yn dweud fawr ddim wrthym ynglŷn ag a yw'r arian hwnnw'n cyrraedd busnesau ledled Cymru gyfan. Felly, a wnaiff y Comisiwn gyhoeddi dadansoddiad rhanbarthol o wariant ei fodel caffael, gan gynnwys faint sy'n mynd i fusnesau bach a chanolig? A pha gamau ymarferol y mae'n eu cymryd i sicrhau bod y cwmnïau lleiaf mewn ardaloedd fel sir Gaerfyrddin yn gallu cystadlu am gontractau, gan gynnwys rhannu contractau mwy yn lotiau llai lle bo hynny'n briodol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau i Gomisiwn y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Indeed. Well, one of the good illustrations of this is, of course, what we do in terms of the contract we have here with the public food suppliers. Interestingly, I noted that we're exceeding the KPI in aggregate by 55 per cent against our target of 50 per cent, but actually the food procurement by our catering suppliers here, using good Welsh suppliers that do, indeed, break down the individual contracts to really favour smaller suppliers within the Welsh food supply chain, they are achieving in excess of 70 per cent with Welsh suppliers. So, we're actually doing well. But we're always open to more ideas. I'll take away the thoughts that you've given us and see whether we can disaggregate the data even more. But I have to say the story is one of positive success.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn wir. Wel, un o'r pethau sy'n dangos hyn yn dda, wrth gwrs, yw'r hyn a wnawn gyda'r contract sydd gennym yma gyda'r cyflenwyr bwyd cyhoeddus. Yn ddiddorol, nodais ein bod yn rhagori ar y dangosydd perfformiad allweddol o 55 y cant yn erbyn ein targed o 50 y cant, ond mewn gwirionedd mae'r bwyd sy'n cael ei gaffael gan ein cyflenwyr arlwyo yma, gan ddefnyddio cyflenwyr Cymreig da sydd yn wir yn rhannu'r contractau unigol yn rhai llai i ffafrio cyflenwyr llai o faint o fewn y gadwyn gyflenwi bwyd yng Nghymru, maent yn cyflawni dros 70 y cant gyda chyflenwyr o Gymru. Felly, rydym yn gwneud yn dda mewn gwirionedd. Ond rydym bob amser yn agored i fwy o syniadau. Fe ystyriaf y syniadau rydych chi wedi'u rhoi i ni a gweld a allwn ni ddadgyfuno'r data ymhellach eto. Ond mae'n rhaid imi ddweud bod y stori'n un o lwyddiant cadarnhaol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Sbectolau Clyfar
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Smartglasses

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau i Gomisiwn y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Pa fesurau diogelu y bydd y Comisiwn yn eu rhoi ar waith o ran defnyddio sbectolau clyfar ar ystad y Senedd? OQ64771
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. What safeguards will the Commission put in place regarding the use of smartglasses on the Senedd estate? OQ64771

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau i Gomisiwn y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. The Commission already has safeguards in place that restrict filming and recording on the Senedd estate without relevant authorisation. Importantly, those restrictions are technology neutral, and they apply regardless of whether recording is undertaken using conventional equipment, a phone, smartglasses or any other device.

However, we recognise that wearable and AI-enabled technologies are developing rapidly. I've therefore commissioned a review of our policies and guidance to ensure that they remain effective and keep pace with these developments. Our aim is to ensure that Members and their staff, Commission officials and the Senedd estate are properly protected, while allowing the legitimate benefits of new technologies, including, by the way, accessibility benefits, to be realised where their use is appropriate and properly authorised.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Mae gan y Comisiwn fesurau diogelu eisoes ar waith sy'n cyfyngu ar ffilmio a recordio ar ystad y Senedd heb awdurdodiad perthnasol. Yn bwysig, mae'r cyfyngiadau hynny'n niwtral o ran technoleg, ac maent yn berthnasol p'un a yw recordio'n digwydd gan ddefnyddio offer confensiynol, ffôn, sbectol clyfar neu unrhyw ddyfais arall.

Fodd bynnag, rydym yn cydnabod bod technolegau gwisgadwy wedi'u galluogi gan ddeallusrwydd artiffisial yn datblygu'n gyflym. Felly, rwyf wedi comisiynu adolygiad o'n polisïau a'n canllawiau i sicrhau eu bod yn parhau i fod yn effeithiol ac yn cadw i fyny â'r datblygiadau hyn. Ein nod yw sicrhau bod Aelodau a'u staff, swyddogion y Comisiwn ac ystad y Senedd yn cael eu diogelu'n briodol, tra'n caniatáu i fanteision cyfreithlon technolegau newydd, gan gynnwys, gyda llaw, manteision hygyrchedd, gael eu gwireddu lle mae eu defnydd yn briodol ac wedi'i awdurdodi'n briodol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau i Gomisiwn y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member says his glasses caused a stir. They certainly did. The Commission is undertaking a review, the Cabinet Office has enforced a ban, and it's only a matter of time before other organisations follow suit. The review isn't the problem; the gap before it concludes is. The Cabinet Office has already taken action very swiftly, so I'd be grateful to know the Commission's position while that review is under way. I would also argue that this is a question of equity. Everyone should be on a fair and equal footing. A Member wearing a recording device has an advantage over every other person in the room, and they have no idea that they may be filmed. So, whether the glasses weren't filming isn't the point—nobody else can tell, and a rule that depends on checking after isn't a safeguard.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Aelod yn dweud bod ei sbectol wedi achosi cynnwrf. Fe wnaethant hynny yn sicr. Mae'r Comisiwn yn cynnal adolygiad, mae Swyddfa'r Cabinet wedi gosod gwaharddiad, a dim ond mater o amser yw hi cyn i sefydliadau eraill ddilyn eu hesiampl. Nid yr adolygiad yw'r broblem, ond y bwlch cyn iddo gwblhau. Mae Swyddfa'r Cabinet eisoes wedi gweithredu'n gyflym iawn, felly hoffwn wybod safbwynt y Comisiwn tra bod yr adolygiad hwnnw ar y gweill. Buaswn yn dadlau hefyd fod hyn yn fater o gydraddoldeb. Dylai pawb fod ar sail deg a chyfartal. Mae gan Aelod sy'n gwisgo dyfais recordio fantais dros bob person arall yn yr ystafell, ac nid oes ganddynt unrhyw syniad y gallant gael eu ffilmio. Felly, nid nad oedd y sbectol yn ffilmio yw'r pwynt—ni all unrhyw un arall ddweud, ac nid yw rheol sy'n dibynnu ar wirio wedyn yn fesur diogelwch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau i Gomisiwn y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you very much. First of all, on the Cabinet Office, the Cabinet Office may have made a decision on this, and it's perfectly open to Welsh Government to make a decision on how they pursue this policy as well. Also, courts and tribunals have banned the use of film and recording devices outright. Just to reiterate, there is a clear ruling here already, in a technology-neutral way, on any filming and recording device on the Senedd premises. I shouldn't need to remind Members of that. They're fully aware, they went through induction, everybody's aware. I've written out subsequently as well.

On the issue of equity, that's a valid point. It's been raised by other Members. I've actually had some very good written representations about ideas that could be fed into the review. So, I would strongly suggest that all Members, actually, contribute to this review going forward, but recognising that some of this assistive technology has benefits, not least that it has been identified by many within the disability lobby as well to say, 'We want to see the proper, appropriate, authorised use of this in the right situation.'

So, I can just give a further brief update. The initial review of smartglasses and other advancing technologies is now well advanced. I'll be writing to Members before recess to set out further explanation of the way in which the review will carry out its work, including the ways in which Members will be able to participate so that all views can then be taken into account. Just to say, if we get to this point at the speed that we are going, we will be ahead of other Parliaments in actually putting the right procedures in place for this technology.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr. Yn gyntaf oll, ar Swyddfa'r Cabinet, efallai fod Swyddfa'r Cabinet wedi gwneud penderfyniad ar hyn, ac mae'n berffaith agored i Lywodraeth Cymru wneud penderfyniad ar sut y maent hwy'n mynd ar drywydd y polisi hwn hefyd. Hefyd, mae llysoedd a thribiwnlysoedd wedi gwahardd defnyddio dyfeisiau ffilm a recordio yn llwyr. I ailadrodd, mae dyfarniad clir yma eisoes, mewn ffordd niwtral o ran technoleg, ar unrhyw ddyfais ffilmio a recordio ar safle'r Senedd. Ni ddylai fod angen imi atgoffa'r Aelodau o hynny. Maent yn gwbl ymwybodol, fe aethant drwy'r camau sefydlu, mae pawb yn ymwybodol. Rwyf wedi ysgrifennu ar hyn wedyn hefyd.

Ar fater tegwch, mae hwnnw'n bwynt dilys. Mae wedi cael ei godi gan Aelodau eraill. Cefais sylwadau ysgrifenedig da iawn am syniadau y gellid eu bwydo i mewn i'r adolygiad. Felly, buaswn yn awgrymu'n gryf fod yr holl Aelodau'n cyfrannu at yr adolygiad hwn yn y dyfodol, ond gan gydnabod bod gan rywfaint o'r dechnoleg gynorthwyol hon fanteision, nid yn lleiaf ei bod wedi'i nodi gan lawer yn y lobi anabledd hefyd sy'n dweud, 'Rydym am weld defnydd priodol, wedi'i awdurdodi o hyn yn y sefyllfa gywir.'

Felly, gallaf roi diweddariad byr pellach. Mae'r adolygiad cychwynnol o sbectolau clyfar a thechnolegau datblygedig eraill bellach wedi datblygu'n dda. Byddaf yn ysgrifennu at yr Aelodau cyn y toriad i nodi esboniad pellach o'r ffordd y bydd yr adolygiad yn cyflawni ei waith, gan gynnwys y ffyrdd y bydd yr Aelodau'n gallu cymryd rhan fel y gellir ystyried pob barn wedyn. Ac os cyrhaeddwn y pwynt hwn ar y cyflymder rydym yn mynd, byddwn ar y blaen i Seneddau eraill yn rhoi'r gweithdrefnau cywir ar waith ar gyfer y dechnoleg hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau i Gomisiwn y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I appreciate the Llywydd's answer on the Commission's position there. Llywydd, for this review that's taking place with smartglasses, could you confirm whether you're going to be reaching out to charities right now? A lot of them have come forward, like the RNIB, who represent people who are blind or partially sighted, who say this technology has now created an equal playing field. Allowing people who have these glasses who are registered blind or partially sighted on to the estate I think is important in terms of the inclusive side of things. As well, Dyslexia UK is another charity that has come out and actually said these glasses and technology can help equalise the playing field for people's lives in reading in certain colours, and, going forward, I think it's important that the Commission looks to these charities that are coming out expressing views, to make sure the Parliament is as equal as possible.

And in terms of equity, I think it's important that Members should be on an equal playing field. Maybe some Members should be given glasses to help read the manifestos on which they were elected to this Chamber.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n gwerthfawrogi ateb y Llywydd ar safbwynt y Comisiwn. Lywydd, ar gyfer yr adolygiad hwn sy'n digwydd gyda sbectolau clyfar, a wnewch chi gadarnhau y byddwch yn estyn allan at elusennau nawr? Mae llawer ohonynt wedi dweud, fel yr RNIB, sy'n cynrychioli pobl sy'n ddall neu'n gweld yn rhannol, fod y dechnoleg hon bellach wedi sicrhau tegwch. Rwy'n credu bod caniatáu i bobl sydd â'r sbectolau hyn ac sydd wedi'u cofrestru'n ddall neu'n gweld yn rhannol ar yr ystad yn bwysig o ran yr ochr gynhwysol i bethau. Hefyd, mae Dyslexia UK yn elusen arall sydd wedi dweud y gall y sbectol a'r dechnoleg hon helpu i sicrhau tegwch ym mywydau pobl wrth ddarllen mewn lliwiau penodol, ac yn y dyfodol, rwy'n credu ei bod yn bwysig i'r Comisiwn edrych ar yr elusennau hyn sy'n mynegi barn, er mwyn gwneud yn siŵr bod y Senedd mor deg â phosibl.

Ac o ran cydraddoldeb, rwy'n credu ei bod yn bwysig i'r holl Aelodau gael yr un chwarae teg. Efallai y dylid rhoi sbectol i rai Aelodau i'w helpu i ddarllen y maniffestos y cawsant eu hethol arnynt i'r Siambr hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau i Gomisiwn y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Questions to the Senedd Commission
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Simply to add to what I was saying, I think all views are welcome in this. That does include those from organisations outside who do see legitimate use of assistive technology. However, we also need those views about, where any filming and recording devices are used, whether our rules are currently fit for purpose or not, and where these devices may be used in future. So, I'm not pre-empting any outcome of that review, but we're moving on at pace and we do want all views to be heard.

Meanwhile, as I said in the opening part of my answer, the issue here is the integrity of this place, both for Members, staff, visitors and all others who use this, to know that we can do our business in the way that we want it to be done properly.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I ychwanegu at yr hyn roeddwn i'n ei ddweud, rwy'n credu bod croeso i bob safbwynt ar hyn. Mae hynny'n cynnwys rhai gan sefydliadau y tu allan sy'n gweld defnydd cyfreithlon o dechnoleg gynorthwyol. Fodd bynnag, mae angen safbwyntiau arnom hefyd ynglŷn â ble y gwneir defnydd o unrhyw ddyfeisiau ffilmio a recordio, a yw ein rheolau'n addas i'r diben ar hyn o bryd ai peidio, a ble y gellir defnyddio'r dyfeisiau hyn yn y dyfodol. Felly, nid wyf yn achub y blaen ar unrhyw ganlyniad i'r adolygiad hwnnw, ond rydym yn symud ymlaen yn gyflym ac rydym am i bob barn gael ei chlywed.

Yn y cyfamser, fel y dywedais yn rhan agoriadol fy ateb, y cwestiwn sy'n codi yma yw uniondeb y lle hwn, er mwyn i Aelodau, staff, ymwelwyr a phawb arall sy'n defnyddio'r dechnoleg wybod y gallwn wneud ein gwaith yn y ffordd briodol yr ydym am iddo gael ei wneud.
