XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cabinet Minister, last Friday evening, residents of Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf in Nantgarw and Taff's Well, as well as communities in Tongwynlais and Gwaelod-y-garth, alerted NRW to a pollution incident in the River Taff, following a toxic leak from GE Aerosapce Wales's engine maintenance plant. We have been told that up to 25,000 litres of kerosene spilled into the river. The impact on people's health and the environmental damage, at least 2 miles downstream, was immediate. Members of the community we have met have spoken of unbearable conditions, which cause headaches, sickness and drowsiness. And then there has been the deadly impact on wildlife and the natural environment all along the river.

We have spoken to South Wales Fire and Rescue Service, who were called by NRW, and were first on the scene. They suggested that an incident occurred on the site sometime before they arrived. Finally, we have met with GE Aerospace, who have confirmed that they were the source of the leak and have assured us that the fuel lines have now been isolated to prevent any further spillage. We welcome the ongoing work being undertaken by Natural Resources Wales, Public Health Wales and the emergency services to assess and respond to this extremely serious incident, but many questions remain to be answered.

What assurance have you received regarding the volume and chemical make-up of the fuel released, and what further risk is there given that this is an area prone to flooding? What discussions have you had with Natural Resources Wales regarding the next steps being taken around the clean-up operation and habitat restoration, and how long this is likely to last? When can we expect a full and transparent review to identify how, why and when exactly this incident occurred, what safeguards are in place, and what is being done to ensure that this won't happen again? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Weinidog Cabinet, nos Wener diwethaf, dywedwyd wrth CNC gan drigolion Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf yn Nantgarw a Ffynnon Taf, yn ogystal â chymunedau yn Nhongwynlais a Gwaelod-y-garth, am ddigwyddiad llygredd yn afon Taf, yn dilyn gollyngiad gwenwynig o waith cynnal a chadw injans GE Aerospace Wales. Dywedwyd wrthym fod hyd at 25,000 litr o gerosin wedi gollwng i'r afon. Roedd yr effaith ar iechyd pobl a'r niwed amgylcheddol, o leiaf 2 filltir i lawr yr afon, yn uniongyrchol. Mae aelodau o'r gymuned rydym wedi cyfarfod â nhw wedi sôn am amodau annioddefol, sy'n achosi cur pen, salwch a syrthni. At hynny, bu'r effaith ar fywyd gwyllt a'r amgylchedd naturiol ar hyd yr afon yn angheuol.

Rydym wedi siarad â Gwasanaeth Tân ac Achub De Cymru, a gafodd eu galw gan CNC, a nhw oedd y cyntaf i gyrraedd y lleoliad. Fe wnaethant awgrymu bod digwyddiad wedi digwydd ar y safle rywbryd cyn iddynt gyrraedd. Yn olaf, rydym wedi cyfarfod â GE Aerospace, sydd wedi cadarnhau mai nhw oedd ffynhonnell y gollyngiad ac maent wedi rhoi sicrwydd i ni fod y pibellau tanwydd bellach wedi'u hynysu er mwyn atal unrhyw ollyngiadau pellach. Rydym yn croesawu'r gwaith parhaus gan Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru, Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru a'r gwasanaethau brys i asesu ac ymateb i'r digwyddiad hynod ddifrifol hwn, ond mae llawer o gwestiynau'n parhau heb eu hateb.

Pa sicrwydd rydych chi wedi'i gael ynghylch cyfaint a chyfansoddiad cemegol y tanwydd a ollyngwyd, a pha risg bellach sydd yna o ystyried bod hon yn ardal sy'n dueddol o gael llifogydd? Pa drafodaethau a gawsoch gyda Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru ynghylch y camau nesaf sydd i'w cymryd o ran y gwaith glanhau ac adfer cynefinoedd, a pha mor hir y mae hyn yn debygol o bara? Pryd y gallwn ddisgwyl adolygiad llawn a thryloyw i nodi sut, pam a phryd yn union y digwyddodd y digwyddiad hwn, pa fesurau diogelwch sydd ar waith, a beth sy'n cael ei wneud i sicrhau na fydd hyn yn digwydd eto? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr for your question—or for your questions, I should say; there are a number of questions there, but rightly need responding to.

The first thing I would say is that I have spoken directly with Natural Resources Wales about this significant incident and the ongoing response. I fully recognise the concern that it has caused for local communities and for those with an interest in or an involvement with or living nearby the River Taff. NRW have confirmed to me, as I said in my initial answer, that fuel discharge has now stopped and that current mitigation measures are preventing residual fuel in the tributary from reaching the River Taff, and clean-up and environmental assessments are continuing.

You asked about the volume particularly, but also the source and maybe a little bit about the precise circumstances of the release. Those remain matters for NRW's ongoing investigation, but you're right: early reporting made claims that a considerable amount, estimated at up to 25,000 litres, may have been lost into the site's surface water drainage system. But I wouldn't want to present that estimate as some sort of final confirmed figure, because, as I say, investigations continue. For example, my understanding is that the tank could potentially contain that much; it's not clear yet how much was in it. And, of course, not all of it would have found its way into the river—some of it would have been contained or collected on site before reaching there. So, we need to be mindful of that, but, obviously, this will become clearer over time. The pollutant has, though, been identified as kerosene.

I've discussed the ongoing response with NRW, and I'll continue to keep closely sighted on developments there. The site operator's specialist contractor, who they brought in very early on, continue recovery and clean-up activity, including maintaining and replacing containment booms, whilst NRW continues to assess the environmental impact. NRW officers have observed impacts on aquatic invertebrates, which may be linked to this incident. The information currently available doesn't provide a firm timescale for completion of the clean-up—which is another question you asked—or any subsequent habitat restoration that might follow as a consequence. Again, I wouldn't want to speculate on that today, but that work is ongoing. NRW will continue to work with the site operator to establish the cause, and they will ensure that all possible steps are taken to prevent further spills.

The circumstances of the incident and its environmental impacts remain under investigation, and it would therefore not be appropriate for me to speculate on who is responsible, or anticipate any regulatory or enforcement action that might follow. But, again, I would reiterate—I'm sure, on behalf of everyone here—our thanks to all of those who have been involved in the response effort, which, I have to say, happened promptly and in a very effective manner.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr am eich cwestiwn—neu am eich cwestiynau, dylwn ddweud; roedd nifer o gwestiynau yno, ond mae angen ymateb iddynt yn briodol.

Y peth cyntaf y buaswn yn ei ddweud yw fy mod wedi siarad yn uniongyrchol â Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru ynglŷn â'r digwyddiad difrifol hwn a'r ymateb parhaus. Rwy'n llwyr gydnabod y pryder y mae wedi'i achosi i gymunedau lleol ac i'r rhai sydd â buddiant yn afon Taf neu sy'n ymwneud â hi neu sy'n byw gerllaw. Mae CNC wedi cadarnhau i mi, fel y dywedais yn fy ateb cychwynnol, fod y gollyngiadau tanwydd bellach ar ben a bod mesurau lliniaru cyfredol yn atal tanwydd gweddilliol yn yr is-afon rhag cyrraedd afon Taf, ac mae'r gwaith glanhau ac asesiadau amgylcheddol yn parhau.

Fe ofynnoch chi am y cyfaint yn arbennig, ond hefyd y ffynhonnell ac efallai ychydig am amgylchiadau penodol y gollyngiad. Mae'r rheini'n parhau i fod yn faterion ar gyfer ymchwiliad parhaus CNC, ond rydych chi'n llygad eich lle: roedd adroddiadau cynnar yn honni y gallai cryn dipyn o danwydd, hyd at 25,000 litr yn ôl amcangyfrifon, fod wedi gollwng i system ddraenio dŵr wyneb y safle. Ond ni fuaswn eisiau cyflwyno'r amcangyfrif hwnnw fel rhyw fath o ffigur terfynol wedi'i gadarnhau, oherwydd fel y dywedais, mae'r ymchwiliadau'n parhau. Er enghraifft, fy nealltwriaeth i yw ei bod yn bosibl y gallai'r tanc gynnwys cymaint o danwydd â hynny; nid yw'n glir eto faint oedd ynddo. Ac wrth gwrs, ni fyddai'r cyfan ohono wedi mynd i'r afon—byddai rhywfaint ohono wedi'i atal neu ei gasglu ar y safle cyn cyrraedd yr afon. Felly, mae angen inni fod yn ymwybodol o hynny, ond yn amlwg, bydd hyn yn dod yn gliriach dros amser. Fodd bynnag, cadarnhawyd mai cerosin oedd y llygrydd.

Rwyf wedi trafod yr ymateb parhaus gyda CNC, a byddaf yn parhau i gadw llygad barcud ar y datblygiadau yno. Mae contractwr arbenigol gweithredwr y safle, y daethant i mewn â nhw'n gynnar iawn, yn parhau â gweithgarwch adfer a glanhau, gan gynnwys cynnal a chadw ac ailosod bwmau cyfyngu, tra bo CNC yn parhau i asesu'r effaith amgylcheddol. Mae swyddogion CNC wedi nodi effeithiau ar infertebratau dyfrol, a allai fod yn gysylltiedig â'r digwyddiad hwn. Nid yw'r wybodaeth sydd ar gael ar hyn o bryd yn darparu amserlen gadarn ar gyfer cwblhau'r gwaith glanhau—sy'n gwestiwn arall a ofynnwyd gennych—nac unrhyw waith adfer cynefinoedd dilynol a allai ddigwydd o ganlyniad. Unwaith eto, ni fuaswn eisiau dyfalu ynghylch hynny heddiw, ond mae'r gwaith hwnnw'n parhau. Bydd CNC yn parhau i weithio gyda gweithredwr y safle i nodi'r achos, a byddant yn sicrhau bod pob cam posibl yn cael ei gymryd i atal gollyngiadau pellach.

Mae amgylchiadau'r digwyddiad a'i effeithiau amgylcheddol yn parhau i fod yn destun ymchwiliad, ac felly ni fyddai'n briodol imi ddyfalu pwy sy'n gyfrifol, na cheisio darogan unrhyw gamau rheoleiddio neu orfodi a allai ddilyn. Ond unwaith eto, rwyf am ailadrodd—ar ran pawb yma, rwy'n siŵr—ein diolch i bawb sydd wedi bod yn rhan o'r ymateb, a ddigwyddodd, rhaid imi ddweud, yn brydlon ac mewn modd effeithiol iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you to the Member for raising this. Cabinet Minister, I spent over 20 years with South Wales Fire and Rescue Service, so I recognise the efforts of crews, Natural Resources Wales officers, and everyone containing pollution. But the facts are deeply concerning: kerosene from GE Aerospace's Nantgarw site has affected around 4 km of the Taff. Dead fish have been recovered, residents have been advised to close windows and doors, and fumes are present. GE Aerospace said it isolated the source on Friday, yet on Monday Natural Resources Wales said it was still investigating the drainage system to stop further pollution. Stopping the original leak is not the same as stopping pollution reaching the river. And this is not the first time; in 2024, pollution from PB Gelatins UK in Treforest killed fish. The outcome announced this June was the enforcement undertaking, including a £50,000 donation and nearly £15,000 in costs.

Cabinet Minister, you chaired the committee that reported Natural Resources Wales's own concerns that its fines and sanctions weren't enough to deter polluters. You now oversee Natural Resources Wales. Our Reform manifesto commits us to dismantling and fundamentally restructuring Natural Resources Wales, bringing strategic policy under ministerial oversight while environmental protections continue without interruptions.

The public deserve to know what went wrong, who is accountable and who will pay to put it right. So, Cabinet Minister, will you commit to a written statement to this Senedd within 14 days, setting out how much fuel was released, the damage identified so far, the timetable for Natural Resources Wales's investigation and any enforcement decision, and how all legal recoverable costs will be pursued from those found responsible and not the Welsh taxpayer? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch i'r Aelod am godi hyn. Weinidog Cabinet, treuliais dros 20 mlynedd gyda Gwasanaeth Tân ac Achub De Cymru, felly rwy'n cydnabod ymdrechion criwiau, swyddogion Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru, a phawb sy'n rheoli llygredd. Ond mae'r ffeithiau'n peri cryn bryder: mae cerosin o safle GE Aerospace yn Nantgarw wedi effeithio ar oddeutu 4 km o afon Taf. Mae pysgod marw wedi'u casglu, mae trigolion wedi cael eu cynghori i gau ffenestri a drysau, ac mae mygdarth yn bresennol. Dywedodd GE Aerospace eu bod wedi ynysu'r ffynhonnell ddydd Gwener, ond ddydd Llun, dywedodd Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru eu bod yn dal i ymchwilio i'r system ddraenio i atal llygredd pellach. Nid yw atal y gollyngiad gwreiddiol yr un peth ag atal llygredd rhag cyrraedd yr afon. Ac nid dyma'r tro cyntaf; yn 2024, lladdwyd pysgod yn Nhrefforest gan lygredd o PB Gelatins UK. Y canlyniad a gyhoeddwyd ym mis Mehefin eleni oedd yr ymgymeriad gorfodi, gan gynnwys rhodd o £50,000 a bron i £15,000 mewn costau.

Weinidog Cabinet, chi oedd cadeirydd y pwyllgor a adroddodd ar bryderon Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru eu hunain nad oedd eu dirwyon a'u sancsiynau yn ddigon i rwystro llygrwyr. Rydych chi nawr yn goruchwylio Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru. Mae maniffesto Reform yn ein hymrwymo i ddatgymalu ac ailstrwythuro Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru yn gyfan gwbl, gan ddod â pholisi strategol o dan oruchwyliaeth weinidogol tra bod amddiffyniadau amgylcheddol yn parhau heb ymyrraeth.

Mae'r cyhoedd yn haeddu gwybod beth a aeth o'i le, pwy sy'n atebol a phwy fydd yn talu i'w unioni. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, a wnewch chi ymrwymo i wneud datganiad ysgrifenedig i'r Senedd hon o fewn 14 diwrnod, yn nodi faint o danwydd a ollyngwyd, y niwed a nodwyd hyd yma, yr amserlen ar gyfer ymchwiliad Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru ac unrhyw benderfyniad gorfodi, a sut y bydd y rhai a geir yn gyfrifol ac nid trethdalwyr Cymru yn talu'r holl gostau cyfreithiol sy'n adenilladwy? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for the question. Frankly, everything you've asked for is in train. It will be the responsibility of NRW to provide all of that information. On cost recovery, clearly, they will need to establish liability, if there is liability, and then they will proceed in the appropriate manner, either through the courts or whichever way they believe is most appropriate. I have to question, if you dismantle NRW, as you describe it, the question remains, who would actually be dealing with these situations when they arise? Maybe that's something that you may wish to ponder.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich cwestiwn. A dweud y gwir, mae popeth rydych chi wedi gofyn amdano ar y gweill. Cyfrifoldeb CNC fydd darparu'r holl wybodaeth honno. Ar adennill costau, yn amlwg, bydd angen iddynt sefydlu atebolrwydd, os oes atebolrwydd, ac yna byddant yn bwrw ymlaen yn y modd priodol, naill ai drwy'r llysoedd neu ba bynnag ffordd y credant sydd fwyaf priodol. Rhaid imi gwestiynu, os byddwch yn datgymalu Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru, fel rydych chi'n ei ddisgrifio, mae'r cwestiwn yn parhau, pwy fyddai'n delio â'r sefyllfaoedd hyn pan fyddant yn codi? Efallai fod hynny'n rhywbeth y gallech chi fod eisiau ei ystyried.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: In addition to the questions that have already been raised—this is a constituency that I also represent, Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf—we've seen a number of authorities involved in the immediate response, including Natural Resources Wales and Public Health Wales: could the Minister therefore confirm actually which body is ultimately responsible for co-ordinating clear and effective messaging for the public, and also any signs of warnings in advance? Also, building on what Nick said around safeguarding, what safeguards are in place to make sure that residents who live near the river, and the many, many visitors, of course, to the Taff trail, are informed about the potential health risks before they come into contact with contaminated water? Not everyone looks at Facebook, for example. Not everyone is going to get an alert on their phone. How are we going to make sure that the public know, especially if they've got children or dogs, for example, not to go into the river?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn ogystal â'r cwestiynau sydd eisoes wedi'u codi—mae hon yn etholaeth rwyf innau hefyd yn ei chynrychioli, Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf—rydym wedi gweld nifer o awdurdodau’n cyfrannu at yr ymateb uniongyrchol, gan gynnwys Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru ac Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru: a wnaiff y Gweinidog gadarnhau felly pa gorff sy’n gyfrifol yn y pen draw am gydgysylltu negeseuon clir ac effeithiol i’r cyhoedd, a hefyd unrhyw arwyddion o rybuddion ymlaen llaw? Hefyd, gan adeiladu ar yr hyn a ddywedodd Nick ynghylch diogelu, pa fesurau diogelu sydd ar waith i sicrhau bod trigolion sy’n byw ger yr afon, a’r nifer fawr o ymwelwyr, wrth gwrs, â Thaith Taf, yn cael gwybod am y risgiau iechyd posibl cyn iddynt ddod i gysylltiad â dŵr halogedig? Nid yw pawb yn edrych ar Facebook, er enghraifft. Nid yw pawb yn mynd i gael rhybudd ar eu ffôn. Sut y gallwn sicrhau bod y cyhoedd yn gwybod, yn enwedig os oes ganddynt blant neu gŵn, er enghraifft, i beidio â mynd i mewn i’r afon?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for those questions. NRW are leading the effort in that environmental context, that is their role, but they are also liaising very closely with Public Health Wales and fire and rescue services as well. In terms of public health, you're right, there have been messages put out there by Public Health Wales; some will see them, others, unfortunately, will not. That's a constant challenge in these situations, and any learning that can be taken from any event is taken on board, I hope, and reflected upon. The advice has been clear. Obviously, if you can smell kerosene, then the advice is to keep windows and doors closed and avoid contact with any affected water—that goes for pets and children particularly. Anyone who does consequently feel unwell or concerned needs to contact NHS Wales 111, and the system will respond to that in the best way it can. I think public bodies have been providing that information as best they can, but there will always be room for improvement in that sphere.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich cwestiynau. Mae CNC yn arwain yr ymdrech yn y cyd-destun amgylcheddol hwnnw, dyna yw eu rôl, ond maent hefyd yn cysylltu'n agos iawn ag Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru a'r gwasanaethau tân ac achub hefyd. O ran iechyd y cyhoedd, rydych chi'n llygad eich lle, mae negeseuon wedi'u cyhoeddi gan Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru; bydd rhai yn eu gweld, ac yn anffodus, ni fydd eraill. Mae honno'n her gyson yn y sefyllfaoedd hyn, ac mae unrhyw wersi y gellir eu dysgu o unrhyw ddigwyddiad yn cael eu nodi, rwy'n gobeithio, a'u hystyried. Mae'r cyngor wedi bod yn glir. Yn amlwg, os gallwch arogli cerosin, y cyngor yw cadw ffenestri a drysau ar gau ac osgoi cysylltiad ag unrhyw ddŵr yr effeithiwyd arno—mae hynny'n wir am anifeiliaid anwes a phlant yn arbennig. Mae angen i unrhyw un sy'n teimlo'n sâl neu'n bryderus o ganlyniad gysylltu â GIG Cymru 111, a bydd y system yn ymateb i hynny yn y ffordd orau y gall. Rwy'n credu bod cyrff cyhoeddus wedi bod yn darparu'r wybodaeth honno cystal ag y gallant, ond mae lle i wella bob amser o ran hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I was appalled at the weekend to learn about the kerosene leak from the GE Aerospace site in Nantgarw in my constituency. I'm really concerned about the environmental impact of this pollution as it seeps into the waterways and into the River Taff that runs right through the heart of our city, right down to this place. I understand Natural Resources Wales were made aware of the incident on Friday and have been taking action with fuel-absorbing barriers at the confluence between the tributary and the Taff, but there are some discrepancies between the two organisations' public statements that we've seen. GE Aerospace claimed that the source of the spill was fully identified and isolated on Friday, but NRW have said that they're still seeking to confirm the source.

Cabinet Minister, I'm glad to hear that you're being briefed by NRW. Could you confirm whether or not GE Aerospace are fully co-operating with the investigation? Will GE Aerospace be held fully accountable for their failures, which allowed this to happen? And what will be done to assess and remediate impacts on the fish and animals that live in and around the River Taff, and how will that be paid for?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Cefais fy mrawychu dros y penwythnos wrth glywed am y gollyngiad cerosin o safle GE Aerospace yn Nantgarw yn fy etholaeth. Rwy'n bryderus iawn ynghylch effaith amgylcheddol y llygredd hwn wrth iddo dreiddio i'r dyfrffyrdd ac i afon Taf sy'n rhedeg drwy galon ein dinas, yr holl ffordd i lawr i'r lle hwn. Rwy'n deall bod Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru wedi cael gwybod am y digwyddiad ddydd Gwener ac wedi bod yn cymryd camau gyda rhwystrau amsugno tanwydd wrth y cydlifiad rhwng yr is-afon ac afon Taf, ond mae rhai anghysondebau rhwng y datganiadau cyhoeddus a welsom gan y ddau sefydliad. Honnodd GE Aerospace fod ffynhonnell y gollyngiad wedi'i nodi a'i hynysu'n llawn ddydd Gwener, ond mae CNC wedi dweud eu bod yn dal i geisio cadarnhau'r ffynhonnell.

Weinidog Cabinet, rwy'n falch o glywed eich bod yn cael eich briffio gan CNC. A allwch chi gadarnhau p'un a yw GE Aerospace yn cydweithredu'n llawn â'r ymchwiliad ai peidio? A fydd GE Aerospace yn cael eu dal yn gwbl atebol am eu methiannau, a ganiataodd i hyn ddigwydd? A beth a wneir i asesu ac i adfer yr effeithiau ar y pysgod a'r anifeiliaid sy'n byw yn ac o amgylch afon Taf, a sut y caiff hynny ei ariannu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Look, until the investigations have been completed, I am loath to point the finger as much as Members would like me to. Clearly, where liability is identified—let's put it that way—then NRW will take appropriate action. That is their role and that is what we all expect of them.

In terms of seeking the source of the incident, my understanding is that whilst maybe it had been identified early on, once it was in the drainage system, which can be very complex, it's very difficult then to know exactly where that goes. So, maybe there's a bit of confusion around the source as opposed to the numbers of ways that that water could actually escape the site. But again, all of this will come out in the wash once the initial response and recovery has taken place. There will be a process then to make sure that we look at the results of all of that.

In terms of the environmental impact, of course—and that is clearly an important factor here—NRW are waiting for results of samples for biological and ecological investigations. Drone surveys have been conducted so that they can visually assess the impact as well. I am told that 10 dead fish have been recovered from the river as a consequence of this. Ten dead fish. But, of course, impacts on invertebrates will mean greater ecological impacts as well, and I'm not downplaying that for a second.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Edrychwch, hyd nes bod yr ymchwiliadau wedi'u cwblhau, rwy'n gyndyn i bwyntio bys i'r graddau y byddai'r Aelodau'n hoffi i mi ei wneud. Yn amlwg, lle nodir atebolrwydd—gadewch inni ei roi felly—bydd CNC yn rhoi camau priodol ar waith. Dyna yw eu rôl a dyna y mae pob un ohonom yn ei ddisgwyl ganddynt.

O ran chwilio am ffynhonnell y digwyddiad, er efallai ei fod wedi'i nodi'n gynnar, pan gyrhaeddodd y system ddraenio, a all fod yn gymhleth iawn, fy nealltwriaeth i yw ei bod hi'n anodd iawn gwybod i ble'n union y mae'n mynd. Felly, efallai fod rhywfaint o ddryswch ynghylch y ffynhonnell yn hytrach na nifer y ffyrdd y gallai'r dŵr hwnnw ddianc o'r safle mewn gwirionedd. Ond unwaith eto, bydd hyn oll yn dod i'r amlwg pan fydd yr ymateb cychwynnol a'r gwaith adfer wedi'i gwblhau. Bydd proses wedyn i sicrhau ein bod yn edrych ar ganlyniadau hynny i gyd.

O ran yr effaith amgylcheddol, wrth gwrs—ac mae hynny'n amlwg yn ffactor pwysig yma—mae CNC yn aros am ganlyniadau samplau ar gyfer ymchwiliadau biolegol ac ecolegol. Mae arolygon drôn wedi'u cynnal fel y gallant asesu'r effaith yn weledol hefyd. Dywedir wrthyf fod 10 pysgodyn marw wedi'u casglu o'r afon o ganlyniad i hyn. Deg pysgodyn marw. Ond wrth gwrs, bydd effeithiau ar infertebratau yn golygu effeithiau ecolegol mwy hefyd, ac nid wyf yn bychanu hynny am eiliad.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ac yn olaf, Weinidog, Leticia Gonzalez.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: And finally, Minister, Leticia Gonzalez.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Llywydd. There has been a lot of attention recently on the legacy of industrial contamination in Wales and its devastating impact on local communities and the environment. But this week's shocking news demonstrates that it's not just an issue from our past that we're dealing with, but something from our present too. Can the Cabinet Minister confirm that you're working closely with the Cabinet Minister for health and with Public Health Wales on providing assurance to residents across my constituency of Caerdydd Penarth impacted by this leak?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Mae llawer o sylw wedi bod yn ddiweddar i waddol halogiad diwydiannol yng Nghymru a'i effaith ddinistriol ar gymunedau lleol a'r amgylchedd. Ond mae newyddion syfrdanol yr wythnos hon yn dangos nad mater o'n gorffennol yn unig rydym yn delio ag ef, ond rhywbeth o'n presennol hefyd. A all y Gweinidog Cabinet gadarnhau eich bod yn gweithio'n agos gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros iechyd ac Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru i roi sicrwydd i drigolion ledled fy etholaeth, Caerdydd Penarth, y mae'r gollyngiad hwn wedi effeithio arnynt?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yes. And? [Laughter.]
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gallaf. Ac? [Chwerthin.]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Sorry. And does the Welsh Government reaffirm its stance on the polluter-pays principle, ensuring that those responsible bear the cost of addressing its remediation?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae’n ddrwg gennyf. Ac a yw Llywodraeth Cymru yn ailddatgan ei safbwynt ar yr egwyddor mai’r llygrwr sy’n talu, gan sicrhau mai'r rhai sy'n gyfrifol sy'n talu'r costau cyweirio?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yes and yes. And you will note, of course, that the Deputy Minister with responsibility for public health is here to make sure that all of Members' concerns are fully taken on board. This is an ongoing issue, not just particularly in relation to this incident. These are the challenges that we will continually have to face. A changing climate makes that battle more difficult as well, as we experience more extreme weather events, which no doubt will test infrastructure and these kinds of facilities to a greater extent in years to come.

It does remind us that we always need to be vigilant, always need to be diligent, and I would encourage, by the way, members of the public to make full use of NRW's hotline. There is a hotline there. People can go to their MSs, they can go and put stuff on social media, but ultimately, if you want a swift response, you need to let NRW know first. That would be another plea of mine today. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Ydy. Ac fe sylwch, wrth gwrs, fod y Dirprwy Weinidog sy'n gyfrifol am iechyd y cyhoedd yma i sicrhau bod holl bryderon yr Aelodau'n cael eu hystyried yn llawn. Mae hwn yn fater parhaus, ac nid mewn perthynas â'r digwyddiad penodol hwn yn unig. Dyma'r heriau y bydd yn rhaid i ni eu hwynebu'n barhaus. Mae hinsawdd sy'n newid yn gwneud y frwydr honno'n fwy anodd hefyd, wrth inni wynebu digwyddiadau tywydd mwy eithafol, a fydd, heb os, yn profi'r seilwaith a'r mathau hyn o gyfleusterau i raddau mwy yn y blynyddoedd i ddod.

Mae'n ein hatgoffa bod angen inni fod yn wyliadwrus bob amser, fod angen inni fod yn ddiwyd bob amser, ac rwyf am annog aelodau'r cyhoedd, gyda llaw, i wneud defnydd llawn o linell gymorth CNC. Mae llinell gymorth ar gael. Gall pobl fynd at eu Haelod o'r Senedd, gallant roi pethau ar y cyfryngau cymdeithasol, ond yn y pen draw, os ydych chi eisiau ymateb cyflym, mae angen ichi roi gwybod i CNC yn gyntaf. Mae honno'n apêl arall gennyf heddiw. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn, Weinidog. Roeddwn i'n disgwyl i chi ratlo off y rhif ffôn am yr hotline yna. [Chwerthin.] Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, Cabinet Minister. I was waiting for you to rattle off the phone number for that hotline there. [Laughter.] Thank you very much.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiadau 90 Eiliad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. 90-second Statements
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. I recently had the pleasure of visiting Big Pit National Coal Museum in Blaenavon, where I met with staff and learnt about the excellent work they are doing to preserve and promote Wales's rich industrial heritage. What impressed me most was the museum's commitment not only to protecting our history, but to engaging people of all ages, through education, community outreach and innovative exhibitions. Big Pit continues to play a vital role in ensuring that future generations understand the sacrifices and achievements of those who built our coalfield communities.

During my visit, I also had the opportunity to see the Stories from Aberfan exhibition. And as we mark the sixtieth anniversary of the Aberfan disaster today, this exhibition is a poignant and powerful reminder of the 144 lives lost, the devastating impact on the community and the extraordinary courage and resilience shown in the decades since. The personal stories and artefacts on display help ensure that the memory of Aberfan endures and that the lessons of that tragedy are never forgotten. I would like to thank everyone in Big Pit for their dedication to preserving these important stories and sharing them with future generations, and I encourage all people to visit.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Yn ddiweddar, cefais y pleser o ymweld ag Amgueddfa Lofaol Cymru Big Pit ym Mlaenafon, lle cyfarfûm â staff a dysgu am y gwaith rhagorol a wnânt i warchod a hyrwyddo treftadaeth ddiwydiannol gyfoethog Cymru. Yr hyn a wnaeth yr argraff fwyaf arnaf oedd ymrwymiad yr amgueddfa nid yn unig i ddiogelu ein hanes, ond i ymgysylltu â phobl o bob oed, drwy addysg, allgymorth cymunedol ac arddangosfeydd arloesol. Mae Big Pit yn parhau i chwarae rhan hanfodol yn sicrhau bod cenedlaethau'r dyfodol yn deall aberth a chyflawniadau'r rhai a adeiladodd ein cymunedau glofaol.

Yn ystod fy ymweliad, cefais gyfle hefyd i weld arddangosfa Hanesion Aberfan. Ac wrth inni nodi 60 mlynedd ers trychineb Aberfan heddiw, mae'r arddangosfa hon yn atgof ingol a phwerus o'r 144 o fywydau a gollwyd, yr effaith ddinistriol ar y gymuned a'r dewrder a'r gwydnwch rhyfeddol a ddangoswyd yn y degawdau ers hynny. Mae'r hanesion personol a'r arteffactau yn yr arddangosfa yn helpu i sicrhau bod y cof am Aberfan yn parhau ac nad aiff gwersi'r drasiedi honno byth yn angof. Hoffwn ddiolch i bawb yn Big Pit am eu hymroddiad i ddiogelu'r hanesion pwysig hyn a'u rhannu â chenedlaethau'r dyfodol, ac rwy'n annog pawb i ymweld.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. 90-second Statements
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Last week, I was, along with you and other cross-party colleagues, delighted to welcome Danielle Webb to the Senedd women's caucus. Danielle is an inspirational woman and I am fortunate to call her a friend and know her as a former colleague. As vice-chair of Little People UK, she spoke passionately about her experiences as a little person as part of Dwarfism Awareness Month. She highlighted the everyday challenges that many little people face—as students, when entering employment, commuting or simply navigating spaces that too often fail to accommodate them.

There are between 3,000 and 7,000 people with dwarfism in the UK and over 200 different types of dwarfism. Depending on the condition, people may experience significant medical complications, including spinal stenosis, hydrocephalus and arthritis. Diagnosis and treatment can require genetic testing, scans and x-rays, as well as a co-ordinated team of medical specialists. Dwarfism Awareness Month is an opportunity to challenge misconceptions, raise understanding and confront the barriers that people with dwarfism face every day. We must listen to people like Danielle, champion their experiences and ensure our public spaces, workplaces and services are accessible and inclusive. Greater awareness must be matched by practical action so that people with dwarfism can participate fully in every aspect of life in Wales. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yr wythnos diwethaf, roeddwn i, ynghyd â chi a chyd-Aelodau trawsbleidiol eraill, yn falch iawn o groesawu Danielle Webb i gawcws menywod y Senedd. Mae Danielle yn fenyw ysbrydoledig ac rwy'n ffodus i'w galw'n ffrind a'i hadnabod fel cyn-gydweithiwr. Fel is-gadeirydd Little People UK, siaradodd yn angerddol am ei phrofiadau fel person bach fel rhan o Fis Ymwybyddiaeth Corachedd. Tynnodd sylw at yr heriau y mae llawer o bobl fach yn eu hwynebu bob dydd—fel myfyrwyr, wrth ddechrau cyflogaeth, cymudo neu symud o gwmpas mannau nad ydynt, yn rhy aml, yn darparu ar eu cyfer.

Mae rhwng 3,000 a 7,000 o bobl â chyflwr corachedd yn y DU a dros 200 o wahanol fathau o gyflyrau corachedd. Yn dibynnu ar y cyflwr, gall pobl brofi cymhlethdodau meddygol sylweddol, gan gynnwys stenosis yr asgwrn cefn, hydroseffalws ac arthritis. Gall diagnosis a thriniaeth alw am brofion genetig, sganiau a delweddau pelydr-x, yn ogystal â thîm cydlynol o arbenigwyr meddygol. Mae Mis Ymwybyddiaeth Corachedd yn gyfle i herio camsyniadau, gwella dealltwriaeth ac wynebu'r rhwystrau y mae pobl â chyflyrau corachedd yn eu hwynebu bob dydd. Rhaid inni wrando ar bobl fel Danielle, hyrwyddo eu profiadau a sicrhau bod ein mannau cyhoeddus, ein gweithleoedd a'n gwasanaethau yn hygyrch ac yn gynhwysol. Rhaid i weithredu ymarferol fynd law yn llaw â gwell ymwybyddiaeth er mwyn i bobl â chyflwr corachedd gymryd rhan lawn ym mhob agwedd ar fywyd yng Nghymru. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiadau 90 Eiliad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. 90-second Statements
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Dirprwy Lywydd, this month marks Menopause Awareness Month, and on Sunday just gone, we recognised World Menopause Day. Until recently, when I thought about menopause, I naively pictured what I assume many people do: women of a certain age, hot flushes and many a conversation about the temperature of a room. Perhaps that highlights a lack of appropriate education around menopause growing up. I was wrong, and I'm learning that the hard way.

Menopause can cause chronic pain, but also cognitive and mental health challenges that can affect work, relationships and everyday life. And for women who are neurodivergent, in particular those with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, those changes can bring additional challenges that we need to understand and talk about too. We also need to challenge the assumption that menopause only happens to women of a certain age. I want to take this moment to acknowledge premature ovarian insufficiency, or POI—something I had never heard of until I was diagnosed with it at 36. This coming Sunday marks the second-ever World POI Day, which in itself shows how much more awareness and understanding is still needed.

Dirprwy Lywydd, I'll say it again: this Chamber works best when we use our time to shine a light on aspects of people's lives that too often go under the radar. So, to those living with menopause and POI, you deserve to be listened to, understood and supported. And during my time here, I will do what I can to make sure these experiences are seen, heard and taken seriously. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Ddirprwy Lywydd, mae'n Fis Ymwybyddiaeth Menopos y mis hwn, a ddydd Sul, fe wnaethom gydnabod Diwrnod Menopos y Byd. Tan yn ddiweddar, pan oeddwn yn meddwl am y menopos, roeddwn i'n dychmygu, yn naïf, yr hyn rwy'n tybio y mae llawer o bobl yn ei ddychmygu: menywod o oedran penodol, chwiwiau poeth a llawer o sgyrsiau am dymheredd ystafell. Efallai fod hynny'n tynnu sylw at ddiffyg addysg briodol ynglŷn â'r menopos wrth dyfu i fyny. Roeddwn yn anghywir, ac rwy'n dysgu hynny y ffordd anodd.

Gall y menopos achosi poen cronig, a heriau iechyd gwybyddol a meddyliol hefyd a all effeithio ar waith, perthnasoedd a bywyd bob dydd. Ac i fenywod sy'n niwrowahanol, yn enwedig y rhai sydd ag anhwylder diffyg canolbwyntio a gorfywiogrwydd, gall y newidiadau hynny greu heriau ychwanegol y mae angen inni eu deall a siarad amdanynt. Mae angen inni herio'r rhagdybiaeth mai dim ond menywod o oedran penodol sy'n mynd drwy'r menopos. Hoffwn achub ar y cyfle hwn i gydnabod methiant ofarïaidd cynamserol, neu POI—rhywbeth nad oeddwn erioed wedi clywed amdano hyd nes imi gael diagnosis ohono yn 36 oed. Dydd Sul nesaf yw ail Ddiwrnod POI y Byd erioed, sydd ynddo'i hun yn dangos faint yn rhagor o ymwybyddiaeth a dealltwriaeth sydd ei angen o hyd.

Ddirprwy Lywydd, fe ddywedaf eto: mae'r Siambr hon yn gweithio orau pan fyddwn yn defnyddio ein hamser i daflu goleuni ar agweddau ar fywydau pobl sy'n mynd o dan y radar yn rhy aml. Felly, i'r rhai sy'n byw gyda menopos a POI, rydych chi'n haeddu cael eich clywed, eich deall a'ch cefnogi. Ac yn fy amser yma, fe wnaf bopeth yn fy ngallu i sicrhau bod y profiadau hyn yn cael eu gweld, eu clywed a'u cymryd o ddifrif. Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. I'd like to congratulate Cwm Taf Morgannwg public health team and the Treherbert learning community team, who recently won the inclusion and respect award at this year's Seren awards. Their work forms part of the wider Treherbert initiative, with Grow Rhondda as a key partner. The initiative asked one simple question: what was needed to help people in Treherbert to live healthier lives? This question was taken directly to the people and some clear themes began to emerge: affordable healthy food, mental health support, youth facilities and much more. Importantly, following this, work has started to act on some of these priorities, resulting, for example, in the creation of a low-cost fruit and veg market at Grow Rhondda's cafe, where nothing costs more than £1.50. This shows the importance of working with and listening to a community when looking for concrete actions to improve people's lives. So, congratulations once again to Cwm Taf Morgannwg public health and Treherbert learning community team, and I look forward to seeing what the future holds and what further activities they deliver. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Hoffwn longyfarch tîm iechyd y cyhoedd Cwm Taf Morgannwg a thîm cymuned ddysgu Treherbert, a enillodd y wobr cynhwysiant a pharch yn ddiweddar yng ngwobrau Seren eleni. Mae eu gwaith yn rhan o fenter ehangach Treherbert, gyda Grow Rhondda yn bartner allweddol. Gofynnodd y fenter un cwestiwn syml: beth oedd ei angen i helpu pobl yn Nhreherbert i fyw bywydau iachach? Cyflwynwyd y cwestiwn hwn yn uniongyrchol i'r bobl a daeth rhai themâu clir i'r amlwg: bwyd iach fforddiadwy, cymorth iechyd meddwl, cyfleusterau ieuenctid a llawer mwy. Yn bwysig, yn dilyn hyn, mae gwaith wedi dechrau i weithredu ar rai o'r blaenoriaethau hyn, gan arwain, er enghraifft, at greu marchnad ffrwythau a llysiau rhad yng nghaffi Grow Rhondda, lle nad oes unrhyw beth yn costio mwy na £1.50. Mae hyn yn dangos pwysigrwydd gweithio gyda chymuned a gwrando arni wrth chwilio am gamau gweithredu pendant i wella bywydau pobl. Felly, llongyfarchiadau unwaith eto i dîm iechyd y cyhoedd Cwm Taf Morgannwg a thîm cymuned ddysgu Treherbert, ac edrychaf ymlaen at weld beth sydd gan y dyfodol i'w gynnig a pha weithgareddau pellach y maent yn eu cyflawni. Diolch.

Dwi'n mynd i ofyn i chi a ydych chi'n fodlon trio cwtogi er mwyn bod yn deg i'ch cyd-Aelodau er mwyn i mi drio galw cymaint â dwi'n gallu mewn hanner awr. Galwaf ar Gwyn Williams i wneud y cynnig.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl Ddeddfwriaethol Aelodau o dan Reol Sefydlog 11.21(iv): Bil y GIG yn gyntaf
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Members' Legislative Debate under Standing Order 11.21(iv): An NHS first Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cynnig NDM9275 Gwyn Williams

Cefnogwyd gan Cristiana Emsley, Gareth Beer, Huw Thomas, Jane Dodds, Janet Finch-Saunders, John Davies, Kiera Marshall, Leticia Gonzalez, Lindsay Whittle, Lis McLean, Lyn Ackerman, Mike Hedges, Niamh Salkeld, Nick Carter, Paul Rock, Safa Elhassan, Sarah Cooper-Lesadd, Sera Evans, Shav Taj, Zaynub Akbar

Cynnig bod y Senedd:

1. Yn nodi'r cynnig ar gyfer Bil y GIG yn gyntaf.

2. Yn nodi mai diben y Bil fyddai:

a) cynyddu, lle bynnag y bo'n bosibl, ddarpariaeth meddygfeydd a chlinigau menter rhestr aros yn y GIG yn hytrach na thrwy'r sector preifat;

b) ei gwneud yn ofynnol i bob bwrdd iechyd geisio a datblygu cynlluniau wedi'u costio ar gyfer gweithgareddau clinigol ychwanegol gan adrannau o fewn eu sefydliadau eu hunain cyn llunio contractau gyda darparwyr preifat;

c) sefydlu rhagdybiaeth o blaid cynlluniau a arweinir gan y GIG dros ddarpariaeth y sector preifat mewn ymdrech i leihau rhestrau aros;

d) rhoi awdurdod i arweinwyr clinigol y GIG wrthod cynigion darparwyr preifat pan gânt eu hystyried yn anniogel yn glinigol neu os oes diffyg trefniadau dilynol priodol; ac

e) cyflwyno dyletswydd ar fyrddau iechyd i gyhoeddi data yn dryloyw ar ddefnyddio darpariaeth y sector preifat.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Motion NDM9275 Gwyn Williams

Supported by Cristiana Emsley, Gareth Beer, Huw Thomas, Jane Dodds, Janet Finch-Saunders, John Davies, Kiera Marshall, Leticia Gonzalez, Lindsay Whittle, Lis McLean, Lyn Ackerman, Mike Hedges, Niamh Salkeld, Nick Carter, Paul Rock, Safa Elhassan, Sarah Cooper-Lesadd, Sera Evans, Shav Taj, Zaynub Akbar

To propose that the Senedd:

1. Notes the proposal for an NHS first Bill.

2. Notes that the purpose of the Bill would be to:

a) increase, wherever possible, the delivery of waiting list initiative surgeries and clinics within the NHS, rather than through the private sector;

b) require all health boards to seek and develop costed plans for additional clinical activity from departments within their own organisations before entering into contracts with private providers;

c) establish a presumption in favour of NHS-led plans over private sector provision in efforts to reduce waiting lists;

d) provide NHS clinical leads with the authority to refuse private provider proposals where they are considered clinically unsafe or lack appropriate follow-up arrangements; and

e) introduce a duty on health boards to transparently publish data on the use of private sector provision.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cynigiwyd y cynnig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Motion moved.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl Ddeddfwriaethol Aelodau o dan Reol Sefydlog 11.21(iv): Bil y GIG yn gyntaf
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Members' Legislative Debate under Standing Order 11.21(iv): An NHS first Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr, Ddirprwy Lywydd. This debate, in a nutshell, is, essentially, about putting the NHS first when deciding how to reduce waiting lists, and I'm grateful for the cross-party support on this matter.

I should declare an obvious interest, which you're all expecting me to say anyway, that I'm a consultant eye doctor at Singleton Hospital in Swansea. I've worked in the NHS for 23 years as a doctor and 10 as a consultant. I believe in the NHS, work in the NHS, and I've seen the problems and opportunities first-hand. Our clinicians know their patients, they know the hospitals and, more importantly, they know the systems that they work in. We should give them the opportunity to put forward plans for reducing waiting lists before asking private providers if they can do so. And this is not party political, or at least it shouldn't be.

I believe we all want people across Wales to receive safe, timely care. We want waiting lists to fall and we want public money to deliver the greatest possible benefits for our patients. So, what does this proposal ask for? Three things: to favour NHS-led provision; to give clinical leads the power to reject unsafe private proposals or inadequate follow-up arrangements; and to demand transparent publication of data on private provision from every health board. And why? Because I believe that putting the NHS first can help us deliver safer care, work more efficiently and make better use of NHS money. And I will take each one of these things in turn.

Deliver safer care. One appointment or a surgery is only one part of the process in a patient's diagnosis and treatment journey. It isn't, and, indeed, can't be, a stand-alone thing. Likewise, an operation also. What happens afterwards matters too, and, indeed, before, with listing and pre assessment. It's obviously not hugely safe to send one link of this chain to an unfamiliar provider and then the patient is returned. Clinicians all over Wales can speak about experiences, for example, with patients returning to the NHS with some form of complication following a cataract operation, for example, privately via outsourcing. These complications can and should require urgent treatment, which then takes priority over elective cases, such as macula hole repairs. The proposed legislation would give clinical leads the authority to refuse private arrangements they consider unsafe or which lack appropriate follow-up care. The people responsible for patients' care must have a say in how that care is provided—the people who mop up the mess.

Secondly, to work more efficiently. Local NHS teams know the patients, the department and the systems, yet decisions to outsource or insource work to companies can be taken several levels above them, before they have the opportunity to offer an in-house solution. Oftentimes, if the patients are not known to the company clinicians, who also can't access records and are not responsible for follow-up—we don't have an electronic patient record all around Wales, for example—decisions are deferred, as it is merely an exercise in kicking the can down the road to make the figures look temporarily better. But it always catches up worse than before. I'm a fan of the HBO miniseries Chernobyl, where Professor Valery Legasov says,

'Every lie we tell incurs a debt to the truth. Sooner or later that debt is paid.'

And when is that? When the contract ends in this case.

This proposal would require health boards to seek the development of those solutions first: additional waiting list initiative clinics and operating lists within the NHS, planned by the teams who understand the service. And we also need to consider the effect on our workforce. When clinicians cut their NHS hours to do more private-provider work, which does remunerate better, it has to be said, the private sector grows and the NHS capacity atrophies. We become more dependent on the very provision that is drawing our staff away, and we're, in fact, paying to drain the very service we need to strengthen. If an NHS team cannot undertake all the additional work, private provision would remain an option. This proposed Bill would merely establish a presumption in favour of NHS-led plans.

Thirdly, to make better use of public money, if indeed we do put the NHS first. Private contracts use public money. I think Mabon recently quoted £1.5 million that was spent over the past few years on outsourcing. That money used in an NHS setting would have helped develop services and make a permanent improvement to departments all over Wales. We need to appreciate and understand the full cost of the contracts, including follow-up, complications and any work that then returns to NHS services.

Cataracts, for example—obviously, I'm biased towards cataracts—[Laughter.]—are not undertaken and simply sent back. Complications are needing extra surgery, appointments in eye casualty, as well as administrative problems caused by one eye being operated on privately via outsourcing and the other eye falling through the cracks, which is a terrible image. [Laughter.]

Health boards should publish transparent data on their use of private provision so we can see what has been purchased and assess what it delivers. And why does this matter to constituents across Wales? Because behind every waiting list figure is a person waiting for treatment. They need safe care, timely treatment, and confidence that someone will take responsibility for their follow-up. The decision we make today affects the NHS's ability to treat patients tomorrow. We need to reduce waiting lists while strengthening the service people will continue to depend on.

And why does this matter to me personally? Because this is why I'm here. This is why I came into this job and why I sit in this chair: to give the clinicians delivering care the opportunity to put forward solutions. We have an opportunity to put NHS capacity, clinical judgment and accountability at the centre of decisions about waiting lists—not an expensive, unsafe, can-kicking, sticking-plaster exercise that erodes the health service upon which we depend. Let's stand up for the NHS. Let's put the NHS first. Let's show the people of Wales that we take their safety, their waiting times and their public money seriously, by giving the people who know the patients and deliver their care the opportunity to lead. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Mae'r ddadl hon, yn gryno, yn ymwneud â rhoi'r GIG yn gyntaf wrth benderfynu sut i leihau rhestrau aros, ac rwy'n ddiolchgar am y gefnogaeth drawsbleidiol ar y mater hwn.

Dylwn ddatgan buddiant amlwg, fel rydych chi i gyd yn disgwyl i mi ei wneud beth bynnag, fy mod i'n feddyg llygaid ymgynghorol yn Ysbyty Singleton yn Abertawe. Rwyf wedi gweithio yn y GIG ers 23 mlynedd fel meddyg a 10 fel meddyg ymgynghorol. Rwy'n credu yn y GIG, yn gweithio yn y GIG, ac rwyf wedi gweld y problemau a'r cyfleoedd yn uniongyrchol. Mae ein clinigwyr yn adnabod eu cleifion, maent yn adnabod yr ysbytai ac yn bwysicach fyth, maent yn adnabod y systemau y maent yn gweithio ynddynt. Dylem roi cyfle iddynt gyflwyno cynlluniau ar gyfer lleihau rhestrau aros cyn gofyn i ddarparwyr preifat wneud hynny. Ac nid mater o wleidyddiaeth plaid yw hyn, neu o leiaf nid dyna ddylai fod.

Rwy'n credu ein bod ni i gyd eisiau i bobl ledled Cymru gael gofal diogel ac amserol. Rydym eisiau i restrau aros leihau ac rydym eisiau i arian cyhoeddus ddarparu'r buddion mwyaf posibl i'n cleifion. Felly, am beth y mae'r cynnig hwn yn gofyn? Tri pheth: ffafrio darpariaeth dan arweiniad y GIG; rhoi pŵer i arweinwyr clinigol wrthod cynigion preifat anniogel neu drefniadau dilynol annigonol; a mynnu bod pob bwrdd iechyd yn cyhoeddi data ar ddarpariaeth breifat. A pham? Oherwydd rwy'n credu y gall rhoi'r GIG yn gyntaf ein helpu i ddarparu gofal mwy diogel, gweithio'n fwy effeithlon a gwneud gwell defnydd o arian y GIG. Ac fe roddaf sylw i bob un o'r pethau hyn yn eu tro.

Darparu gofal mwy diogel. Dim ond un rhan o'r broses yn nhaith diagnosis a thriniaeth claf yw un apwyntiad neu lawdriniaeth. Nid yw, ac yn wir, ni all fod, yn rhywbeth sy'n sefyll ar ei ben ei hun. Yn yr un modd, ni all llawdriniaeth wneud hynny chwaith. Mae'r hyn sy'n digwydd wedyn yn bwysig hefyd, a chynt yn wir, gyda rhestru ac asesiadau cyn llawdriniaeth. Mae'n amlwg nad yw'n hynod ddiogel i anfon un ddolen o'r gadwyn hon at ddarparwr anghyfarwydd a bod y claf yn cael ei ddychwelyd wedyn. Gall clinigwyr ledled Cymru siarad am brofiadau, er enghraifft, gyda chleifion yn dychwelyd i'r GIG gyda rhyw fath o gymhlethdod yn dilyn llawdriniaeth gataract, er enghraifft, yn breifat trwy gontract allanol. Fe all ac fe ddylai'r cymhlethdodau hyn alw am driniaeth frys, sydd wedyn yn cael blaenoriaeth dros achosion a gynlluniwyd, fel atgyweirio twll y macwla. Byddai'r ddeddfwriaeth arfaethedig yn rhoi awdurdod i arweinwyr clinigol wrthod trefniadau preifat y maent yn eu hystyried yn anniogel neu lle nad oes ganddynt ofal dilynol priodol. Rhaid i'r bobl sy'n gyfrifol am ofal cleifion gael llais yn y ffordd y caiff y gofal hwnnw ei ddarparu—y bobl sy'n clirio'r llanast.

Yn ail, gweithio'n fwy effeithlon. Mae timau GIG lleol yn adnabod y cleifion, yr adran a'r systemau, ond mae penderfyniadau i allanoli gwaith i gwmnïau'n gallu cael eu gwneud sawl lefel uwch eu pennau, cyn iddynt gael cyfle i gynnig ateb mewnol. Yn aml, os nad yw clinigwyr y cwmni'n adnabod y cleifion, ac na allant gael mynediad at gofnodion ac nad ydynt yn gyfrifol am ofal dilynol—nid oes gennym gofnod electronig am gleifion ledled Cymru, er enghraifft—mae penderfyniadau'n cael eu gohirio er mwyn gwneud i'r ffigurau edrych yn well dros dro. Ond mae bob amser yn dal i fyny'n waeth nag o'r blaen. Rwy'n hoff o gyfres HBO Chernobyl, lle mae'r Athro Valery Legasov yn dweud,

'Mae pob celwydd a ddywedwn yn creu dyled i'r gwir. Yn hwyr neu'n hwyrach mae'r ddyled honno'n cael ei thalu.'

A phryd y digwydd hynny? Pan ddaw'r contract i ben yn yr achos hwn.

Byddai'r cynnig hwn yn ei gwneud yn ofynnol i fyrddau iechyd geisio datblygu'r atebion hynny yn gyntaf: clinigau ychwanegol i'r cynllun rhestrau aros a rhestrau llawdriniaethau o fewn y GIG, wedi'u cynllunio gan y timau sy'n deall y gwasanaeth. Ac mae angen inni ystyried yr effaith ar ein gweithlu hefyd. Pan fydd clinigwyr yn torri eu horiau GIG i wneud mwy o waith darparwr preifat, sy'n talu'n well, rhaid dweud, mae'r sector preifat yn tyfu ac mae capasiti'r GIG yn crebachu. Down yn fwy dibynnol ar yr union ddarpariaeth sy'n mynd â'n staff, ac mewn gwirionedd, rydym yn talu i ddraenio'r union wasanaeth y mae angen i ni ei gryfhau. Os na all tîm y GIG gyflawni'r holl waith ychwanegol, byddai darpariaeth breifat yn parhau i fod yn opsiwn. Byddai'r Bil arfaethedig hwn ond yn sefydlu rhagdybiaeth o blaid cynlluniau dan arweiniad y GIG.

Yn drydydd, gwneud gwell defnydd o arian cyhoeddus, os yn wir ein bod yn rhoi'r GIG yn gyntaf. Mae contractau preifat yn defnyddio arian cyhoeddus. Rwy'n credu bod Mabon yn ddiweddar wedi dweud bod £1.5 miliwn wedi'i wario dros y blynyddoedd diwethaf ar gontractau allanol. Byddai'r arian hwnnw o'i ddefnyddio mewn lleoliad GIG wedi helpu i ddatblygu gwasanaethau a gwneud gwelliant parhaol i adrannau ledled Cymru. Mae angen inni werthfawrogi a deall cost lawn y contractau, gan gynnwys trefniadau dilynol, cymhlethdodau ac unrhyw waith sy'n dychwelyd i wasanaethau'r GIG wedyn.

Nid yw cataractau, er enghraifft—yn amlwg, rwy'n rhagfarnu o blaid cataractau—[Chwerthin.]—yn cael eu gwneud a chânt eu hanfon yn ôl. Mae angen llawdriniaeth ychwanegol ar gymhlethdodau, apwyntiadau mewn adrannau anafiadau llygaid, yn ogystal â phroblemau gweinyddol a achosir gan un llygad yn cael llawdriniaeth breifat trwy gontract allanol a'r llygad arall yn disgyn drwy'r rhwyd, sy'n ddelwedd ofnadwy. [Chwerthin.]

Dylai byrddau iechyd gyhoeddi data tryloyw ar eu defnydd o ddarpariaeth breifat fel y gallwn weld beth sydd wedi'i brynu ac asesu'r hyn y mae'n ei ddarparu. A pham y mae hyn yn bwysig i etholwyr ledled Cymru? Oherwydd y tu ôl i bob ffigur rhestr aros mae unigolyn sy'n aros am driniaeth. Mae angen gofal diogel arnynt, triniaeth amserol, a hyder y bydd rhywun yn ysgwyddo cyfrifoldeb am eu gofal dilynol. Mae'r penderfyniad a wnawn heddiw yn effeithio ar allu'r GIG i drin cleifion yfory. Mae angen inni leihau rhestrau aros gan gryfhau'r gwasanaeth y bydd pobl yn parhau i ddibynnu arno.

A pham y mae hyn yn bwysig i mi'n bersonol? Am mai dyna pam fy mod i yma. Dyma pam y deuthum i'r swydd hon a pham rwy'n eistedd yn y gadair hon: i roi cyfle i'r clinigwyr sy'n darparu gofal gynnig atebion. Mae gennym gyfle i roi capasiti, barn glinigol ac atebolrwydd y GIG wrth wraidd penderfyniadau ynghylch rhestrau aros—nid ymarfer drud, anniogel sy'n gohirio, plastr dros dro, sy'n erydu'r gwasanaeth iechyd rydym yn dibynnu arno. Gadewch inni sefyll dros y GIG. Gadewch inni roi'r GIG yn gyntaf. Gadewch inni ddangos i bobl Cymru ein bod o ddifrif ynghylch eu diogelwch, eu hamseroedd aros a'u harian cyhoeddus, drwy roi cyfle i'r bobl sy'n adnabod y cleifion ac sy'n darparu eu gofal i arwain. Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl Ddeddfwriaethol Aelodau o dan Reol Sefydlog 11.21(iv): Bil y GIG yn gyntaf
