XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Reform UK Debate: Prostate cancer strategy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
And then Paul Davies—and thank you, Paul, for giving your own personal experience. You and I have talked a lot about this in the past, about your own personal experience of living with prostate cancer and the need to include it within that cancer strategy. That's something that we need to see, because it is the biggest killer of men in terms of cancer. We do need to make sure that it is included. You also raised the consultation, and we all need to see that, if consultations are had by Government, then the lived experience of people has to come through that consultation. It can't just be a tick-box exercise, as you raised. It actually needs to be considered and thought out. You also raised, and I know you've been a real champion for it, the national screening programme, when it was first discussed, and then the UK screening committee decided not to roll it out. I know that you were deeply disappointed about that, like a lot of others, and I'd just like to thank you for the work you've done, not just in this Parliament but in other Parliaments across the UK, to understand why that screening programme should be happening. You also talked about the advances in medical technology as well, and that men in Wales should have access to that technology and not outdated technology, and that was picked up a little bit by the Cabinet Minister.

Matthew, your commitment to cancer is unmatched, really, in this Chamber. You worked for a number of cancer charities before you even came to this place, and now you're chairman of the cross-party group on cancer. As someone who's been here before, I can say that that cross-party group does an awful lot of very good work, and it's informed a lot of the work of the cancer strategy over the years as well. So thank you for that. You talked about the excitement that there is amongst a number of third sector bodies and our charities about a cancer strategy, something that a number of us have been shouting about for a long time to have, so it's positive that that is coming forward. You raised the cancer pathways as well, and the delays that some people are experiencing through those pathways. I'm sure that's something that the Government will take heed of from your cross-party group as well, to see how we can improve, not just for prostate cancer but all cancers, to improve the pathways.

Ken Skates then opened with his support for the motion. I will give credit to the last Government—I don't give them credit much—for the new Velindre cancer care centre. [Interruption.] You can keep rolling your hand, Ken, but that's as far as it's going. And the work it did with the new cancer centre in Nevill Hall Hospital, the Velindre cancer centre there, and just how that's opened up so many more avenues to get care closer to home. I know the new Cabinet Minister has been there, and I've also been there in a personal capacity with a family member. I know just how important that centre is for so many people. He also talked about the strategy being evidence led by stuff that's going on at a UK level. I think that was really important to highlight.

Adrian, you raised your personal experience, like a lot of others did, with cancer, and that a lot of men don't seek out help. That's something that we do see across men's health across the country. A lot of people don't seek help with their own health problems, they just tend to deal with it quietly, and they don't go to the GP, and they don't go for tests. They just put it in a box somewhere and say, 'We won't talk about it'. I think that's really important. You also raised screening, and that the Welsh Government here should follow the advice as it develops. You also mentioned the support that can be given to patients and their families. I think that's really important.

Janet, thank you very much. I know about your personal experience. As you said, you and I have also talked about that a lot. You raised the point that 40 per cent of people are only caught at stage 3 and 4, which is an absolutely shocking statistic. It's coming well too late. That's probably one of the worst out of all the cancers, actually, except some of our rarer cancers. And you, like others, raised the screening programme as well. So I'm sure the Cabinet Minister has heard that, that a lot of us in this Chamber want that. 

Gareth, you said that cancer can affect everyone, and that men in deprived areas are actually more likely to get diagnosed later than those in more affluent areas, and that's something about health inequalities, which the health committee have looked at on a number of occasions, and how we do need to make sure there is that health equality across Wales, without detriment to anyone in any part of the country. And the postcode lottery—I don't know how many times the Cabinet Minister and I have both heard that before, and others in this Chamber, about how where you live across Wales can really decide how your outcomes and prognosis look, which is also shocking.

Elwyn Vaughan talked about people who live in rural areas. You and I and a lot of others share this as well, about the barriers we face to diagnosis. You talked about the farming community especially. Just raising something from my own community, Shearing is Caring raised an awful lot of money for Prostate Cymru, and that's about the farming community and getting men talking more about their health. You talked about the link with the Farming Community Network at Macmillan. I'll give a shameless plug now that I'm running a Hyrox race next week for Macmillan. So if anybody wants to sponsor me, I'm still taking sponsorship. You also talked about the Welsh Government's plan for the rapid diagnostic centre in Powys. I don't agree with Plaid Cymru on much, but I think this could actually be an area where I think it's really positive for the people who live in rural areas, especially in Powys.

Helen Jenner spoke about her own personal experience in her own family, and I think it's very important that people do talk about their personal experience. I think it's something that really shapes a parliamentary democracy, that we've got people in here who actually do understand the issue, that have got family going through it. You also said about your father not wanting to worry people. How many times have we heard that with men who are going through a diagnosis? ‘I'm just not going to tell my family.’ I've even known people who've passed away from cancer, and their own family don't even know why they've passed away until after, because it's been hidden from them, because they just don't want them to worry. So, making sure that men talk more is important. You also raised the data and the years of missed targets, and I think that's something that the Cabinet Minister needs to reflect on, and perhaps other Members in the Chamber who were in Government before, that actually this is a historical issue and a historical injustice that really does need to be sorted.

Then we moved on to our Cabinet Minister, and I do not pretend that you're not showing commitment to this area. I know you and I have worked closely in the past on cancer pathways and improving cancer care across Wales, so I don't doubt your commitment to that. As you said, cancer is the leading cause of death for men in Wales. It's still too high, and it needs to be addressed. As I said earlier, you talked about us wanting to be the best in Europe. I want us to be the best in the world when it comes to addressing cancer, especially prostate cancer. We're a small nation that spends an awful lot of our public money on the health service. For the money we put into it, we actually get a pretty poor return. Making that money work better to get better outcomes for the people of Wales, and especially men struggling with prostate cancer, is really important.

You also talked about the Welsh Government wanting new technologies and tests. I know there are new lung screening tests that are coming through, but there are new tests coming through as well for prostate cancer, and it would be really good if Wales could be a leading partner with charities and with the university institutions to develop these new technologies so people can get seen quicker.

You mentioned screening. Something I haven't heard before, actually, is the commitment from the Government—that they've asked Public Health Wales to look at the screening. It's perhaps not as wide as some Members want, but it's screening for perhaps a portion of the population who are at higher risk of getting prostate cancer.

The clock has now gone red, but I'm going to make another shameless plug. It's something that I've always been very keen on. It was something in our manifesto—a proper men's health strategy for Wales. I think that is something that is needed. Prostate cancer is a leading cause of death in men, but there are also a lot of other health areas that need to be addressed for our men across the country. We don't talk about it often enough, and I think that's something that the Government should take into serious consideration—a proper men's health strategy for Wales to address the health inequalities of a number of men across our country. I urge all Members to support our motion this afternoon. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Ac yna Paul Davies—a diolch, Paul, am rannu eich profiad personol. Rydych chi a minnau wedi siarad llawer am hyn yn y gorffennol, am eich profiad personol o fyw gyda chanser y prostad a'r angen i'w gynnwys yn y strategaeth ganser honno. Mae hynny'n rhywbeth y mae angen inni ei weld, gan mai dyma'r canser sy'n lladd y nifer fwyaf o ddynion. Mae angen inni sicrhau ei fod wedi'i gynnwys yn y strategaeth. Fe wnaethoch chi grybwyll yr ymgynghoriad hefyd, ac mae angen i bob un ohonom sicrhau, os bydd y Llywodraeth yn cynnal ymgynghoriad, fod rhaid cynnwys profiad bywyd pobl yn yr ymgynghoriad hwnnw. Ni all fod yn ymarfer ticio blychau'n unig, fel y nodoch chi. Mae angen ei ystyried yn iawn. Fe wnaethoch chi hefyd grybwyll y rhaglen sgrinio genedlaethol, a gwn eich bod wedi bod yn hyrwyddwr go iawn drosti, pan gafodd ei thrafod gyntaf, ac yna penderfynodd pwyllgor sgrinio'r DU beidio â'i chyflwyno. Gwn eich bod wedi'ch siomi'n fawr gan hynny, fel llawer o bobl eraill, a hoffwn ddiolch i chi am y gwaith a wnaethoch, nid yn unig yn y Senedd hon ond mewn Seneddau eraill ledled y DU, i ddeall pam y dylai'r rhaglen sgrinio honno fod ar waith. Fe sonioch chi hefyd am y datblygiadau mewn technoleg feddygol, ac y dylai dynion yng Nghymru gael mynediad at y dechnoleg honno ac nid technoleg sydd wedi dyddio, a chafodd hynny ei ategu i raddau gan y Gweinidog Cabinet.

Matthew, mae eich ymrwymiad i ganser yn ddihafal yn y Siambr hon. Fe fuoch chi'n gweithio i nifer o elusennau canser cyn i chi ddod i'r lle hwn, a nawr, rydych chi'n gadeirydd y grŵp trawsbleidiol ar ganser. Fel rhywun sydd wedi bod yma, gallaf ddweud bod y grŵp trawsbleidiol hwnnw'n gwneud llawer iawn o waith da iawn, ac mae wedi llywio llawer o waith y strategaeth ganser dros y blynyddoedd hefyd. Felly, diolch am hynny. Fe sonioch chi am y cyffro ymhlith nifer o gyrff y trydydd sector a'n helusennau ynghylch strategaeth ganser, rhywbeth y mae nifer ohonom wedi bod yn gweiddi amdano ers amser maith, felly mae'n gadarnhaol fod honno'n cael ei chyflwyno. Fe godoch chi'r llwybrau canser hefyd, a'r oedi y mae rhai pobl yn ei wynebu drwy'r llwybrau hynny. Rwy'n siŵr bod hynny'n rhywbeth y bydd y Llywodraeth yn ei ystyried oddi wrth eich grŵp trawsbleidiol hefyd, i weld sut y gallwn wella, nid yn unig ar gyfer canser y prostad, ond pob canser, i wella'r llwybrau.

Yna agorodd Ken Skates gyda'i gefnogaeth i'r cynnig. Rwyf am roi clod i'r Llywodraeth ddiwethaf—nid wyf yn rhoi llawer o glod iddynt—am ganolfan gofal canser newydd Felindre. [Torri ar draws.] Gallwch barhau i chwifio'ch llaw, Ken, ond dyna pa mor bell y mae'r clod yn mynd. A'r gwaith a wnaeth gyda'r ganolfan ganser newydd yn Ysbyty Nevill Hall, y ganolfan ganser Felindre yno, a sut y mae hynny wedi agor cymaint yn fwy o lwybrau i gael gofal yn nes at adref. Gwn fod y Gweinidog Cabinet newydd wedi bod yno, ac rwyf innau wedi bod yno gydag aelod o'r teulu. Gwn pa mor bwysig yw'r ganolfan honno i gynifer o bobl. Soniodd hefyd am y strategaeth a gaiff ei harwain gan dystiolaeth drwy bethau sy'n digwydd ar lefel y DU. Rwy'n credu bod hynny'n bwysig iawn i'w nodi.

Adrian, fe sonioch chi am eich profiad personol, fel y gwnaeth llawer o Aelodau eraill, gyda chanser, a'r ffaith bod yna lawer o ddynion nad ydynt yn ceisio cymorth. Mae hynny'n rhywbeth a welwn ar draws iechyd dynion ledled y wlad. Mae llawer o bobl nad ydynt yn ceisio cymorth gyda'u problemau iechyd eu hunain, maent yn tueddu i ddelio â'r peth yn dawel, ac nid ydynt yn mynd at y meddyg teulu, ac nid ydynt yn mynd am brofion. Maent yn ei roi mewn blwch yn rhywle ac yn dweud, 'Wnawn ni ddim siarad am y peth'. Rwy'n credu bod hynny'n bwysig iawn. Fe sonioch chi am sgrinio hefyd, a dweud y dylai Llywodraeth Cymru ddilyn y cyngor wrth iddo ddatblygu. Fe sonioch chi hefyd am y cymorth y gellir ei roi i gleifion a'u teuluoedd. Rwy'n credu bod hynny'n bwysig iawn.

Janet, diolch yn fawr iawn. Gwn am eich profiad personol. Fel y dywedoch chi, rydym ninnau'n dau wedi siarad llawer am hynny hefyd. Fe godoch chi'r pwynt fod 40 y cant o achosion o ganser y prostad ond yn cael eu dal yng nghamau 3 a 4, sy'n ystadegyn cwbl frawychus. Mae'n digwydd yn llawer rhy hwyr. Mae'n debyg mai dyna un o'r rhai gwaethaf o ran hynny o'r holl ganserau mewn gwirionedd, ac eithrio rhai o'n canserau mwyaf prin. Ac fe wnaethoch chi sôn, fel y gwnaeth eraill, am y rhaglen sgrinio. Felly, rwy'n siŵr bod y Gweinidog Cabinet wedi clywed hynny, fod llawer ohonom yn y Siambr hon eisiau hynny.

Gareth, fe ddywedoch chi y gall canser effeithio ar bawb, a bod dynion mewn ardaloedd difreintiedig yn fwy tebygol o gael diagnosis yn hwyrach na'r rheini mewn ardaloedd mwy cyfoethog, ac mae hynny'n dweud rhywbeth am anghydraddoldebau iechyd, y mae'r pwyllgor iechyd wedi edrych arnynt ar nifer o achlysuron, a sut y mae angen inni sicrhau y ceir cydraddoldeb iechyd ledled Cymru, heb greu anfantais i unrhyw un mewn unrhyw ran o'r wlad. A'r loteri cod post—nid wyf yn gwybod sawl gwaith y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet a minnau wedi clywed hynny o'r blaen, ac eraill yn y Siambr hon, ynglŷn â sut y gall ble rydych chi'n byw yng Nghymru benderfynu eich canlyniadau a'ch prognosis, sydd hefyd yn frawychus.

Siaradodd Elwyn Vaughan am bobl sy'n byw mewn ardaloedd gwledig. Rydych chi a minnau a llawer o bobl eraill yn rhannu hyn hefyd, y rhwystrau a wynebwn i ddiagnosis. Fe sonioch chi am y gymuned ffermio yn benodol. I nodi rhywbeth yn fy nghymuned fy hun, cododd Shearing is Caring lawer iawn o arian i Prostate Cymru, ac mae a wnelo hynny â'r gymuned ffermio ac annog dynion i siarad mwy am eu hiechyd. Fe sonioch chi am y cysylltiad â Farming Community Network yn Macmillan. Rwyf am roi hysbysiad digywilydd nawr fy mod yn rhedeg ras Hyrox yr wythnos nesaf i Macmillan. Felly os oes unrhyw un eisiau fy noddi, rwy'n dal i gasglu noddwyr. Fe sonioch chi hefyd am gynllun Llywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer y ganolfan ddiagnosis cyflym ym Mhowys. Nid wyf yn cytuno â Phlaid Cymru ar lawer, ond rwy'n credu y gallai hwn fod yn faes gwirioneddol gadarnhaol i'r bobl sy'n byw mewn ardaloedd gwledig, yn enwedig ym Mhowys.

Soniodd Helen Jenner am ei phrofiad personol yn ei theulu ei hun, a chredaf ei bod yn bwysig iawn fod pobl yn siarad am eu profiad personol. Rwy'n credu ei fod yn rhywbeth sy'n rhoi siâp i ddemocratiaeth seneddol, fod gennym bobl yma sy'n deall y mater, sydd â theulu yn mynd drwyddo. Fe ddywedoch chi hefyd nad oedd eich tad eisiau peri gofid i bobl. Sawl gwaith y clywsom hynny gan ddynion sy'n mynd drwy ddiagnosis? 'Nid wyf am ddweud wrth fy nheulu.' Rwyf hyd yn oed wedi adnabod pobl a fu farw o ganser, nad oedd eu teulu eu hunain yn gwybod pam eu bod wedi marw tan ar ôl iddynt farw, am eu bod wedi'i guddio oddi wrthynt, rhag gwneud iddynt boeni. Felly, mae'n bwysig sicrhau bod dynion yn siarad mwy. Fe wnaethoch chi nodi'r data a'r blynyddoedd o dargedau a fethwyd hefyd, a chredaf fod hynny'n rhywbeth y mae angen i'r Gweinidog Cabinet fyfyrio arno, ac Aelodau eraill yn y Siambr a oedd yn arfer bod yn y Llywodraeth, fod hwn mewn gwirionedd yn fater hanesyddol ac yn anghyfiawnder hanesyddol y mae gwir angen ei ddatrys.

Yna, fe wnaethom symud ymlaen at ein Gweinidog Cabinet, ac nid wyf am esgus nad ydych chi'n dangos ymrwymiad i'r maes hwn. Gwn eich bod chi a ninnau wedi gweithio'n agos yn y gorffennol ar lwybrau canser a gwella gofal canser ledled Cymru, felly nid wyf yn amau eich ymrwymiad i hynny. Fel y dywedoch chi, canser yw prif achos marwolaeth ymhlith dynion yng Nghymru. Mae'n dal i fod yn rhy uchel, ac mae angen mynd i'r afael â hynny. Fel y dywedais yn gynharach, fe sonioch chi ein bod eisiau bod y gorau yn Ewrop. Rwyf eisiau inni fod y gorau yn y byd o ran mynd i'r afael â chanser, yn enwedig canser y prostad. Rydym yn genedl fach sy'n gwario llawer iawn o'n harian cyhoeddus ar y gwasanaeth iechyd. Am yr arian a roddwn iddo, mae'r enillion a gawn yn eithaf gwael mewn gwirionedd. Mae gwneud i'r arian hwnnw weithio'n well i gael gwell canlyniadau i bobl Cymru, ac yn enwedig dynion â chanser y prostad, yn bwysig iawn.

Fe ddywedoch chi hefyd fod Llywodraeth Cymru eisiau technolegau a phrofion newydd. Gwn fod profion sgrinio newydd i'w cael ar gyfer yr ysgyfaint, ond mae profion newydd i'w cael ar gyfer canser y prostad hefyd, a byddai'n dda iawn pe gallai Cymru fod yn bartner blaenllaw gydag elusennau a chyda'r sefydliadau prifysgol i ddatblygu'r technolegau newydd hyn fel y gellir gweld pobl yn gyflymach.

Fe sonioch chi am sgrinio. Rhywbeth nad wyf wedi'i glywed o'r blaen mewn gwirionedd yw'r ymrwymiad gan y Llywodraeth—eu bod wedi gofyn i Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru edrych ar y sgrinio. Efallai nad yw mor eang ag y byddai rhai Aelodau yn ei ddymuno, ond mae'n wasanaeth sgrinio ar gyfer cyfran o'r boblogaeth a allai wynebu mwy o risg o gael canser y prostad.

Mae'r cloc wedi troi'n goch nawr, ond rwy’n mynd i roi cais digywilydd arall. Mae'n rhywbeth rwyf wedi bod yn awyddus iawn i'w weld. Roedd yn ein maniffesto—strategaeth iechyd dynion go iawn i Gymru. Credaf fod hynny'n rhywbeth sydd ei angen. Mae canser y prostad yn un o brif achosion marwolaeth ymhlith dynion, ond mae llawer o feysydd iechyd eraill hefyd y mae angen mynd i'r afael â nhw ar ran ein dynion ledled y wlad. Nid ydym yn siarad amdano'n ddigon aml, ac rwy'n credu bod hynny'n rhywbeth y dylai'r Llywodraeth ei ystyried o ddifrif—strategaeth iechyd dynion go iawn i Gymru i fynd i'r afael ag anghydraddoldebau iechyd nifer o ddynion ledled ein gwlad. Rwy'n annog pob Aelod i gefnogi ein cynnig y prynhawn yma. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cynnig NDM9335 Lynne Neagle

Cynnig bod y Senedd:

1. Yn credu bod cynigion Llywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer lliniaru tagfeydd ar yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd yn annigonol.

2. Yn galw ar Lywodraeth Cymru i:

a) diystyru cau cyffyrdd; a

b) dechrau ar y gwaith o adeiladu ffordd liniaru briodol ar gyfer yr M4.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Motion NDM9335 Lynne Neagle

To propose that the Senedd:

1. Believes that the Welsh Government’s proposals for the relief of congestion on the M4 around Newport are inadequate.

2. Calls on the Welsh Government to:

a) rule out junction closures; and

b) begin work on an appropriate relief road for the M4.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. Newport is the city where I was born, grew up in, and live in, and I speak today as part of a group of Welsh Labour Senedd Members who know that this issue has gone unresolved for far too long. You do not need to live locally to know that the M4 around Newport is broken. Sadly, the Brynglas tunnels have become synonymous with gridlock. The vast majority of M4 traffic is not local, but the motorway was never designed to carry the weight of a modern national economy. This stretch of road is the main gateway to south and west Wales. It is critical to our industries, both established and emerging, our ports and our tourism, yet it bisects a growing city.

While congestion on this stretch of the M4 puts a handbrake on economic growth, it is the people of Newport who pay the price every single day with air pollution, which is a silent killer. Welsh Labour has laid this motion today because the people of Newport and connected communities in Cwmbran, Torfaen and Caerphilly have had enough. These communities are not some theoretical testbed, and the Plaid Cymru Welsh Government is toying with costly and ineffective proposals that will wreak havoc on people's lives.

Let's take the Government's serious proposals to close junctions. Fully closing High Cross and the eastbound slips at Malpas and Caerleon is not a quick fix. The Welsh Government's own report shows that it would only take up to 3 per cent of traffic off the motorway. Not everyone can work from home, and junction closures, whether temporary or permanent, would also affect public transport, access to healthcare, childcare and property prices. It's astounding that the Government is even considering this.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Casnewydd yw'r ddinas lle cefais fy ngeni, fy magu, a lle rwy'n byw, ac rwy'n siarad heddiw fel rhan o grŵp o Aelodau Senedd Llafur Cymru sy'n gwybod bod y mater hwn heb ei ddatrys ers gormod o amser. Nid oes angen ichi fyw'n lleol i wybod bod rhywbeth o'i le gyda'r M4 o amgylch Casnewydd. Yn anffodus, mae twnelau Bryn-glas wedi dod yn gyfystyr â thagfeydd. Nid yw'r mwyafrif helaeth o draffig yr M4 yn draffig lleol, ond ni chafodd y draffordd ei chynllunio i ysgwyddo pwysau economi genedlaethol fodern. Y darn hwn o ffordd yw'r prif borth i dde a gorllewin Cymru. Mae'n allweddol i'n diwydiannau, y rhai sefydledig a'r rhai newydd, ein porthladdoedd a'n twristiaeth, ond eto mae'n hollti dinas sy'n tyfu.

Er bod tagfeydd ar y darn hwn o'r M4 yn rhwystro twf economaidd, pobl Casnewydd sy'n talu'r pris bob dydd drwy lygredd aer, sy'n lladdwr tawel. Mae Llafur Cymru wedi cyflwyno'r cynnig hwn heddiw am fod pobl Casnewydd a chymunedau cysylltiedig yng Nghwmbrân, Torfaen a Chaerffili wedi cael digon. Nid rhyw fath o arbrawf damcaniaethol yw'r cymunedau hyn, ac mae Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru yn chwarae gyda chynigion costus ac aneffeithiol a fydd yn achosi anhrefn ym mywydau pobl.

Gadewch inni ystyried cynigion y Llywodraeth i gau cyffyrdd. Nid yw cau High Cross yn llwyr a'r slipffyrdd tua'r dwyrain ym Malpas a Chaerllion yn ateb cyflym. Mae adroddiad Llywodraeth Cymru ei hun yn dangos na fyddai ond yn mynd â hyd at 3 y cant o draffig oddi ar y draffordd. Ni all pawb weithio o gartref, a byddai cau cyffyrdd, boed dros dro neu'n barhaol, hefyd yn effeithio ar drafnidiaeth gyhoeddus, mynediad at ofal iechyd, gofal plant a phrisiau eiddo. Mae'n syfrdanol fod y Llywodraeth hyd yn oed yn ystyried hyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
When I asked the Deputy Minister how the remaining junctions at Tredegar Park and the Coldra would cope with the displaced traffic, he had no answer, because it wouldn't cope; it would just funnel toxic air and gridlock into residential streets. That's why, Llywydd, we're asking that this Senedd charts a new course today. Welsh Labour believes that local people should be at the heart of this new Government's approach to the M4 around Newport. Successive Governments—the Conservatives before devolution, a Plaid Cymru Minister in 2009, and Welsh Labour Governments—have all failed to resolve this challenge.

When the independent planning inspector examined the black route nearly a decade ago, he concluded there was a compelling case on economic and human grounds to build the relief road. This was a comprehensive and lengthy process that engaged with communities, including public hearings, and incorporated detailed plans to enhance and protect the environment.

Major infrastructure done right can enhance, rather than destroy, our natural environment. Indeed, the wonderful and much-loved Newport wetlands nature reserve was established to compensate for habitat lost during the construction of the Cardiff Bay barrage. Many of us across the Labour movement have known for a long time how vital a relief road is, and that's why I could not vote to scrap it in this Chamber in 2019. Today, as a party, Welsh Labour is clear: while the decision to reject the inspector's recommendations may have been understandable on narrow financial grounds, it has left the issue unresolved. Innovative funding models should have been explored, like public-private partnerships, regional borrowing by local authorities supported by the Welsh Government, or land value capture, rather than rejecting it outright.

Let's be clear: these decisions are difficult, and for too long the M4 has been put in the 'too difficult' box. The Plaid Cymru Welsh Government's recent report from Arup states, on page 3:

'None of the options or any combination of options considered as part of this review would fully resolve the M4 problem.'

If the Government is serious about solving this issue, why on earth has the Government remained wedded to their belief that a new relief road is out of scope? It seems Plaid Cymru is perfectly content to build roads and bridges elsewhere in Wales, but not when it comes to solving the M4 around Newport.

In addition to junction closures, the review identifies the options of widening the Brynglas tunnels, combined with the ineffective interventions on local roads, and the so-called blue route is back on the table, which would take traffic closer to communities like Liswerry, Ringland, Pill and Duffryn. The blue route might seem like an option for people who don't live in the area, but with thousands of homes built at Glan Llyn and Milton Park since the initial option was proposed, and thousands more being built, turning what's known as the SDR, the southern distributor road, into a quasi motorway is completely divorced from reality. Everyone knows locally how busy that road is.

The option of widening the Brynglas tunnels cannot be regarded in a credible way. The report states that widening the tunnels is not expected to reduce traffic on the M4 as it involves online works and does not create an alternative route elsewhere. The two lanes start back before the tunnels, and whilst we want the traffic to flow better, it will not tackle the air pollution problem. And we must not forget what the disruption to local homes and businesses above and next to the motorway will be.

Plaid Cymru's public transport plans are not new. They were in progress before this Government. The Burns train stations and better public transport are vital. Welsh Labour championed them, and we need them to be delivered. And while we're glad to see Magor and Undy and Cardiff parkway stations progress, these stations alone will not solve congestion at the Brynglas tunnels. We need to see the Plaid Cymru Government act with urgency to deliver the stations in Newport at Somerton, Liswerry and Tredegar Park. Public transport must be regular, reliable and affordable for people to use it. I say this as someone who's long campaigned for the Ebbw Vale to Newport line and commuters on that line still face unacceptable cancellations and overcrowding. Public transport and road infrastructure must meet the needs of a growing population, and Newport is the faster-growing city with the youngest population in Wales. 

So, let's be clear: a new relief road would not be the old black route. Houses and schools have been built, people have moved to the area and the bar for environmental delivery has rightly risen following the roads review. What we need now is an appropriate, modern relief road that acts as a template for responsible infrastructure. Imagine a road built with the lowest possible embedded carbon and strong site of special scientific interest protections.

The way forward should not be shaped by Ministers lecturing, but by people affected in and around Newport. Welsh Labour believes we should empower those local leaders across councils and the south-east Wales capital region, building on the collaborative Burns model, to develop an appropriate relief road and a creative multisource funding package supported by Welsh Government. Contrary to what we've seen so far, the Government must remember that the people of Newport and south-east Wales aren't just data points in a transport policy document, they're individuals, families and businesses. So, I urge the Senedd to back our motion today. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Pan ofynnais i'r Dirprwy Weinidog sut y byddai'r cyffyrdd eraill ym Mharc Tredegar a'r Coldra yn ymdopi â'r traffig wedi'i ddadleoli, nid oedd ganddo ateb, gan na fyddai'n ymdopi; byddai'n sianelu aer gwenwynig a thagfeydd i mewn i strydoedd preswyl. Dyna pam, Lywydd, ein bod yn gofyn i'r Senedd hon gynllunio trywydd newydd heddiw. Mae Llafur Cymru yn credu y dylai pobl leol fod wrth wraidd dull y Llywodraeth newydd hon o ddelio â'r M4 o amgylch Casnewydd. Mae Llywodraethau olynol—y Ceidwadwyr cyn datganoli, Gweinidog Plaid Cymru yn 2009, a Llywodraethau Llafur Cymru—oll wedi methu datrys yr her hon.

Pan archwiliodd yr arolygydd cynllunio annibynnol y llwybr du bron i ddegawd yn ôl, daeth i'r casgliad fod achos cryf ar sail economaidd a dynol dros adeiladu'r ffordd liniaru. Roedd hon yn broses gynhwysfawr a hir a fu'n ymgysylltu â chymunedau, gan gynnwys gwrandawiadau cyhoeddus, ac roedd yn cynnwys cynlluniau manwl i wella a diogelu'r amgylchedd.

Gall seilwaith mawr wedi'i gyflwyno'n iawn wella, yn hytrach na dinistrio, ein hamgylchedd naturiol. Yn wir, sefydlwyd gwarchodfa natur hyfryd a phoblogaidd gwlyptiroedd Casnewydd i wneud iawn am gynefinoedd a gollwyd yn ystod y gwaith o adeiladu morglawdd Bae Caerdydd. Mae llawer ohonom ar draws y mudiad Llafur wedi gwybod ers amser maith pa mor hanfodol yw ffordd liniaru, a dyna pam na allwn bleidleisio dros roi'r gorau i'w datblygu yn y Siambr hon yn 2019. Heddiw, fel plaid, mae Llafur Cymru yn glir: er y gallai'r penderfyniad i wrthod argymhellion yr arolygydd fod wedi bod yn ddealladwy ar sail ariannol gul, mae wedi gadael y mater heb ei ddatrys. Dylid bod wedi archwilio modelau ariannu arloesol, fel partneriaethau cyhoeddus-preifat, benthyca rhanbarthol gan awdurdodau lleol wedi'i gefnogi gan Lywodraeth Cymru, neu gipio gwerth tir, yn hytrach na'i wrthod yn llwyr.

Gadewch inni fod yn glir: mae'r penderfyniadau hyn yn anodd, ac ers gormod o amser, mae'r M4 wedi cael ei rhoi yn y blwch 'rhy anodd'. Mae adroddiad diweddar Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru gan Arup yn datgan, ar dudalen 3:

'Ni fyddai'r un o'r opsiynau nac unrhyw gyfuniad o opsiynau a ystyriwyd fel rhan o'r adolygiad hwn yn datrys problem yr M4 yn llawn.'

Os yw'r Llywodraeth o ddifrif ynglŷn â datrys y mater hwn, pam ar y ddaear y mae'r Llywodraeth wedi glynu wrth eu cred fod ffordd liniaru newydd yn amhosibl? Ymddengys bod Plaid Cymru yn berffaith fodlon adeiladu ffyrdd a phontydd mewn mannau eraill yng Nghymru, ond nid pan ddaw'n fater o ddatrys yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd.

Yn ogystal â chau cyffyrdd, mae'r adolygiad yn nodi'r opsiynau ar gyfer lledu twnelau Bryn-glas, ynghyd â'r ymyriadau aneffeithiol ar ffyrdd lleol, ac mae'r hyn a elwir yn llwybr glas yn ôl ar y bwrdd, a fyddai'n mynd â thraffig yn agosach at gymunedau fel Llyswyry, Ringland, Pilgwenlli a Dyffryn. Efallai y gallai'r llwybr glas swnio fel opsiwn da i bobl nad ydynt yn byw yn yr ardal, ond gyda miloedd o gartrefi wedi'u hadeiladu yng Nglan Llyn a Pharc Milton ers i'r opsiwn cychwynnol gael ei gynnig, a miloedd yn rhagor yn cael eu hadeiladu, mae troi'r hyn a elwir yn ffordd ddosbarthu ddeheuol yn lled-draffordd yn gwbl ynfyd. Mae pawb lleol yn gwybod pa mor brysur yw'r ffordd honno.

Ni ellir ystyried yr opsiwn i ledu twnelau Bryn-glas mewn ffordd gredadwy. Mae'r adroddiad yn nodi nad oes disgwyl i'r gwaith o ledu'r twnelau leihau traffig ar yr M4 gan ei fod yn cynnwys gwaith ar ffordd weithredol eisoes ac nid yw'n creu llwybr amgen yn rhywle arall. Mae'r ddwy lôn yn dechrau cyn y twnelau, ac er ein bod am i'r traffig lifo'n well, ni fydd yn mynd i'r afael â phroblem llygredd aer. A rhaid inni beidio ag anghofio'r tarfu ar gartrefi a busnesau lleol uwchlaw ac wrth ymyl y draffordd.

Nid yw cynlluniau trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus Plaid Cymru yn newydd. Roeddent ar y gweill cyn y Llywodraeth hon. Mae gorsafoedd trên Burns a gwell trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus yn hanfodol. Fe'u cefnogwyd gan Lafur Cymru, ac mae angen iddynt gael eu darparu. Ac er ein bod yn falch o weld cynnydd ar orsafoedd Magwyr a Gwndy a pharcffordd Caerdydd, ni fydd y gorsafoedd hyn ar eu pen eu hunain yn datrys tagfeydd yn nhwnelau Bryn-glas. Mae angen inni weld Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru yn gweithredu ar frys i ddarparu'r gorsafoedd yng Nghasnewydd yn Somerton, Llyswyry a Pharc Tredegar. Rhaid i drafnidiaeth gyhoeddus fod yn rheolaidd, yn ddibynadwy ac yn fforddiadwy i bobl ei defnyddio. Rwy'n dweud hyn fel rhywun sydd wedi ymgyrchu ers amser maith dros y rheilffordd o Lynebwy i Gasnewydd ac mae cymudwyr ar y rheilffordd honno'n dal i wynebu trenau gorlawn a chanslo annerbyniol. Rhaid i drafnidiaeth gyhoeddus a seilwaith ffyrdd ddiwallu anghenion poblogaeth sy'n tyfu, a Chasnewydd yw'r ddinas sy'n tyfu gyflymaf ac sydd â'r boblogaeth ieuengaf yng Nghymru.

Felly, gadewch inni fod yn glir: ni fyddai ffordd liniaru newydd yn dilyn yr hen lwybr du. Mae tai ac ysgolion wedi'u hadeiladu, mae pobl wedi symud i'r ardal ac mae'r safonau amgylcheddol ar gyfer cyflawni wedi codi, yn gwbl briodol, yn dilyn yr adolygiad ffyrdd. Yr hyn sydd ei angen arnom nawr yw ffordd liniaru fodern, addas sy'n gweithredu fel templed ar gyfer seilwaith cyfrifol. Dychmygwch ffordd wedi'i hadeiladu gyda chyn lleied â phosibl o garbon corfforedig ac amddiffyniadau cryf ar gyfer safleoedd o ddiddordeb gwyddonol arbennig.

Ni ddylai'r ffordd ymlaen gael ei llunio gan Weinidogion yn pregethu, ond gan bobl yr effeithir arnynt yng Nghasnewydd a'r cyffiniau. Mae Llafur Cymru'n credu y dylem rymuso'r arweinwyr lleol hynny ar draws cynghorau a phrifddinas-ranbarth de-ddwyrain Cymru, gan adeiladu ar fodel cydweithredol Burns, i ddatblygu ffordd liniaru briodol a phecyn ariannu amlffynhonnell creadigol a gefnogir gan Lywodraeth Cymru. Yn groes i'r hyn a welsom hyd yma, rhaid i'r Llywodraeth gofio nad pwyntiau data mewn dogfen polisi trafnidiaeth yw pobl Casnewydd a de-ddwyrain Cymru, ond unigolion, teuluoedd a busnesau. Felly, rwy'n annog y Senedd i gefnogi ein cynnig heddiw. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Gwelliant 1—Heledd Fychan

Dileu popeth a rhoi yn ei le:

Cynnig bod y Senedd:

1. Yn gresynu at fethiant Llywodraeth flaenorol Cymru i fynd i’r afael â phroblem hirdymor tagfeydd a gwydnwch gwael ar yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd, sy’n parhau i effeithio ar gymunedau, busnesau a gweithgarwch economaidd ar draws de-ddwyrain Cymru.

2. Yn nodi mai penderfyniad Llywodraeth flaenorol Cymru oedd gwaredu cynllun ffordd liniaru’r M4, ac felly nid yw’r llwybr arfaethedig bellach yn hyfyw.

3. Yn croesawu penderfyniad Llywodraeth Cymru fod yn rhaid i welliannau i ffyrdd a pheirianneg fod yn rhan o’r ymateb hirdymor i dagfeydd ar yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd a’i hymrwymiad i bennu datrysiad ymarferol a ffefrir.

4. Yn nodi’r rhaglen o fesurau i’w cyflwyno ar unwaith ac yn y tymor canolig a gyhoeddwyd gan Lywodraeth Cymru, gan gynnwys buddsoddi yn y draffordd bresennol, gwelliannau i wydnwch y rhwydwaith, cymorth ar gyfer cysylltedd trenau a bysiau a mesurau i hwyluso cludo nwyddau.

5. Yn cefnogi dull Llywodraeth Cymru o weithredu yn awr i wella dibynadwyedd a chysylltedd tra bo datrysiad hirdymor yn cael ei ddatblygu.

6. Yn croesawu ymrwymiad Llywodraeth Cymru i barhau i ymgysylltu â phobl, busnesau a chymunedau yng Nghasnewydd a’r cyffiniau wrth i ddatrysiadau gael eu datblygu a’u gweithredu.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Amendment 1—Heledd Fychan

Delete all and replace with:

To propose that the Senedd:

1. Regrets previous Welsh Governments’ failure to tackle the long-standing issue of congestion and poor resilience on the M4 around Newport, which continues to affect communities, businesses and economic activity across south-east Wales.

2. Notes that the decision to scrap the M4 relief road was taken by a previous Welsh Government, and that the proposed route is therefore no longer viable.

3. Welcomes the Welsh Government’s decision that road and engineering improvements must form part of the long-term response to congestion on the M4 around Newport and its commitment to identify a preferred, deliverable solution.

4. Notes the programme of immediate and medium-term measures announced by the Welsh Government, including investment in the existing motorway, improvements to network resilience, support for rail and bus connectivity, and measures to improve freight movement.

5. Supports the Welsh Government’s approach of taking action now to improve reliability and connectivity while developing the long-term solution.

6. Welcomes the Welsh Government’s commitment to sustained engagement with people, businesses and communities in and around Newport as solutions are developed and implemented.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. This is the first time I rise in this Chamber having to admit that I'm in awe of the Labour Party—for the barefaced cheek it takes to bring this motion to the floor of the Senedd, having cancelled the previous scheme in 2019. Let us not forget that, in Government, they spent £135 million not to build the very thing they are now demanding of Plaid Cymru today. Public money spent on a road that they cancelled, and I note that the leader of the Labour group was the transport Minister at the time. Labour cannot expect people to forget simply because they are now sitting on the opposition benches. Indeed, the public have not forgotten. For all of their online sham protests, I would suggest they read the comments from the public on their social media accounts.

Burnham's branch office is entitled to argue for a different road, but it owes the people who paid for the last scheme an explanation of what it would do differently this time. Its motion gives us no way of knowing which road it means or how it would be funded. Labour needs to explain what its motion would add to the work Ministers have already announced. The Government has already accepted that road and engineering improvements are needed around Newport. It has announced an 18-month study to select a third—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Dyma'r tro cyntaf imi godi yn y Siambr hon i orfod cyfaddef fy mod yn edmygu'r Blaid Lafur—oherwydd yr ehofndra llwyr sydd ei angen i ddod â'r cynnig hwn i lawr y Senedd, ar ôl canslo'r cynllun blaenorol yn 2019. Gadewch inni beidio ag anghofio, yn y Llywodraeth, eu bod wedi gwario £135 miliwn i beidio ag adeiladu'r union beth y maent yn ei fynnu gan Blaid Cymru heddiw. Arian cyhoeddus wedi'i wario ar ffordd a ganslwyd ganddynt, ac rwy'n nodi mai arweinydd y grŵp Llafur oedd y Gweinidog trafnidiaeth ar y pryd. Ni all Llafur ddisgwyl i bobl anghofio am eu bod bellach yn eistedd ar feinciau'r wrthblaid. Yn wir, nid yw'r cyhoedd wedi anghofio. Er gwaethaf eu holl brotestiadau ffug ar-lein, buaswn yn awgrymu y dylent ddarllen y sylwadau gan y cyhoedd ar eu cyfrifon cyfryngau cymdeithasol.

Mae hawl gan swyddfa gangen Burnham i ddadlau dros ffordd wahanol, ond mae arni esboniad i'r bobl a dalodd am y cynllun diwethaf ynghylch yr hyn y byddai'n ei wneud yn wahanol y tro hwn. Nid yw ei chynnig yn rhoi unrhyw ffordd inni wybod pa ffordd y mae'n ei golygu na sut y byddai'n cael ei hariannu. Mae angen i Lafur esbonio beth y byddai eu cynnig yn ei ychwanegu at y gwaith y mae Gweinidogion eisoes wedi'i gyhoeddi. Mae'r Llywodraeth eisoes wedi derbyn bod angen gwelliannau ffyrdd a pheirianneg o amgylch Casnewydd. Mae wedi cyhoeddi astudiaeth 18 mis i ddewis trydydd—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
—road option alongside improvements to the existing motorway and public transport. The study needs to lead to a decision that Ministers can fund and carry through. I also expect progress on the existing network while this work takes place. People should be able to see what is being delivered within those 18 months and when they can expect to improve their journeys.

For people in Casnewydd Islwyn, the roads that lead to the M4 matter as much as the motorway itself. Changes at the Newport junction could affect journeys from the Valleys and put more traffic through residential areas. The Arup review warns that traffic could be displaced around Malpas, High Cross and Ridgeway, which affects noise and air quality. A proposal could therefore improve the flow of traffic on the motorway while making some local journeys worse. We need to know where that traffic would go and what the consequences would be for the people living around those routes. The Government has said that no decision to implement junction closures has been taken. It is committed to further traffic modelling before any decisions are made. I support the decision and look forward to seeing the updated data before the Government makes any final decision.

Based on the evidence, I am supporting the amendment and urge Members to do the same. The electorate expect us to act in this Chamber on their behalf, and not descend into pantomime politics by pretending that the easy solution exists to solve complex problems. This is how we end up here in the first place.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
—opsiwn ffordd ochr yn ochr â gwelliannau i drafnidiaeth gyhoeddus a'r draffordd bresennol. Mae angen i'r astudiaeth arwain at benderfyniad y gall Gweinidogion ei ariannu a'i gyflawni. Rwyf hefyd yn disgwyl cynnydd ar y rhwydwaith presennol tra bo'r gwaith hwn yn mynd rhagddo. Dylai pobl allu gweld beth sy'n cael ei gyflawni o fewn y 18 mis a phryd y gallant ddisgwyl gwella eu teithiau.

I bobl yng Nghasnewydd Islwyn, mae'r ffyrdd sy'n arwain at yr M4 yr un mor bwysig â'r draffordd ei hun. Gallai newidiadau wrth gyffordd Casnewydd effeithio ar deithiau o'r Cymoedd a chyfeirio mwy o draffig drwy ardaloedd preswyl. Mae adolygiad Arup yn rhybuddio y gallai traffig gael ei ddadleoli o amgylch Malpas, High Cross a Ridgeway, sy'n effeithio ar sŵn ac ansawdd aer. Felly, gallai cynnig wella llif traffig ar y draffordd gan waethygu rhai teithiau lleol. Mae angen inni wybod i ble fyddai'r traffig hwnnw'n mynd a beth fyddai'r canlyniadau i'r bobl sy'n byw o amgylch y llwybrau hynny. Mae'r Llywodraeth wedi dweud nad oes unrhyw benderfyniad wedi'i wneud i gau cyffyrdd. Mae wedi ymrwymo i ragor o fodelu traffig cyn gwneud unrhyw benderfyniadau. Rwy'n cefnogi'r penderfyniad ac yn edrych ymlaen at weld y data wedi'i ddiweddaru cyn i'r Llywodraeth wneud unrhyw benderfyniad terfynol.

Yn seiliedig ar y dystiolaeth, rwy'n cefnogi'r gwelliant ac yn annog yr Aelodau i wneud yr un peth. Mae'r etholwyr yn disgwyl inni weithredu yn y Siambr hon ar eu rhan, a pheidio ag ymostwng i wleidyddiaeth pantomeim drwy esgus bod ateb hawdd yn bodoli i ddatrys problemau cymhleth. Dyma sut y gwnaethom gyrraedd y fan hon yn y lle cyntaf.

Oh, have I waited for this one. [Laughter.] Now, we, Reform, will of course support the motion today. It's pretty clear, though, that it's an obvious attempt to cut the strings of Labour's puppet master, Mark Drakeford. Now, we welcome the decision and we congratulate Welsh Labour on taking 27 years to come to the same conclusion that it took us exactly one minute to make. And that one minute was 59 seconds too long, in my opinion.

Now, every day, tens of thousands of motorists sit in queues on the M4. Businesses lose money, workers lose time and families spend more of their lives sitting in traffic than sitting at home with loved ones. And after literally decades of promises, what have they been given? More congestion, more excuses and absolutely no solution. The very politicians responsible for this failure are trying to convince the people of Wales that they have the answer.

Let's start with Labour. Twenty-seven years in Government. Twenty-seven years to deliver a solution to the most important transport problem in recent Welsh history. One hundred and fifty million pounds of taxpayers' money spent on plans, consultations and reviews. And what did the people of Wales receive for that substantial investment? Nothing. Perhaps a few sheets of paper. Mark Drakeford cancelled the M4 relief road, abandoning a project that would have made a real difference. And who was the Government Minister at the time? A gentleman called Ken Skates. [Interruption.] Good timing, sir.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
O, rwyf wedi bod yn aros am hyn. [Chwerthin.] Nawr, fe fyddwn ni, Reform, yn cefnogi'r cynnig heddiw wrth gwrs. Mae'n eithaf clir, serch hynny, ei fod yn ymgais amlwg i dorri llinynnau meistr pypedau Llafur, Mark Drakeford. Nawr, rydym yn croesawu'r penderfyniad ac rydym yn llongyfarch Llafur Cymru ar gymryd 27 mlynedd i ddod i'r un casgliad ag a wnaethom ni mewn un funud. Ac roedd yr un funud honno 59 eiliad yn rhy hir, yn fy marn i.

Nawr, bob dydd, mae degau o filoedd o fodurwyr yn eistedd mewn ciwiau ar yr M4. Mae busnesau'n colli arian, mae gweithwyr yn colli amser ac mae teuluoedd yn treulio mwy o'u bywydau yn eistedd mewn traffig nag yn eistedd gartref gyda'u hanwyliaid. Ac ar ôl degawdau'n llythrennol o addewidion, beth y maent wedi'i gael? Mwy o dagfeydd, mwy o esgusodion a dim ateb o gwbl. Mae'r union wleidyddion sy'n gyfrifol am y methiant hwn yn ceisio argyhoeddi pobl Cymru fod ganddynt yr ateb.

Gadewch inni ddechrau gyda Llafur. Saith mlynedd ar hugain mewn Llywodraeth. Saith mlynedd ar hugain i ddarparu ateb i'r broblem drafnidiaeth bwysicaf yn hanes diweddar Cymru. Cant a hanner o filiynau o bunnoedd o arian trethdalwyr wedi'i wario ar gynlluniau, ymgynghoriadau ac adolygiadau. A beth a gafodd pobl Cymru am y buddsoddiad sylweddol hwnnw? Dim byd. Ychydig dudalennau o bapur efallai. Canslodd Mark Drakeford ffordd liniaru'r M4, gan gefnu ar brosiect a fyddai wedi gwneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol. A phwy oedd Gweinidog y Llywodraeth ar y pryd? Gŵr bonheddig o'r enw Ken Skates. [Torri ar draws.] Amseru da, syr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Not at all. Reform has been very clear: we will build the M4 relief road. So, that's our position. That's the one we're currently going down, and it will not be a toll road. It will be paid for out of the sovereign wealth fund from the UK Government. Thank you very much.

But continuing, did you stand up and challenge the decision? No. Did you stand up and fight for businesses, commuters and families who desperately need that road? No. You defended the very Government that cancelled it. Now Labour wants to lecture this Chamber about the importance of building a relief road. It is quite funny. The same party that killed the project want to take credit for bringing it back to life. So, here's my question to Labour: if the M4 relief road is so desperately needed today, why didn't you build it when you were in power? The truth is, Labour hasn't changed. They've discovered the political consequences of ignoring it. And now, frightened of losing even more support to Reform UK, they're desperately trying to distance themselves from the anti-motorist legacy of Mark Drakeford and Lee Waters. But the people of Wales won't forget, and neither will we.

So, let me now turn to Plaid Cymru, a party that promised change but are determined to continue the same failed approach. The black route has apparently been ruled out. But good news, stranded motorists, we've been offered more studies, more assessments and even more delays, and astonishingly, proposals to close motorway junctions and divert traffic onto local roads in Newport and the surrounding towns. Now, think about that for a moment. Their answer to congestion on the M4 is to move that congestion into the communities of Newport. How on earth is that supposed to improve the lives of the people we represent?

Now, thanks to resurfaced tweets, we have greater clarity on the mind behind the junction closures. In 2019, the Minister stated he wanted to discourage car use on the M4 because of the climate emergency, and even went so far as to seriously suggest that the way to solve the M4 issue was that workers in Wales, in the public sector, should work a day fewer a week. Now, they call us climate conspiracy theorists, of course, yet they're the ones blocking the relief road as part of their net-zero agenda. That is their design: punish motorists and push them onto public transport. And if you don't believe me, just take a look at the transport Minister's own words for it. 

Today is about setting the record straight. Labour had the opportunity to build the road and cancelled it. Plaid Cymru had the opportunity to deliver a solution and is ruling out the very project that would provide one. Now, one party cancelled it, the other refuses to build it, but we all know it was the constant pressure of Reform, our historic election result and our grass-roots campaign that has got us here today. The people of Wales already know how they're going to get this M4 road delivered, and that is with a Reform UK Government.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Ddim o gwbl. Mae Reform wedi dweud yn glir iawn: byddwn yn adeiladu ffordd liniaru'r M4. Felly, dyna ein safbwynt ni. Dyna rydym yn ei drafod ar hyn o bryd, ac ni fydd yn dollffordd. Bydd cronfa gyfoeth sofran Llywodraeth y DU yn talu amdani. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

Ond i barhau, a wnaethoch chi sefyll i herio'r penderfyniad? Na. A wnaethoch chi sefyll ac ymladd dros fusnesau, cymudwyr a theuluoedd y mae taer angen y ffordd honno arnynt? Na. Fe wnaethoch chi amddiffyn yr union Lywodraeth a'i canslodd. Nawr, mae Llafur eisiau pregethu wrth y Siambr hon am bwysigrwydd adeiladu ffordd liniaru. Mae'n eithaf doniol. Mae'r un blaid a laddodd y prosiect eisiau cymryd y clod am ei atgyfodi. Felly, dyma fy nghwestiwn i Lafur: os oes cymaint o angen ffordd liniaru'r M4 heddiw, pam na wnaethoch chi ei hadeiladu pan oeddech chi mewn grym? Y gwir amdani yw nad yw Llafur wedi newid. Maent wedi darganfod canlyniadau gwleidyddol ei anwybyddu. A nawr, a hwythau'n ofni colli hyd yn oed mwy o gefnogaeth i Reform UK, maent yn ceisio ymbellhau oddi wrth waddol gwrth-fodurwyr Mark Drakeford a Lee Waters. Ond ni fydd pobl Cymru yn anghofio, ac ni fyddwn ninnau chwaith.

Felly, gadewch imi droi nawr at Blaid Cymru, plaid a addawodd newid ond sy'n benderfynol o barhau â'r un dull aflwyddiannus o weithredu. Ymddengys bod y llwybr du wedi'i ddiystyru. Ond newyddion da, fodurwyr diobaith, rydym wedi cael cynnig mwy o astudiaethau, mwy o asesiadau a hyd yn oed mwy o oedi, ac yn rhyfeddol, cynigion i gau cyffyrdd traffyrdd a dargyfeirio traffig i ffyrdd lleol yng Nghasnewydd a'r trefi cyfagos. Nawr, meddyliwch am hynny am eiliad. Eu hateb i dagfeydd ar yr M4 yw symud y tagfeydd hynny i mewn i gymunedau Casnewydd. Sut ar y ddaear y mae hynny i fod i wella bywydau'r bobl a gynrychiolwn?

Nawr, diolch i drydariadau sydd wedi dod yn ôl i'r wyneb, mae gennym fwy o eglurder ynghylch y rhesymeg sy'n sail i gau'r cyffyrdd. Yn 2019, dywedodd y Gweinidog ei fod am annog pobl i beidio â defnyddio ceir ar yr M4 oherwydd yr argyfwng hinsawdd, ac aeth mor bell ag awgrymu o ddifrif mai'r ffordd i ddatrys problem yr M4 oedd y dylai gweithwyr yng Nghymru, yn y sector cyhoeddus, weithio diwrnod yn llai yr wythnos. Nawr, maent yn ein galw ni'n ddamcaniaethwyr cynllwyn mewn perthynas â'r hinsawdd, ond nhw sy'n rhwystro'r ffordd liniaru fel rhan o'u hagenda sero net. Dyna yw eu cynllun: cosbi modurwyr a'u gwthio ar drafnidiaeth gyhoeddus. Ac os nad ydych chi'n fy nghredu, edrychwch ar eiriau'r Gweinidog trafnidiaeth ei hun ar hyn.

Mae a wnelo heddiw ag unioni'r sefyllfa. Cafodd Llafur gyfle i adeiladu'r ffordd, ac fe wnaethant ei chanslo. Cafodd Plaid Cymru gyfle i gyflwyno ateb, ac maent yn diystyru'r union brosiect a fyddai'n darparu un. Nawr, mae un blaid wedi canslo'r ffordd, mae'r llall yn gwrthod ei hadeiladu, ond gŵyr pob un ohonom mai pwysau cyson Reform, canlyniad ein hetholiad hanesyddol a'n hymgyrch lawr gwlad sydd wedi dod â ni yma heddiw. Mae pobl Cymru eisoes yn gwybod sut y cânt y ffordd M4 hon wedi'i chyflawni—drwy Lywodraeth Reform UK.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm delighted to support this Labour motion today. The gridlock of traffic congestion on the M4 around Newport has been a national embarrassment for over 30 years. The consequences of all Senedd parties being unable to agree a way forward for the M4 around Newport is ever-rising levels of congestion and pollution in Newport, and the connected Valleys communities north of the M4 in Torfaen and Caerphilly. The Confederation of British Industry and local businesses have been advising for years that the gridlock on the M4 is a brake on economic growth and prosperity for communities along the whole of the M4 corridor in south Wales.

One of the key lessons that this Welsh Labour group takes from its losses in the Senedd elections in May is that we must do more for people today. This is why we must speak out against what Plaid Cymru is proposing to visit on the people of Newport and the south-east Wales Valleys through its proposals on the M4 around Newport review.

Every party in this Chamber will, of course, be keen to support the public transport proposals developed under the last Labour Government for more rail services on the south Wales main line, and this will eventually offer many commuters a rail-based public transport option. And bus and active travel solutions also have a role to play. But the problem is that these public transport interventions will only take 7 per cent of traffic off the M4 on completion, and that's after six to seven years of construction. This is less than a third of the 25 per cent or more of traffic that needs to be diverted from the M4 around Newport.

The last Welsh Labour Government commissioned a series of major road studies in readiness for a new Government, looking at the M4 and also the A55 and the A494 corridors in particular. This work under Labour enabled the Minister to make his announcements on the Menai bridge and the M4 in recent weeks.

The most effective intervention for the M4 would be a relief road. It would meet the key criteria of reducing congestion and thereby pollution made worse by stationary and crawl-speed traffic, and improve resilience, providing an alternative route to the M4 in case of accidents. The other options seemingly championed by the Minister are not fit for purpose. For a 3 per cent reduction in traffic on the M4, junction closures will cause congestion mayhem, pollution and economic harm in and around Newport.

Widening the Brynglas tunnels is a surprising option, dismissed by all previous reviews. The A48 and blue route are not credible either. They would destroy health and wealth in Newport, and the proposals will face great challenges from new housing and the urban context. Looking at this Welsh Government's half-baked review options, it would need to implement a combination of these that it sets out, and the cost of these combinations would exceed £3 billion, and take nearly 30 years as the works on them cannot be done concurrently. All this in the context of a Government with an annual borrowing limit of £165 million, and a total borrowing cap of £1.1 billion.

The Welsh Government cannot deliver an M4 solution on its own. It will need partners prepared to pool financial resources, subject to fit-for-purpose options being agreed. It's time to get real. The proposed junction closures must be ruled out for the benefit of the people of Newport. The only option that delivers reduced congestion, better environmental outcomes by keeping traffic moving and releasing the chokehold of the M4 on the economy is a relief road. We need local leaders empowered to lead the planning of a new relief road for the M4—a partnership of the Welsh Government and local authorities able to consider innovative funding and fully grounded in engagement with the community. Diolch, Lywydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n falch iawn o gefnogi'r cynnig Llafur hwn heddiw. Mae'r tagfeydd traffig ar yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd wedi bod yn embaras cenedlaethol ers dros 30 mlynedd. Canlyniad methiant holl bleidiau'r Senedd i gytuno ar ffordd ymlaen ar gyfer yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd yw lefelau cynyddol o dagfeydd a llygredd yng Nghasnewydd, a chymunedau cysylltiedig y Cymoedd i'r gogledd o'r M4 yn Nhorfaen a Chaerffili. Mae Cydffederasiwn Diwydiant Prydain a busnesau lleol wedi bod yn cynghori ers blynyddoedd fod y tagfeydd traffig ar yr M4 yn rhwystr i dwf economaidd a ffyniant cymunedau ar hyd coridor cyfan yr M4 yn ne Cymru.

Un o'r gwersi allweddol y mae grŵp Llafur Cymru wedi eu dysgu o'i golledion yn etholiadau'r Senedd ym mis Mai yw bod yn rhaid inni wneud mwy dros bobl heddiw. Dyma pam y mae'n rhaid inni siarad yn erbyn yr hyn y mae Plaid Cymru yn bwriadu ei wneud i bobl Casnewydd a Chymoedd de-ddwyrain Cymru drwy ei chynigion ar yr adolygiad o'r M4 o amgylch Casnewydd.

Bydd pob plaid yn y Siambr hon, wrth gwrs, yn awyddus i gefnogi'r cynigion trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus a ddatblygwyd o dan y Llywodraeth Lafur ddiwethaf ar gyfer mwy o wasanaethau rheilffordd ar brif linell de Cymru, a bydd hyn yn y pen draw yn cynnig trên fel opsiwn trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus i lawer o gymudwyr. Ac mae gan fysiau ac atebion teithio llesol ran i'w chwarae hefyd. Ond y broblem yw mai dim ond 7 y cant o draffig y bydd yr ymyriadau trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus hyn yn ei dynnu oddi ar yr M4 ar ôl eu cwblhau, a hynny ar ôl chwech i saith mlynedd o adeiladu. Mae hyn yn llai na thraean o'r 25 y cant neu fwy o draffig y mae angen ei ddargyfeirio oddi ar yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd.

Comisiynodd Llywodraeth Lafur ddiwethaf Cymru gyfres o astudiaethau ffyrdd mawr i baratoi ar gyfer Llywodraeth newydd, gan edrych ar yr M4 yn ogystal â choridorau’r A55 a’r A494 yn benodol. Y gwaith hwn o dan Lafur a alluogodd y Gweinidog i wneud ei gyhoeddiadau ar bont Menai a’r M4 yn yr wythnosau diwethaf.

Yr ymyrraeth fwyaf effeithiol ar gyfer yr M4 fyddai ffordd liniaru. Byddai'n bodloni'r meini prawf allweddol o leihau tagfeydd, a thrwy hynny'n lleihau'r llygredd a waethygir gan draffig segur a thraffig araf iawn, ac yn gwella gwydnwch, gan ddarparu llwybr amgen i'r M4 pan fydd damweiniau'n digwydd. Nid yw'r opsiynau eraill y mae'r Gweinidog i'w weld yn eu hyrwyddo yn addas i’r diben. Ar gyfer gostyngiad o 3 y cant mewn traffig ar yr M4, bydd cau cyffyrdd yn achosi anhrefn o ran tagfeydd, llygredd a niwed economaidd yn ac o amgylch Casnewydd.

Mae lledu twnelau Bryn-glas yn opsiwn annisgwyl, a gafodd ei wrthod gan bob adolygiad blaenorol. Nid yw'r A48 a'r llwybr glas yn gredadwy chwaith. Byddent yn dinistrio iechyd a chyfoeth yng Nghasnewydd, a bydd y cynigion yn wynebu heriau mawr ar ffurf tai newydd a'r cyd-destun trefol. Wrth edrych ar opsiynau adolygiad hanner pob y Llywodraeth hon yng Nghymru, byddai angen iddi weithredu cyfuniad o'r opsiynau y mae'n eu nodi, a byddai cost y cyfuniadau hyn yn fwy na £3 biliwn, ac yn cymryd bron i 30 mlynedd gan na ellir gwneud y gwaith arnynt ar yr un pryd. Hyn oll yng nghyd-destun Llywodraeth â therfyn benthyca blynyddol o £165 miliwn, a chyfanswm cap benthyca o £1.1 biliwn.

Ni all Llywodraeth Cymru ddarparu ateb i'r M4 ar ei phen ei hun. Bydd angen partneriaid sy'n barod i rannu adnoddau ariannol, yn amodol ar gytuno ar opsiynau addas i’r diben. Mae'n bryd bod yn realistig. Rhaid diystyru'r cynigion arfaethedig i gau cyffyrdd er budd pobl Casnewydd. Yr unig opsiwn sy'n lleihau tagfeydd, yn sicrhau gwell canlyniadau amgylcheddol drwy gadw traffig i symud ac yn rhyddhau tagfa'r M4 ar yr economi yw ffordd liniaru. Mae angen arweinwyr lleol arnom sydd wedi'u grymuso i arwain y gwaith o gynllunio ffordd liniaru newydd ar gyfer yr M4—partneriaeth rhwng Llywodraeth Cymru ac awdurdodau lleol sy'n gallu ystyried cyllid arloesol ac sy'n gwbl seiliedig ar ymgysylltiad â'r gymuned. Diolch, Lywydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Welsh Labour Debate: The M4 around Newport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm not going to lie, I do feel like I've walked into the twilight zone today with this particular debate happening. As someone who was born and raised in Newport, I have to say on behalf of myself, as well as all the residents, commuters and businesses, that Newport has been forced to suffer for years with unacceptable traffic chaos, especially when it comes to the M4. This vital stretch of road is regularly clogged, with hotspots like the Brynglas tunnels often gridlocked. Not only does this affect residents going about their daily lives, it has a major impact on visitors and seriously damages our economic prosperity. Something absolutely needs to be done to tackle the M4's never-ending problems. By closing junctions 26, 27 and 25, it's simply not going to be the answer to everyone's prayers. Now, instead of providing any sort of relief, as the Government claims, junction closures will consign Newport to even more misery. Traffic won't magically disappear when these junctions close, it will just be moved to our city's A-roads and residential streets, creating more problems. 

And then there's the price tag. The Government is looking at spending £14 million on closing these three junctions for a measly 3 per cent expected drop in traffic on the M4. Do you really think that's worth it? That £14 million could go towards building an M4 relief road—something that would actually improve the traffic problems across and around Newport. Since news of the junction closure plans came to light, the public uproar in Newport and its surrounding communities has been loud and clear. They do not want to see Plaid politicians spending £14 million on a scheme that is going to make their lives a living misery. And I don't blame them one bit. Residents have been contacting me in their droves over the past few weeks to highlight the problems junction closures will cause for them, and I want to share some of their stories with all of you here in the Chamber today. These are the words of one of my constituents: 'If the Welsh Government continues to pursue these oppressive and poorly thought out policies, it makes me seriously question my future here and I am genuinely considering moving my family and my taxes across the border to England. I know I'm not alone in giving this serious thought.' 

Another constituent told me, 'The closure of these junctions will not only cause chaos on the roads in and around Newport, it will create problems on the roads leading down to the two valleys, which are already congested. It will cause businesses to lose valuable custom, increase their fuel costs and make deliveries a logistical nightmare. It will make commutes longer, more time consuming and more costly.' Another bewildered constituent said, 'Newport residents should not have to pay the price for years of inadequate transport planning and infrastructure investment. Stopping the M4 relief road was, in my view, a major failure in planning towards the future of Wales. Closing M4 junctions is not a solution, it is simply going to move the problem elsewhere. Has anyone seriously considered what the consequences will be for local residents, businesses, commuters and emergency services? We need proper infrastructure investment and long-term thinking. We need additional road capacity and better connectivity across south-east Wales towards England, not measures that make existing congestion even worse. Newport residents deserve better, Wales deserves better.'

Now, that's just a snapshot of the feeling amongst my constituents. I could stand here, genuinely, all afternoon and read you e-mail after e-mail, but I appreciate there's simply not enough time. However, I would be more than happy to share these with the Deputy Minister for Transport so he can get a better understanding of how his plans have gone down in communities across my constituency. Taking feedback and views from residents, businesses and key stakeholders is paramount, Presiding Officer, and whilst I believe these junction closures should be categorically ruled out, if this Government is hell bent on pushing this piece of work through, then there must be a serious consultation. Last week, I raised this point with the Welsh Government, and to say I was disappointed by the response would be an understatement. The Government keeps saying it will engage with communities in Newport about the junction plans, but we haven't heard to date one time—one time alone—how they will be doing this or when this piece of work will indeed be commencing. So, I'm going to try again, and I hope that the Deputy Minister will address these points when he responds to this debate later on.

These are genuine concerns about the impact junction closures will have on emergency services and accessing medical care. One constituent that I spoke to, who has a child with medically complex needs, is sincerely fearful of the potential extra delay she will face as a result of more traffic when getting her daughter to the Grange hospital. The Gwent police and crime commissioner, Jane Mudd, has also sounded the alarm over junction closures, saying it runs the risk of slowing down emergency response times. Not only that, but Malpas fire station is just a stone's throw away from junction 26, which has been earmarked for partial closure. Has the Welsh Government taken this into account? Has the Minister had serious discussions with Gwent Police, the ambulance service, Newport City Council and Aneurin Bevan University Health Board? If so, what has their feedback been so far?

My Welsh Conservative colleagues and I will absolutely be supporting Labour's motion this afternoon, calling for the M4 junction closures to be ruled out and a relief road to be built. But it would be very much remiss of me not to point out the sheer hypocrisy of the Labour Party when it comes to this issue. Let's not all forget, Labour were in power here for 27 years before being turfed out in May. You had more than a quarter of a century to do something to solve the M4 problem, but you did nothing. Labour spent more than £100 million of taxpayers' money on research and development for the M4 relief road, including buying a caravan park, everybody, only for the former First Minister, Mark Drakeford, to scrap the project. And let's not forget that the Conservative Prime Minister, David Cameron, offered your Labour Welsh Government the money to build the relief road, but it was rejected. Where was the outcry from Newport Labour politicians then? Everyone sat there in silence. By not acting when you were in Government, you are equally to blame that these junction closure plans—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Nid wyf am ddweud celwydd, rwy'n teimlo fy mod wedi cerdded i mewn i fyd arall heddiw gyda'r ddadl hon. Fel rhywun a gafodd ei geni a'i magu yng Nghasnewydd, rhaid imi ddweud ar fy rhan fy hun, yn ogystal â'r holl drigolion, cymudwyr a busnesau, fod Casnewydd wedi cael ei gorfodi i ddioddef ers blynyddoedd gydag anhrefn traffig annerbyniol, yn enwedig gyda'r M4. Mae'r darn hanfodol hwn o ffordd yn dioddef tagfeydd rheolaidd, gyda thraffig yn dod i stop yn fynych mewn mannau problemus fel twnelau Bryn-glas. Mae hyn nid yn unig yn effeithio ar drigolion sy'n byw eu bywydau bob dydd, mae hefyd yn cael effaith fawr ar ymwelwyr ac yn niweidio ein ffyniant economaidd yn ddifrifol. Mae angen gwneud rhywbeth i fynd i'r afael â phroblemau diddiwedd yr M4. Nid yw cau cyffyrdd 26, 27 a 25 yn mynd i fod yn ateb i weddïau pawb. Nawr, yn hytrach na darparu unrhyw fath o ryddhad, fel y mae'r Llywodraeth yn honni, bydd cau cyffyrdd yn achosi mwy fyth o ddiflastod i Gasnewydd. Ni fydd traffig yn diflannu'n wyrthiol pan fydd y cyffyrdd hyn yn cau, bydd yn cael ei symud i ffyrdd A a strydoedd preswyl ein dinas, gan greu mwy o broblemau.

Ac yna mae'r tag pris. Mae'r Llywodraeth yn edrych ar wario £14 miliwn ar gau'r tair cyffordd ar sail gostyngiad bychan o 3 y cant yn y traffig ar yr M4. A ydych chi'n meddwl o ddifrif fod hynny'n werth ei wneud? Gallai'r £14 miliwn fynd tuag at adeiladu ffordd liniaru'r M4—rhywbeth a fyddai'n gwella'r problemau traffig ar draws Casnewydd a'r cyffiniau. Ers i'r newyddion am gynlluniau cau'r cyffyrdd ddod i'r amlwg, mae'r gwrthwynebiad cyhoeddus yng Nghasnewydd a'r cymunedau cyfagos wedi bod yn glir iawn. Nid ydynt eisiau gweld gwleidyddion Plaid Cymru'n gwario £14 miliwn ar gynllun sy'n mynd i wneud eu bywydau'n ddiflas. Ac nid wyf yn gweld unrhyw fai arnynt. Mae llu o drigolion wedi cysylltu â mi dros yr wythnosau diwethaf i dynnu sylw at y problemau y bydd cau cyffyrdd yn eu hachosi iddynt hwy, ac rwyf am rannu rhai o'u straeon gyda chi i gyd yma yn y Siambr heddiw. Dyma eiriau un o'm hetholwyr: 'Os bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn parhau i ddilyn y polisïau gormesol a difeddwl hyn, mae’n gwneud i mi gwestiynu fy nyfodol yma, ac o ddifrif, rwy’n ystyried symud fy nheulu a thalu fy nhrethi dros y ffin yn Lloegr. Rwy'n gwybod nad wyf ar fy mhen fy hun yn meddwl o ddifrif am wneud hynny.'

Dywedodd etholwr arall wrthyf, 'Bydd cau'r cyffyrdd hyn nid yn unig yn achosi anhrefn ar y ffyrdd yng Nghasnewydd a'r cyffiniau, bydd hefyd yn creu problemau ar y ffyrdd sy'n arwain i lawr i'r ddau ddyffryn, sydd eisoes yn dioddef tagfeydd. Bydd yn achosi i fusnesau golli cwsmeriaid gwerthfawr, yn cynyddu eu costau tanwydd ac yn gwneud dosbarthu nwyddau'n hunllef logistaidd. Bydd yn gwneud cymudo'n hirach, gan gymryd mwy o amser ac yn fwy costus.' Dywedodd etholwr dryslyd arall, 'Ni ddylai trigolion Casnewydd orfod talu'r pris am flynyddoedd o gynlluniau trafnidiaeth a buddsoddiad seilwaith annigonol. Roedd rhoi'r gorau i ffordd liniaru'r M4 yn fethiant mawr i gynllunio tuag at ddyfodol Cymru yn fy marn i. Nid yw cau cyffyrdd yr M4 yn ateb, nid yw ond yn symud y broblem i fan arall. A oes unrhyw un wedi ystyried o ddifrif beth fydd y canlyniadau i drigolion lleol, busnesau, cymudwyr a gwasanaethau brys? Mae angen buddsoddiad priodol yn y seilwaith a meddwl hirdymor. Mae angen capasiti ffyrdd ychwanegol a gwell cysylltedd ar draws de-ddwyrain Cymru tuag at Loegr, nid mesurau sy'n gwneud y tagfeydd presennol hyd yn oed yn waeth. Mae trigolion Casnewydd yn haeddu gwell, mae Cymru'n haeddu gwell.'

Nawr, cipolwg yn unig ar deimladau fy etholwyr yw hwnnw. Yn onest, gallwn sefyll yma drwy'r prynhawn yn darllen e-bost ar ôl e-bost i chi, ond rwy'n derbyn nad oes digon o amser. Ond rwy'n fwy na hapus i rannu'r rhain gyda'r Dirprwy Weinidog Trafnidiaeth er mwyn iddo gael gwell dealltwriaeth o'r ymateb i'w gynlluniau mewn cymunedau ar draws fy etholaeth. Mae derbyn adborth a barn gan drigolion, busnesau a rhanddeiliaid allweddol yn hollbwysig, Lywydd, ac er fy mod yn credu y dylid diystyru cau'r cyffyrdd hyn yn bendant iawn, os yw'r Llywodraeth hon yn benderfynol o wthio'r gwaith hwn drwodd, rhaid sicrhau ymgynghoriad trylwyr. Yr wythnos diwethaf, codais y pwynt hwn gyda Llywodraeth Cymru, a byddai dweud fy mod wedi fy siomi gan yr ymateb yn danosodiad. Mae'r Llywodraeth yn parhau i ddweud y bydd yn ymgysylltu â chymunedau yng Nghasnewydd ynglŷn â'r cynlluniau ar gyfer y cyffyrdd, ond nid ydym wedi clywed unwaith hyd yma—ddim unwaith—sut y byddant yn gwneud hyn na phryd y bydd y gwaith yn dechrau. Felly, rwy'n mynd i geisio eto, ac rwy'n gobeithio yr aiff y Dirprwy Weinidog i'r afael â'r pwyntiau hyn pan fydd yn ymateb i'r ddadl hon yn nes ymlaen.

Mae'r rhain yn bryderon gwirioneddol am yr effaith y bydd cau cyffyrdd yn ei chael ar wasanaethau brys a mynediad at ofal meddygol. Mae un etholwr y siaradais â hi, sydd â phlentyn ag anghenion meddygol cymhleth, yn ofni'n fawr yr oedi ychwanegol posibl y bydd yn ei wynebu o ganlyniad i fwy o draffig wrth fynd â'i merch i ysbyty'r Faenor. Mae comisiynydd heddlu a throseddu Gwent, Jane Mudd, hefyd wedi rhybuddio ynghylch cau cyffyrdd, gan ddweud ei fod yn creu risg o arafu amseroedd ymateb brys. Nid yn unig hynny, mae gorsaf dân Malpas dafliad carreg i ffwrdd o gyffordd 26, sydd wedi'i chlustnodi ar gyfer ei chau'n rhannol. A yw Llywodraeth Cymru wedi ystyried hyn? A yw'r Gweinidog wedi cael trafodaethau difrifol gyda Heddlu Gwent, y gwasanaeth ambiwlans, Cyngor Dinas Casnewydd a Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Aneurin Bevan? Os felly, beth yw eu hadborth hyd yn hyn?

Bydd fy nghyd-Aelodau yn y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig a minnau'n cefnogi cynnig Llafur y prynhawn yma, sy'n galw am ddiystyru cau cyffyrdd yr M4 ac am adeiladu ffordd liniaru. Ond buaswn ar fai'n peidio â nodi rhagrith llwyr y Blaid Lafur ar y mater hwn. Gadewch inni beidio ag anghofio bod Llafur wedi bod mewn grym yma am 27 mlynedd cyn cael ei diorseddu ym mis Mai. Fe gawsoch chi dros chwarter canrif i wneud rhywbeth i ddatrys problem yr M4, ond ni wnaethoch chi unrhyw beth. Fe wariodd Llafur fwy na £100 miliwn o arian trethdalwyr ar ymchwil a datblygu ar gyfer ffordd liniaru'r M4, gan gynnwys prynu maes carafanau, bawb, ddim ond i'r cyn-Brif Weinidog, Mark Drakeford, ddileu'r prosiect. A gadewch inni beidio ag anghofio bod y Prif Weinidog Ceidwadol, David Cameron, wedi cynnig arian i'ch Llywodraeth Lafur i adeiladu'r ffordd liniaru, ond cafodd ei wrthod. Ble roedd y brotest gan wleidyddion Llafur Casnewydd bryd hynny? Eisteddodd pawb mewn tawelwch. Drwy beidio â gweithredu pan oeddech chi'n Llywodraeth, mae llawn cymaint o fai arnoch chi fod y cynlluniau hyn i gau cyffyrdd—
